News.title: ADHD could have a scary impact on your long-term health, researchers reveal
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

People who live with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, known widely as ADHD, may be at a 70 percent greater risk of early death than people without the condition, according to new research.

Those diagnosed with the brain disorder - the most common brain disorder in children - had a 90 percent higher risk of suicide, a 55 percent higher risk of death from both intentional and accidental injuries and a 27 percent higher risk of death from natural causes, U.K. researchers said in analysis of 16 million adults included in19 studies.

The findings are worrying for the over 15.5 million Americans who live with ADHD and point to the influence of known symptoms, including difficulty with impulse control and attention that impacts the ability to follow healthy behaviors, such as diet and exercise.

There is evidence that people with ADHD are more likely to face mental health problems, too. Adults with ADHD are nearly three times as likely to experience depression than adults without the condition, according to the Attention Deficit Disorder Association.

“They also experience more societal exclusion, disadvantage, and stigma. Unintentional injury deaths, such as road deaths, may also be linked to differences in attention,” the university said.

open image in gallery People with ADHD may be at a much greater risk of death than those without the brain disorder, new research has shown ( Getty Images/iStock )

Previous research has also found people with ADHD experience higher rates of health conditions, including cardiovascular disease, metabolic disorders, diabetes and cancer.

Adults with ADHD could die up to 11 years earlier than those without ADHD, another study from the same researchers found in January 2025.

Women with ADHD were the most impacted, dying up to 11 years earlier than their peers. Whereas men could die up to nine years earlier.

The burden appears to be reduced in people who take medication for ADHD, the researchers noted.

open image in gallery Taking ADHD medication may help lower mortality risk, the analysis also found ( Getty Images/iStock )

The new analysis also found people who take medication for ADHD appear to have a 25 percent lower mortality risk. The medications work to improve focus and curb impulses.

Though other research published in January has found the stimulants don’t work as previously believed, impacting the brain’s reward and wakefulness centers instead of regions that affect attention.

“Many people with ADHD face challenges throughout their lives, so equitable access to evidence-based assessment and treatment is vital to ensure they can live long, healthy lives,” senior author Dr. Amber John, a lecturer at the University of Liverpool, said.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in the U.K. and experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

News.title: Trump won’t let me fly with him today — but he can’t silence me
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

I am writing this under duress.

Over nearly two decades as a reporter in Washington, DC, I’ve tried never to make myself the story — our job is to report the news, not make the news. First-person essays are just not my style.

But since the head of the Executive Branch decided to make me part of his story (and because the issue is what’s central here) I don’t have that luxury right now.

I had planned to get ready Thursday for a short late-afternoon flight to Sioux City, Iowa to cover the latest in President Donald Trump’s rally-a-day barnstorms to try and save his party — and himself — a great midterms embarrassment. That’s because The Independent was scheduled to be in the “print pool” seat aboard Air Force One, part of the 13-member traveling press pool that follows the president any time he leaves Washington.

In some ways it’s a prestigious assignment — we are only one of 15 outlets that share this responsibility, rotating on an alphabetical basis.

open image in gallery The author is pictured asking President Donald Trump a question aboard Air Force One during one of his travel pool rotations in May 2025 ( AFP/Getty )

Yesterday, for example, a reporter from HuffPost was the print pool representative when Trump flew to South Carolina for a rally in support of Sen. Darline Graham. That meant The Independent was in line for the next trip the president would takes, whenever that might be.

That’s why when I saw that the president was slated to hold rallies every day this week, I did some quick calculations to figure out which day I’d be traveling and sent a White House aide an email on Monday asking if they had me penciled in for Thursday’s trip to Iowa. I got a reply shortly thereafter indicating that I’d calculated correctly.

But I’m not going to Sioux City today, after all.

On Wednesday, I went to the White House to shoot a video for The Independent’s YouTube channel — and to reconfirm that I’d be responsible for print pool duties on Thursday’s trip.

But back at home hours later, I received an unsigned email from the press office informing me that I had been removed from the trip.

The anonymous email did not say why, but it was obvious that I was being punished for what happened on Tuesday, when I had been in the Oval Office for the unveiling of a “tip line” to award so-called “whistleblowers” bounties of up to $30,000 for exposing what the administration deems to be “fraud.”

At that event both Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance became annoyed by a question I’d asked about the necessity of the program, I continued to raise my hand and chime in when, from my vantage point directly in line with the president as he sat at the Resolute desk, it appeared that Trump was calling on me once more.

But each time, the president became more and more incensed, at one point calling me a “sick person” and adding: “I actually think there’s something wrong with you.”

open image in gallery Trump and his allies, especially Vice President JD Vance, laid into the author for simply asking a question on Tuesday ( AFP/Getty )

Not long after, the official White House messaging apparatus kicked in to start denigrating me. The administration’s “rapid response” operation called me a “M***** Moron” — spewing a slur for someone with developmental disabilities, a phrase I would never use — and the vice president on his official government X account labeled me an “imbecile.”

Apparently the bullying wasn’t enough because I did not take it quietly.

Although I asked the White House to explain the decision to keep me off of Thursday’s trip, I still haven’t received a reply. But I find it hard to believe that anyone in the West Wing was genuinely bothered by my attempts to ask follow-up queries.

Trump frequently encounters reporters who talk over each other and jump in at the slightest opening to question him. It literally happens any time he takes questions. It’s been the case since the day he was sworn in — the first time, nearly a decade ago.

And even though the White House might insist that they are simply acting to preserve decorum around the president, they’re really trying to create a safe space where the boss won’t get uncomfortable follow-ups from reporters.

Since the White House decided to usurp management of the press pool rotation from the White House Correspondents Association (a decision made in part to avoid honoring a court decision blocking their attempt to ban the Associated Press from the Oval Office), the press office has made sure that anytime Trump takes questions, many if not a majority of the “reporters” present will be from ideologically-driven media outlets that are more or less dedicated less to reporting news than supporting Republicans and denigrating Democrats.

open image in gallery Trump’s jabs at CNN and ABC News come after the president demanded that The Independent ’s White House Correspondent Andrew Feinberg be 'quiet' and asked if he was a 'sick person' ( Getty )

To be fair, many of the people who work for those outlets do ask good questions on occasion. And most of them seem like good people.

But they’re in a different business than I am.

I’m not there to be friendly with this president or administration. And guess what? I wasn’t there to be friendly with the last one, either.

I routinely got into dust-ups with Biden White House spokespeople, whether it was over questioning them on whether Joe Biden had dementia or why the U.S. wasn’t pushing harder for Israel to stop bombing civilians and killing aid workers.

There will be an administration after this one. It may well be one with a Democratic president in the Oval Office once more.

And I’ll be there, doing the exact same thing.

News.title: Karoline Leavitt weighs in on successor Katie Zacharia’s 5-day tenure as press secretary
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt weighed in on her successor Katie Zacharia’s five-day stint in the role, noting the job “obviously was not for her.”

“Look, White House press secretary is a tough job. I know that because I did it,” Leavitt said in a Thursday interview with Fox News Digital.

“Many people say it’s one of the hardest jobs in politics. It takes a lot of preparation. Sometimes you don’t know how someone will perform until they go out there,” she said. “As the president said, we wish Katie the best. The job obviously was not for her.”

Leavitt, who left the role in August after giving birth to her second child, said that she has been trying to help President Donald Trump in his search for Zacharia’s replacement.

“I do obviously talk to him about what the job entails, and he knows it very well. Nobody understands the press better than Donald Trump. He knows that he needs someone who is tough, who is smart, who understands his policies, who is loyal and can go out there and put up a fight,” she said.

open image in gallery Karoline Leavitt said her successor, Katie Zacharia, was not fit for the role of White House press secretary ( AFP/Getty )

Zacharia, a former Homeland Security spokesperson and Newsmax contributor, took over as press secretary on October 12. Leavitt, who was Trump’s press secretary for the start of his second term, starting in January 2025, stepped back in August to spend more time with her young children. Upon announcing Zacharia’s appointment, Trump hailed her as a “loyal and brilliant supporter.”

Despite the hype, Zacharia fell short during her first briefing October 13, which lasted a measly 14 minutes. During that time, she awkwardly read from prepared remarks, accidentally referred to her husband as “my president” and took questions from only three journalists.

The lackluster performance drew backlash from Trump critics and administration officials. Within five days, she had been fired.

Her vacancy comes with midterm elections less than two weeks away — and as polls suggest Republicans may face major losses.

open image in gallery Katie Zacharia was fired just five days into her role as White House press secretary ( AFP/Getty )

“President Trump and his team are focused on the midterm elections,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung told The Independent earlier this week. “The President is the best messenger and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party and he will continue crisscrossing the country to share his commonsense, America First agenda directly with the American people.”

Several names have been floating around — and betted on — for Zacharia’s replacement.

The two top candidates seem to be Anna Kelly, the current White House principal deputy press secretary, CNN’s MAGA pundit Scott Jennings and Elizabeth Pipko, a former model who worked on Trump’s 2016 campaign. Kelly is currently the frontrunner to succeed Zacharia, according to Kalshi bettors.

The former beauty queen has a 15 percent chance of getting the role, while Jennings has a 13 percent. He was widely considered to be favorite for the role when Trump sought to replace then-outgoing Secretary Karoline Leavitt and reportedly privately campaigned for the position.

News.title: Harry Brook hits historic double century – but England still lose to Sri Lanka
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to the fourth match of the autumn tri-series in Pakistan. After two wins for the hosts, the two touring sides face each other for the first time in Rawalpindi, the last match here before the circus leaves for Lahore. England and Sri Lanka played each other only last month in this format, England winning at Chester-le-Street and the Oval by a distance, those victories sandwiching a narrow defeat at Headingley where, if you remember, Harry Brook’s side were cruising until Jos Buttler ripped his left hamstring. He did eventually come back out to bat on one leg as his rattled team-mates flapped and fell to Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga.

On Tuesday against Pakistan, England again were flying with both ball and bat but they let the middle-order rebuild, losing control of the rate. Their two most experienced white-ball bowlers, Adil Rashid, who looked rusty after breaking his hand in August, and Sam Curran, who missed the end of August and all of September following groin surgery, went for 6.87 and eight runs an over respectively. Then, after a promising opening partnership, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull, Tom Banton flicked straight to midwicket and Will Jacks later fell in identical fashion when well-set to marshal the chase. Arafat Minhas ended up with six for 40, bowling Harry Brook with a beauty, and there will be more trial by spin today.

Although there was some talk of England failing in end-of-days Bazball fashion, it most reminded me of the teething troubles of Eoin Morgan’s side in 2015 and 2016 when they were experimenting with players, viz this Rose Bowl collapse. We have to acknowledge that Joe Root, the best player of spin, was undone by one that kept low from Naseem Shah and both Brook and Jordan Cox lost their wickets to very good deliveries from Arafat, a bowler, on a feast day. Dunith Welllalage will return to try to replicate his line of attack today but he is a bowler that England know well. He has had his days against them but they have also given him some tap in the past.

News.title: Health authorities race to investigate first human death linked to Shamonda virus
News.content:
A French man has become the first person to contract Shamonda virus, a disease previously only found in animals and spread through midges.

The patient, who had a weakened immune system, has since died, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).

Shamonda virus was first identified in Nigeria in the 1960s and has this year been detected in farm animals all across Europe.

It was confirmed to have spread to the British Isles in September, after being found in a cattle herd on the island of Jersey. There have also been cases in Ireland.

The French patient, who was immunocompromised, died earlier this month while infected with the virus, but it is unclear if the infection contributed to his death, the ECDC said in a statement.

Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director of the World Health Organization (WHO) said in a statement on X that he was “in contact with French authorities, who are collecting information to better understand the source of infection.”

He added the patient was “immunocompromised, which made them more vulnerable to infection and severe disease.”

There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the French health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement.

Dr Ben Brennan, Group Leader and Senior Lecturer, MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, University of Glasgow, said: “This is an important scientific finding, as it is the first reported human infection with Shamonda virus [..] at present, there is no evidence that Shamonda virus causes widespread human disease, although further investigation is needed to understand its ability to infect people.”

In animals, Shamonda virus attacks the central nervous system and can lead to severe inflammation and haemorrhage. It can also lead to miscarriages.

Affected horses have been reported to exhibit seizures, lethargy, fever, muscle twitching, and difficulty walking.

Authorities are also still trying to ascertain whether the man himself was infected by a biting midge – the route of transmission between animals – or if he could have been infected by close contact with livestock.

It is thought he was infected in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating in midges and animals earlier in the year.

“Despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia, no human cases had been documented until now. This is therefore an exceptional case occurring in a severely immunocompromised patient,” French health authorities said in a statement.

The UK Plant and Health Agency said some of the neurological signs of the disease in horses resemble West Nile fever, human cases of which reached a record high on mainland Europe this year.

News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

News.title: Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match
News.content:
There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Second investigation confirmed as three punishments laid out
Sports.content:

Welcome to Mirror Sport's live blog about Manchester City's 114 guilty charges.

Sports.content:
Antonio Conte's two demands to take Man Utd job emerge after giving green light

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is under pressure to deliver results and the former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Antonio Conte has been linked with the role

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with the managerial position at Manchester United

Antonio Conte will make two demands to the Manchester United hierarchy if he is to take over from Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Napoli boss has been repeatedly linked with a move to Old Trafford given the club's recent struggles.

‌



‌

Sports.title: Man Utd at civil war and Bruno Fernandes criticism leaves Michael Carrick with no way back
Sports.content:
It now feels like a question of when and not if for Michael Carrick.

Manchester United’s humiliating defeat at Como in the Champions League has only sharpened the focus on a growing crisis at Old Trafford which has left Carrick on the brink. The worst start to a league season since 1986 and United crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle.

Incredibly, they are closer to the Premier League relegation zone than the top four. But, undoubtedly, the most damaging part of this week might actually be Bruno Fernandes openly questioning the manager and his tactics.

Sadly, you know the game is up when the dressing room begins to turn and no one should underestimate the power and impact of Fernandes’ words after that Como game. That felt like a new low for Carrick even in such a disappointing season where they have now gone six games without a win.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s tactics after the defeat at Como. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

When asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes also told TNT Sports: “That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me.”

‌



There is an old saying in football that when a manager loses the fans you are a dead man walking. Maybe that explains why Carrick, at the end of the Como game, went over to the travelling fans before anyone else to effectively apologise for the lame performance and surrender.

But, meanwhile, Carrick is clearly in danger of losing the players anyway which is generally the tipping point for any manager. Without the players fighting for you on the pitch, the manager stands no chance of getting a performance from the players.

It was Erik ten Hag who this week talked to The Athletic about “player power” and a “toxic” environment at Old Trafford during his time in charge.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes called out Michael Carrick's tactics (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



Dutchman Ten Hag said he had to be the bad cop. Ruben Amorim came in and was probably too honest. Carrick clearly got brilliant results and performances from the players last season to lift the club from mediocrity and into the Champions League places.

Carrick got the players onside but that approach will only work for so long. Being a nice guy in football is probably seen as a sign of weakness and that makes you the No.1 target when you do not get results.

The most obvious thing about United this season has been a lack of intensity, a lack of sharpness and direction. The recruitment has been poor but the opening day defeat at Hull City was more about the team’s lack of fitness. That still looks well below par.

United have not improved and now you have criticism coming from all angles. Last week it was Lisandro Martinez taking aim at the club’s hierarchy and poor recruitment.

‌



Why did they sign Youri Tielemans? He is a good player, but what was the plan? He does not fit into their system. So, why sign him? That’s United’s transfer policy to a tee.

And what on earth did those signings make of those Martinez remarks? That was the first sign of civil war.

Should Manchester United sack Michael Carrick? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick apologised to Manchester United's fans (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



This week, we have the captain speaking out against the manager. That feels like the point of no return. There is surely no way back for the United manager.

United should, in hindsight, have been bold in the summer and thanked Carrick for steering the club back into the top four and then looked to hire an elite, experienced manager.

Instead, they stuck with Carrick and are now stuck back in a cycle which just mirrors what happened with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. An upturn in results as the dressing room like him, they turn things around - and then run out of steam.

That is what happened with Carrick. It’s rinse and repeat. Carrick has run out of credit with the players. Frankly, after a 4-1 defeat, one of the worst defeats in the club’s proud European history, it would have been no surprise if they had pulled the trigger.

‌



Now it just feels like Carrick is treading water. He stumbles on until Bournemouth on Sunday. He may get until the next international break. Then it will be the next cab off the rank from the ranks of Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte or Eddie Howe.

Conte would get results but present a scorched earth policy. Howe inherited a bigger mess at Newcastle but did a great job. He is free, available and would be keen. But even Howe can only succeed if the structure above is right. And at United, that is the bigger problem.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes' £4m mansion robbed by masked gang while Man Utd captain away with team
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes' £4m mansion robbed by masked gang while Man Utd captain away with team

Bruno Fernandes' family home in Cheshire was ransacked by three masked criminals while he was away playing for Manchester United against Como on Wednesday night

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes was in Italy while his house was robbed (Image: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes returned from Manchester United's dismal defeat by Como on Wednesday night to find that his home had been ransacked by criminals.

‌



‌



Fernandes made headlines on Wednesday for taking aim at United manager Michael Carrick's tactics following their 4-1 thrashing in northern Italy. And the disappointment on the pitch was followed by worse news from home.

‌



The United captain's £4million mansion in Cheshire was raided by three masked figures on Wednesday night. His house in Nether Alderley was targeted by thieves at 8.30pm.

‌



As first reported by The Sun, one of Fernandes' neighbours called the police after spotting three suspicious people. It is thought that they scaled the back fence of the garden, which backs onto woodland, before making off with valuables.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision READ MORE :

They managed to get away, despite the home being fitted out with a hi-tech security system including alarms, CCTV and an electric gate. It is not clear whether Fernandes' Ana Pinho and their two young children were in the house at the time of the incident.

‌



Mirror Football have contacted Fernandes' representatives and Manchester United to request comment.

A Cheshire Police spokesperson said: “At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes with his wife Ana Pinho in August (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

“The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property. Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.”

‌



Detective Inspector David Jarvis, of Macclesfield Proactive CID, added: “This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we’re committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

“As part of our enquiries, we’re keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.”

‌



The incident came while Fernandes was in Como, playing in a miserable defeat. United were thrashed 4-1, prompting Fernandes to speak out against Carrick's tactics and call out the club being stuck in the past.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes urges Man Utd to 'stop living in the past' in fresh damning interview
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes urges Man Utd to 'stop living in the past' in fresh damning interview

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes broke ranks to send a clear message to his team-mates and the club hierarchy after the shambolic 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes had some alarming words post-match (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes has accused others at Manchester United of living in the past in a second eye-catching interview after the dismal defeat by Como.

‌



‌



Fernandes' words added fuel to the fire after United were thrashed 4-1 in northern Italy on Wednesday night. Speaking to TNT Sports, the United captain openly questioned Michael Carrick's tactics, piling pressure onto the manager just 11 games into the season.

‌



While the United hierarchy are not about to pull the trigger on Carrick just months after handing him the job on a permanent basis, his position is far from safe. Director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is understood to be pushing for the appointment of Julian Nagelsmann if United sack Carrick, who desperately needs a win against Bournemouth on Sunday.

‌



And the bullish words of Fernandes won't help the perception that not everyone at the club are pulling in the same direction. Speaking to Sky Sports Italy, the midfielder spoke his mind.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision READ MORE :

Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified READ MORE :

“Everyone at the club must understand that it’s no longer the same,” Fernandes said. “We’re no longer in the past and we must look to the future. We must create something different in the present.

‌



“At this club, we focus too much on what was achieved in the past, but we are no longer the same. The club and the players must understand this.

“Unfortunately for us, especially the players, those who come think about winning trophies, matches, and reaching the highest level, but unfortunately it’s been very difficult at this club in recent years. That’s the situation.”

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick is clinging onto his job (Image: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Intriguingly, Sky Sports Italy reporter Pierluigi Bagnulo said that Fernandes was not allowed by the club to conduct the fiery interview in Italian, despite speaking the language fluently following time spent in his early career at Novara, Sampdoria and Udinese.

‌



“It’s a very difficult moment for us, we’re not getting the points and results we want," Fernandes added. “The most important thing is that we’re not performing as we expect.

"Unfortunately, it’s one of those moments where it seems like we can’t get out of it. We have to do something to change this situation and start winning because it’s important.”

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes spoke openly about his frustrations post-match (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI, AFP via Getty Images)

Carrick raised eyebrows by replacing Fernandes with Joshua Zirkzee in the second half in Como. “Nobody likes to leave the pitch, especially with a result like that," the United captain said when asked about the decision.

‌



“It was a very difficult match for us, it was almost impossible to play with the ball, we weren’t close enough to maintain possession and play in their half.

“Como were very brave in their man-to-man pressing, we never did that and we gave them too many opportunities to play between our lines, thus managing to create chances to score.”

‌



United have won just two matches this season, against newly promoted Ipswich and Champions League minnows Sabah. They host Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday before travelling to Chelsea the following weekend.

Sports.title: Man Utd chiefs point finger of blame as Como defeat piles pressure on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Man Utd chiefs point finger of blame as Como defeat piles pressure on Michael Carrick

Michael Carrick has come under fire following Man Utd's defeat to Como in the Champions League but so have the players

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has come under fire following Man Utd's defeat to Como in the Champions League (Image: (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images))

Manchester United bosses believe the players must shoulder some of the responsibility for the dismal 4-1 thrashing by Como in the Champions League. Manager Michael Carrick faces growing scrutiny but his position remains secure for the time being.

‌



‌



The club's senior figures were left astonished by just how abject the on-field performance was from the squad. Nico Paz broke the deadlock inside just two minutes, and a string of Senne Lammens stops kept the scoreline respectable until after the break, when Cesc Fabregas' outfit added two more, with Paz setting up Anastasios Douvikas before netting his second.

‌



On an evening that looked set to hinge on influential playmakers, it was the 22-year-old who commanded proceedings for the Serie A outfit while Bruno Fernandes was deployed out of his natural role before being withdrawn in the 66th minute.

‌



The United skipper was among numerous underwhelming performers on the night, with Andrey Santos, who was substituted at half-time following a booking, toiling in the middle of the park. Mason Mount and Matthijs de Ligt were among the rare starters who appeared completely overwhelmed.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Fitness concerns and a tight schedule forced Carrick into alterations, but he still selected a strong starting XI, which left United bosses stunned by such an inadequate showing, according to The Times. Their report has also suggested that the recent slump in form falls on the players rather than solely on Carrick.

The latter finds himself under considerable scrutiny, though, with United having secured just two victories this campaign. Carrick is not currently thinking his own situation, with his attention focused on reversing the club's fortunes.

‌



"Listen, I've not given my own position any thought," he said. "[My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn't happy at all."

"It's not about me right now and my feelings in that regard. It's more of as a team and as a football club, what we want to look like, what we should look like. And as I said, the results can come and go at times, but you got to do it in a certain way. And that wasn't it."

‌



View 2 Images Senior figures at United believes the players deserve a significant proportion of the blame (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images))

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Once more, remarks from a player in the aftermath of a European loss have sparked debate, with Fernandes this time left incensed by both the performance and the tactical approach.

He told TNT Sports: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence."

‌



When asked point-blank if Carrick had got it wrong, he replied: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.

Carrick was given the opportunity to respond and seemingly threw it back onto the players and their lack of effort on the night. He said: "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that.

Article continues below

"And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Sports.title: Man Utd make Michael Carrick sack decision after Como humiliation
Sports.content:
Man Utd make Michael Carrick sack decision after Como humiliation

Michael Carrick is under huge pressure to keep his job as Manchester United manager, and the Old Trafford hierarchy have now made a decision

View Image Carrick is set to remain as United manager - for now (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick will NOT be sacked as Manchester United manager before Sunday's Premier League clash against Bournemouth.

‌



‌



Carrick oversaw a humiliating defeat by Como on Wednesday night as United were humbled 4-1 in the Champions League. It means they have won just twice in 11 games in all competitions this term.

‌



But Carrick will be afforded the opportunity to carry on, at least for now, and will hold a press conference tomorrow ahead of the Cherries' trip to Old Trafford.

‌



It comes after he lamented his players for their effort against Como and was involved in a public disagreement with captain Bruno Fernandes.

Carrick said after the game: "We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure.

Sports.title: 'I played for Man Utd and under Antonio Conte - he'd be a disaster there'
Sports.content:
'I played for Man Utd and under Antonio Conte - he'd be a disaster there'

Antonio Conte is being linked as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick at Manchester United, though one ex-Old Trafford star has warned it could be a "disaster"

View 2 Images Manchester United have received a warning that Antonio Conte would be a disastrous appointment as manager (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United star Ashley Young has cautioned his old club against appointing Antonio Conte as manager. The Italian is once again being tipped for the job as Michael Carrick comes in for more scrutiny.

‌



‌



United's season went from bad to worse on Wednesday when Carrick's side lost 4-1 away to Como in the Champions League. The club's seventh straight game without a win led to some uncomfortable comments from the manager post-match, suggesting United's players aren't running enough in their efforts to earn results.

‌



That's one specific area in which Young believes Conte, who coached him for 18 months at Inter Milan, would be a poor appointment. The former Juventus, Chelsea and Tottenham chief is renowned as a taskmaster when it comes to conditioning, where some in the current United squad may not meet the grade.

‌



Young appeared on The Overlap Daily, where he was quizzed on whether he felt Conte was a genuine target for United, or the Italian and his team were attempting to orchestrate the move themselves.

"I’d go with the second one," he said. "I think linking himself to the job, saying that big clubs, he wants to get the history back and whatnot.

Man Utd waste no time with sack decisions as Michael Carrick set to face the music READ MORE :

"I’ve worked underneath him at Milan. He’s crazy, by the way. Like he is crazy. He’s a bit like Diego Simeone on the sidelines. Like you hear him non-stop.

‌



"Meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking, if we lost the game, we could go in and do the meeting after the game and it stops literally everything and you could be there for three, four hours. I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places because not just the players, he tries to test mentally, but the board as well and the owners."

Young then proceeded to put his former team on high alert as he addressed United's alleged lack of running. "There has been a lot of talk about Man United’s running stats," he added. "If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster."

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick is under growing pressure to get the boot at United following a grim run of results (Image: AP Photo/Antonio Calanni)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Conte has long held a reputation as having incredibly high standards when it comes to the fitness levels demanded of his players. He's also a keen believer in strict dieting and helped ex-United striker Romelu Lukaku shed weight and improve his conditioning during their time together at Inter.

During his first pre-season in charge of Tottenham in 2022, stories emerged of how Conte and his fitness team were putting the Spurs players through their paces. Reports even claimed one two-hour session in Seoul ended with Harry Kane throwing up, while Son Heung-min collapsed in front of a home audience.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Young - who only retired this year at Ipswich Town, aged 40 - was clearly up to the required standards. The veteran was long regarded as having impressive fitness levels throughout his playing career.

‌



The same might not be said for numerous United players after struggling to keep up with Como's pace in Italy. And it's possible Conte's introduction to the current environment at Old Trafford could either bring the squad onto the next level or end in tears.

Sports.title: Dominant Sunderland punished as Bengtsson earns Lech draw
Sports.content:
Timur Tutierov's first Sunderland goal was not enough to earn them the victory they deserved in Poland as their wastefulness was punished in a 1-1 draw at lowly Lech Poznan.

The 21-year-old got the Black Cats' - and his own - night off to the perfect start with the fastest goal in this season's Europa League, nodding home Nilson Angulo's cross with barely a minute gone after Mateusz Lis' poor clearance was picked off.

Tutierov spent last season on loan in League One with Exeter and was playing just his fourth game for Sunderland, having been fast-tracked into the club's first team following injuries to Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor.

After a brief response from the hosts, and a couple of gilt-edged chances, the Black Cats threatened to add to their lead and hit the post through Angulo, but a host of chances came and went without adding to their early opener. They would end up registering 25 shots, including 11 on target, but it was not enough.

Having lost both of their opening League Phase games 4-0, Lech finally registered their first goal in Europe this season when substitute Martin Bengtsson fired through a crowd of bodies following a knock-down from a corner to beat an unsighted Robin Roefs at his near post with 20 minutes to go.

Though Sunderland pushed to restore their lead and saw substitute Chris Rigg curl a 20-yard effort inches over the bar, they were made to pay for failing to make their dominance count as they were denied victory for the first time in their European campaign, but remain unbeaten in the Europa League following a seventh point from their three matches so far.

Key moments from the INEA Stadion....

2: GOAL! Tutierov scores the fastest goal in this season's Europa League, heading home Angulo's cross when Sunderland press high and force a mistake from Lis.

3: CHANCE! Roefs has to be at his best to make a superb double save from Radoslaw Murawski after initially spilling Patrik Walemark's shot into his path.

16: BIG CHANCE! Daniel Hakans races through from Pablo Rodriguez's pass in behind but misses the target altogether past a sprawling Roefs.

21: OFF THE POST! When Granit Xhaka's shot is tipped away, Fofana strikes the outside of the far post from a tight angle.

70: GOAL! Sunderland are punished for not making their dominance count as substitute Bengtsson fires in an equaliser following a corner.

82: SO CLOSE! Rigg is inches away from restoring Sunderland's lead but can only lift a curling effort onto the roof of the net from 20 yards.

Sports.title: How Grant is using his experience in Charlton homecoming
Sports.content:
"It's nice to be home," is Karlan Grant's reply when asked how the last few months have been sign he re-joined Charlton in the summer.

The Addicks academy graduate returned after six years at West Brom, where he had turned down a new deal. "It all aligned at the time and hopefully it's still aligned at the end of the season," he added of why he decided to come back to south London.

When Grant left The Valley in January 2019 for Huddersfield, it was not well-received by some Charlton fans. But seven years and three clubs later, the 29-year-old is an experienced and established Championship player.

"I think experience is a big thing," the forward exclusively told Sky Sports. "I left so young, I've played a lot of games since then, so it's just bringing my experience to the group.

"I got a bit of stick when I did leave, but that's football. Coming back, I'm one of them, so it's been good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Watford against Charlton in the Sky Bet Championship

Charlton's academy is famous for producing talented players, and is perhaps demonstrated no better than an Addicks forward line that comprises three graduates - Tyreece Campbell, Miles Leaburn and Grant.

"They're good lads. They've done very well to get to this level. I'm here to help with my experience and help the team as well, so it's nice to see them do what they're doing," he said of his now team-mates.

Alan Mwamba is the latest academy product making waves in the first team - Grant also tipping Ruben Reid as one to watch - with south London well-known as a hotbed for scouting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Preston North End, in which Karlan Grant scored the winning goal

It is the location that helps Charlton's academy thrive, with Grant also pointing to the staff as key in helping players develop.

"The coaches here are amazing," he said. "The location in the south east [of London], I was lucky to play with players coming through who have played for England and at the highest level. The pathway has always been there and will always be there.

"That was me when I was a kid, playing cage football. Coming through the community, there's a lot of opportunity here and if kids find their time and believe in the system throughout their youth, they will definitely get a chance.

"I think every year, there will be someone to keep an eye on. There's so many."

It's a long season and still early. It's frustrating because some of those draws are probably going to turn into wins, but you've got to stay positive. I've been in this league a long time now, so I know how much it changes and momentum is massive.

On Saturday, Charlton, without a win in their past eight league games, take on Norwich, a side also short of form as they sit just above the bottom three.

It is the club's annual Red, White and Black weekend, which reinforces the club's commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.

Each year, there is a parade to The Valley including local students and community groups. For the first time, the march will be held ahead of Charlton Women's game against Chelsea Women on Sunday.

The men's match is also dedicated to the EFL's Together Against Racism campaign. Grant, alongside Charlie Kelman, attended a Show Racism the Red Card workshop at The Valley as part of the Charlton Athletic Community Trust's Premier League Primary Stars programme.

"These events are so important because us as players can really help people outside of the football environment," Grant said.

"Football is such a big sport and everyone looks into it and there's a lot of diversity and different cultures within the club.

"It brings everyone together and it just shows that even in football and outside of football, it's so important."

Watch Charlton vs Norwich live on Sky Sports Football and Main Event from 11.30am on Saturday; kick-off 12.30pm.

Sports.title: Brighton held to rare goalless draw by Jablonec
Sports.content:
In-form Brighton saw their six-game winning run come to an end after being held to a 0-0 draw at Jablonec in the UEFA Conference League.

The Premier League's top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in the northern Czech Republic, as despite having 26 efforts at goal, they failed to score for the first time in 10 games.

Around 1,000 Seagulls fans made the trip from the Sussex coast to the homely Stadion Strelnice in the city of Jablonec nad Nisou.

These are heady days for their team, who lie third in the English top flight, fresh from Sunday's 5-0 thrashing of M23 rivals Crystal Palace.

Boss Fabian Hurzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and the omnipresent Pascal Gross keeping their places.

However, despite enjoying 73 per cent possession, the visitors struggled to create any clear-cut openings and it was their hosts who finished the stronger.

Antonin Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha, before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama's drive from hitting the top corner.

Key moments from the Stadion Strelnice

30: BIG CHANCE! Rusek meets a right-wing corner with his head, only to glance his effort wide of the near post with the goal gaping.

71: HUGE CHANCE! Costinha makes a complete mess of a headed clearance, allowing Rusek clean through, but faced with just Verbruggen to beat, Svoboda gets back just in time to make a goal-saving block.

75: WHAT A SAVE! Verbruggen comes to Brighton's with a sensational one-handed stop to turn over Slama's curler from the edge of the area.

Sports.title: Sherrock set to face Littler for first time with £501,000 on the line
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock is set to face Luke Littler for the first time in a special event taking place at the end of this month - 'Beat Luke Littler'.

Sherrock is one of 24 contestants who could go head-to-head with Littler over one leg in Manchester Central next Friday, with the first player to beat Littler winning £501,000.

Sherrock is the most high-profile player while reigning world youth champion Mitchell Lawrie is also in the field along with regular members of the public who play darts socially.

Littler said: "There's half a million quid up for grabs, I won't be going easy at all!

Image: Fallon Sherrock finished runner-up to Beau Greaves in the Women's World Matchplay in July [PDC Darts]

"I'll be wanting to beat everyone who comes up. Maybe the first few legs could be a bit nervy, but once I get going then I don't think anyone will stop me."

Sherrock has won just one title in the PDC Women's Series this year as Beau Greaves continues to dominate the circuit.

But, 'The Queen of the Palace' has already qualified for the World Championship in December as she was in the top five in the Women's Series with Greaves, Lisa Ashton, Gemmy Hayter and Vicky Pruim also qualifying.

Next Friday's exhibition event in Manchester will be broadcast on Netflix and saw thousands of amateur darts players aged 12 and over put their skills to the test in a rigorous three-stage qualification process at Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park earlier this month.

They had to check out 501 in 24 darts or fewer before the reality TV element of the competition came into play, with successful players then interviewed by the show's production team.

The final stage required them to impress a PDC judging panel led by 16-time world champion Phil Taylor, who assessed their darting prowess and decided whether they had the ability to give Littler a realistic challenge in the event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his World Matchplay victory earlier this year Luke Littler said he'd love to be the greatest darts player of all time

"The event is great to be honest, it gives people the opportunity to change their lives," said Taylor.

"It's a Rocky Balboa kind of fairytale really. It will boost the profile of darts even further. Any player who can throw a 12-dart leg has a great chance, but it's also about bottle as well as ability, so we'll see."

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

Sports.title: Carrick will be in charge for 'pivotal' Bournemouth game despite growing concerns
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick will be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth on Sunday but there is growing concern among club bosses about the team's poor run of form.

There is a feeling both inside and outside Old Trafford that Sunday's Premier League match - live on Sky Sports - could be pivotal in determining Carrick's future.

No decision has been taken about plans beyond Sunday as things stand following Wednesday's 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

Bruno Fernandes will not be stripped of the captaincy in light of his criticism of the United coaching staff and is unlikely to face any punishment for his comments after the crushing defeat in Italy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick admitted his team's performance was 'not acceptable' in their 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League

There is a feeling within the Carrington training ground that the performance and result in the Champions League on Wednesday night was unacceptable - as Carrick himself said after the match.

There is sympathy for Carrick when it comes to the injury problems he is dealing with, and many United supporters agreed with Lisandro Martinez's outspoken views of last week when he said the squad is not strong enough to compete at the top level. Martinez levelled the criticism at the United hierarchy, not the head coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson believes Michael Carrick should remain in charge of Man Utd

But it is clear United's bosses feel that, despite those factors, the squad is stronger than it was last season when Carrick secured a third-placed Premier League finish, and so far this season the team has woefully underperformed.

United's directors assessed and interviewed a host of other candidates in January as part of their due diligence before appointing Carrick, and while it is thought there has been no formal contact with those candidates recently, such discussions cannot be ruled out in the coming days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol answers your questions on the problems currently facing Manchester United

Fernandes unlikely to be punished for criticism of staff

Fernandes will not be stripped of the Manchester United captaincy and is unlikely to be disciplined by the club following his criticism of the coaching staff and the tactics in the 4-1 defeat to Como.

Sky Sports News has been told that, while there is disappointment within the club with what last season's PFA Player of the Year said post-match, the wider feeling is that he was voicing an understandable frustration and anger at the manner of the defeat.

In his own post-match news conference, head coach Carrick responded to his captain's comments by saying: "If you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in United's work out of possession, Fernandes defended his team-mates and put the blame on Carrick and his coaches on Wednesday night.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man, and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Was that tactical idea what cost Man Utd in Como? "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes.
