Sports.title: Devin Haney Gets Favorable Matchup In Liam Paro
Sports.content:
Devin Haney has agreed to meet Liam Paro in a WBO and IBF welterweight unification before the close of the year in the United States, according to Mike Coppinger of The Ring. Official confirmation on the date and venue remains pending.

The matchup offers Haney an ideal path toward a second belt. Facing an opponent recently beaten by Richardson Hitchins represents a noticeably safer route than the scrapped Shakur Stevenson clash. Paro carries championship hardware, yet that December 2024 split decision defeat gives Haney a transparent blueprint.

Hitchins took Paro’s 140-pound belt by controlling distance, working behind a disciplined jab, and forcing the Australian to play catch-up all night. Haney possesses the precise reach, jab, and ring generalship required to run the exact same play.

Because of that dynamic, this unification leans toward comfortable territory for Haney. Paro holds a world title, yet Haney does not have to invent a fresh game plan. The tape exists, showing Paro struggling against an opponent armed with a very similar skill set.

The main wildcard rests on Haney’s activity level. He has stayed out of action since his November 2025 victory over Brian Norman. A layoff stretching near a full year is tough preparation for any world-level contest, especially if Paro manages to drag him into deep waters early.

Still, the stylistic matchup heavily favors Haney. He steps back into competition with two world titles on the line while facing a fighter susceptible to his trademark boxing style.

Paro must avoid turning this bout into a fruitless footrace. To take the victory, he has to cut off the ring, hammer the body, and make Haney pay for retreating. Stalking without throwing and waiting for clean openings will merely walk him straight into the WBO champion’s rhythm.

The upside for Haney is massive: capturing a second belt and securing major leverage for future paydays. Defeating Paro takes him one step nearer to an undisputed run at 147, even if it leaves lingering questions about how he handles the division’s truly lethal punchers.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Returns To PPV Against Michal Cieslak
Sports.content:
David Benavidez taking on Michal Cieslak on December 5 is landing on DAZN pay-per-view, but convincing boxing fans to shell out extra cash for this one is going to be a tough sell. The fight looks completely lopsided in favor of Benavidez, while Cieslak barely registers with mainstream fans.

Having three cruiserweight belts on the line does not move the needle either. Cieslak picked up the WBC belt simply by getting elevated from interim status. When fans already see someone as a paper champion, handing over an official sanctioning belt does nothing to turn him into a credible threat.

DAZN locked in the date, stamping PAY PER VIEW across the official fight poster alongside PBC. They have not dropped the price tag yet, but asking subscribers to dig deeper into their pockets for this headliner feels overly ambitious.

That puts the heavy lifting squarely on Benavidez. Being an elite talent inside the ring has never guaranteed monster pay-per-view numbers. He brings real fireworks once the bell sounds, but generating buy rates demands relentless promotional buzz outside the ring.

Benavidez rarely brings that promotional heat. He stays relatively quiet between training camps. His media appearances lean dead serious, skipping the colorful banter that grabs casual viewers who do not follow every twist in boxing.

Nobody expects him to fake a circus persona. Still, without that natural promotional spark, his headliners rely heavily on having an electric opponent. Cieslak does not move the needle there at all. Putting Benavidez on pay-per-view without an elite foil exposes the gap between being a respected champion and being a genuine ticket seller.

From a purely competitive standpoint, the move makes sense for Benavidez. Picking up the WBC crown lets him unify alongside his WBA and WBO straps, pushing him closer to a massive clash with Jai Opetaia. Taking the fight serves his personal goals, but that does not give regular fans a compelling reason to buy the broadcast.

Stacking the undercard might soften the blow. Taken solely as a main event, the booking comes across as an uncompetitive mismatch anchored by a single recognizable name whose solo box office power is unproven. Slapping three world titles onto the promotional artwork will not fix that reality.

Sports.title: Joe Cordina Agrees Terms To Fight Manny Pacquiao
Sports.content:
Joe Cordina has agreed to terms to fight Manny Pacquiao, putting the Welshman in position for a major payday if the proposed contest goes ahead.

The bout is being discussed for the December 11 Fury–Joshua card, although Eddie Hearn’s latest update confirms only that Cordina’s side has accepted the terms. He is still waiting to find out whether the fight will happen.

“We’ve agreed terms to fight Manny Pacquiao, but we don’t know if that’s happening,” Hearn told reporters. “From our side, we’ve agreed to do it.”

That leaves Cordina waiting on a fight that would bring him attention far beyond his usual audience. Pacquiao’s name would make this one of the most watched nights of his career, even with the Filipino well past his best years.

Cordina has every reason to take the opportunity. A fight against Pacquiao offers a different financial ceiling from the conventional route through the lightweight division. Adding it to Fury–Joshua would also give the former super featherweight champion a huge platform in front of a British audience.

The boxing question is what each man would bring at the agreed weight. Hearn did not reveal that detail, and it would have a considerable effect on the matchup. Cordina’s sharp punching and timing would be tested differently against a naturally smaller opponent than against someone accustomed to competing above his weight.

Pacquiao’s age would inevitably dominate the buildup. The name still sells, but the fighter taking the punches must perform on the night. Cordina would need to approach him as an opponent to beat, rather than let the occasion become a celebration of the former champion’s career.

Agreeing terms removes one obstacle from Cordina’s side. It also shows that his team sees enough reward in the proposed fight to accept it.

The next step is getting Pacquiao’s participation settled, and the contest announced. Cordina has accepted his end of the deal; Hearn’s wording makes clear that he cannot yet promise the fight.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Refuses To Move For Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall refuses to move out of Teofimo Lopez’s way, rejecting any payment to surrender his place in the WBA welterweight title queue as their October 22 negotiation deadline arrives.

His message leaves little room for bargaining. Catterall wants the fight he was promised, while Lopez seeks permission to bypass him for a unification against WBC champion Ryan Garcia.

“NO there isn’t an amount of money you can give me to step aside end of discussion,” Catterall posted on X. “I want what i deserve I want what I signed up for and I want to become a world champion and I won’t except any fucking offer to move out the way.”

Teofimo’s team has requested an exception from the WBA to pursue Garcia. Catterall can refuse to cooperate, but the sanctioning body still controls whether its order produces a fight or another delay.

That is where Catterall has reason to worry. The WBA also ordered Jaime Munguia to defend against Bektemir Melikuziev, yet Munguia is scheduled to face little-known Nikita Zon on October 31 instead. The organization has stated that it did not approve that matchup and is reviewing the situation. Bek is still waiting for his ordered opportunity.

Issuing an order does little for a mandatory challenger if the champion continues arranging other fights. The WBA’s response to Munguia has yet to put Bek in the ring with him. Catterall needs more than another statement confirming his position.

Eddie Hearn wants Teofimo to fight Catterall or vacate the belt. If Teofimo prefers the Ryan Garcia payday, Catterall shouldn’t have to put his career on hold to accommodate him.

Catterall won’t move. Now the WBA needs to decide whether Lopez must honor the order or gets to choose another opponent while keeping the title.

Even a promise that the Teofimo-Ryan winner must fight Catterall offers little protection. A lucrative immediate rematch could push him aside again. And if the WBA finally enforces its order, the winner could simply vacate and keep the WBC belt. Catterall would be left without the fight or any compensation for waiting—the same position another promise was supposed to prevent.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Believes He Can Beat Dalton Smith Easily
Sports.content:
Alberto Puello expects to have an easy night at Dalton Smith’s expense this Saturday in Sheffield. The Dominican challenger does not rate the local belt-holder anywhere near his hardest fights, making it clear that Smith will quickly realize finding a target against him is nothing like teeing off on Subriel Matias.

Puello is counting on his slick defense, ring smarts, and footwork to carry the night. In his eyes, Smith had it easy against a flat-footed brawler like Matias, but trying to pin down an awkward southpaw who refuses to stand in the pocket is going to give the champion fits from the opening bell.

“With my experience, hitting him without getting hit, and my skills, I think I can beat him easily,” Puello said to Fight Wire ahead of their October 24 fight in Sheffield.

When asked if Smith is the toughest test of his career, Puello laughed it off with a quick “Not at all.” He pointed right to Gary Antuanne Russell as a far rougher night, and even put Matias above Smith on the danger scale.

“He beat Subriel Matias, of course, but I also think Subriel Matias is a little more difficult than him,” Puello said.

That take is bound to stir up plenty of noise considering Smith stopped Matias. But Puello is looking strictly at styles. Teeing off on an aggressive slugger who marches straight into range is night and day compared to trying to catch a slick technician who makes you swing at fresh air all night.

“I’m a boxer with plenty of defense. I know how to move around the ring. Subriel Matias only has one way of fighting: going forward, taking punches and throwing them. I know how to hit without getting hit.”

Smith will have to work for every opening instead of banking on a sitting target to stay in punching range. If Puello sticks and moves, the local champion could burn serious fuel chasing a ghost all night instead of enjoying the pocket exchanges he had against Matias.

Puello also expects the roaring Sheffield arena to work against Smith. The champion will feel the heat to put on a show and satisfy his hometown crowd, while Puello can relax, stay patient, and stick to the blueprint without any outside pressure.

He is not just planning to scrape by on the cards, either. Puello made it clear his camp has him ready to take a clean twelve-round decision or jump on a stoppage the second Smith gets reckless and leaves an opening.

We already know how the boxing community will treat Smith if he loses to Puello. It will be merciless. The second the final bell sounds, skeptics will point out that the undefeated record was built on domestic fodder and that Matias was simply a flat-footed slugger tailor-made for Smith to counter.

The defeat would leave Smith’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, standing in the ring, needing to tell the fans what went wrong, and likely talking about a rematch.

Sports.title: Fired On His Day Off: Bradley Shreds Shakur Stevenson Over Lost Zuffa Contract
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley pulled no punches on his channel when breaking down how Shakur Stevenson lost his Zuffa Boxing contract. According to Bradley, Shakur fumbled massive money because he failed to deliver the one matchup the promotion actually cared about: Devin Haney.

“Shakur and his team, they thought that they was going to pull off a lick,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “They was just like, ‘Oh yeah, we got these stupid people up here. They don’t know nothing about boxing.’”

Bradley believes Shakur and his handlers completely misread the room, assuming they were dealing with naive outsiders whom they could easily manipulate. In reality, Zuffa’s willingness to spend fifteen million dollars per fight was meant strictly for marquee events, not hand-picked opposition like Gary Antuanne Russell.

“The fight that Zuffa wanted was Haney-Shakur. Period,” Bradley said.

He also mocked how readily Zuffa allowed Shakur to leave his contract, imagining the company responding, “We good.”

“How big of a damn diva you got to be to get released on your contract?” Bradley asked.

Bradley highlighted the absurdity of the split, pointing out how rare it is for a fighter to get released from a massive deal without ever stepping into the ring. He called out Shakur’s team for managing his career poorly, arguing that letting an eight-figure bag slip away was inexcusable.

While Bradley noted that prolonged weight squabbles and promotional moves damaged the negotiations on both sides, he laid the ultimate fault on Shakur’s reluctance to take real risks.

“All this was done because you afraid to lose that O,” he said. “It’s about protecting that damn O, bro.”

Now planning to launch his own promotional outfit, Shakur faces a stark reality. Finding financial backers willing to offer that caliber of purse without top-tier opponents is nearly impossible. As Bradley put it, someone has to put up the money, and Zuffa was ready to do that, but Shakur was unwilling to fight the opponent required to earn it.

When an entity like Zuffa comes into boxing with massive venture backing, they aren’t paying a fighter $15 million a fight out of altruism—they are paying for immediate, marquee box-office events to establish their footprint.

Shakur made three miscalculated moves. For starters, treating Silicon Valley/UFC money like naive marks. Bradley’s phrase that they thought they could “pull off a lick” was dead-on.

Shakur’s camp operated like they could sign the deal, dictate terms from high above, and then demand eight-figure checks to fight safe stylistic matchups like Gary Antuanne Russell. They forgot that Zuffa’s entire business model is built on rigid control, star matchups, and high returns.

Then he got dragged into prolonged posturing over weight. The nine-month negotiation saga over whether they’d fight at 144, 145, or 147 pounds drained every ounce of momentum. By letting the fight stall over a couple of pounds, and then throwing Keyshawn Davis into the mandatory picture as an artificial wedge, they gave Devin and Bill Haney the opening to outmaneuver them entirely and do their own business with DAZN.

Prioritizing the “0” over generational exposure: At 27 or 28, in the prime of his physical career, Shakur had a direct pipeline to beat Haney, fight Ryan Garcia, and cement himself as the premier American star of this era. Instead, the hyper-defensive mindset inside the ring mirrored his mindset outside of it: risk minimization at all costs.

Getting released from an eight-figure contract without ever throwing a single punch under the banner, literally getting “fired on your day off” while only doing a broadcast stint, is almost unheard of at that level of boxing.

Betting on yourself only works if the market is willing to pay what you think you’re worth. Now Shakur is left trying to build his own promotional company in a landscape where broadcast money is tightening, and network buyers aren’t handing out $15 million paydays for sparring sessions.

Sports.title: Arnold Barboza Hints At Devin Haney Title Shot
Sports.content:
Arnold Barboza Jr. dropped word on social media that a massive welterweight title opportunity just landed in his lap on short notice. While he confirmed that 147 pounds is locked in with a belt on the line, he kept the identity of his opponent quiet for now.

Speculation immediately involved Devin Haney after Haney’s anticipated matchup with Shakur Stevenson fell apart. Barboza’s remarks point to a fast-developing opening, even if ink has not officially met paper yet.

“I got some news today. It’s a blessing. I don’t know how real it is, but it sounds pretty real. It might be a big fight sooner than expected,” Barboza said on social media. “I’ll be stepping in at the last minute on some s***, but I don’t know where it’s going to be at, but it’s soon.”

The tight calendar creates the biggest hurdle. Barboza appears fully ready to sign before even knowing the host city, but world championship bouts offer zero room for entering camp cold. Securing an unexpected offer represents one hurdle; having the necessary weeks to dial in a precise tactical blueprint presents an entirely separate challenge.

If Haney ends up standing across the ring, Barboza faces an elite defensive technician. Taking on Haney demands an answer for his distance control, lead hand control, and inside tie ups. Simply tracking him across the canvas without cutting the ring effectively will turn the contest into a frustrating chase.

“A lot sooner than expected. Not no next year fight. A couple of weeks soon. Yeah, I’m fighting at 147. Yeah, it’ll be for a belt. We got to go for legacy,” Barboza said.

Teofimo Lopez also figures heavily into Barboza’s long-range calculations. Barboza sees capturing a 147-pound crown as his quickest ticket to securing a second chance against Lopez after coming up short in their junior welterweight clash.

“It’s not a rematch with Teo. Not yet. I got to win this belt to rematch him,” Barboza admitted.

Holding a world title strap provides massive leverage at the negotiating table. The immediate task requires transforming the sudden opening into an executed contract, setting up a targeted training block, and verifying the sanctioning body timeline.

Sports.title: DAZN Team May Call Canelo-Mbilli From London
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli could fight in Riyadh on October 31, with DAZN’s broadcast team following the action from a studio in London. The potential arrangement adds another question to a card already approaching under difficult circumstances.

Dan Rafael reports that the team is likely to call the event remotely if it goes ahead. His report leaves both points conditional: the card proceeding and the commentators working outside Saudi Arabia.

“Per sources, if #CaneloMbilli goes forward Oct. 31 in Riyadh, the likelihood is that the DAZN broadcast team will not be ringside and will call the card remotely from a studio in London,” Rafael wrote on X.

DAZN’s likely move speaks for itself. Calling one of the year’s biggest fights from television monitors thousands of miles away suggests the broadcast team wants no part of the danger in Riyadh. Promotional talk about the event going ahead cannot erase the attacks on the city’s international airport.

It also creates an awkward contrast. Commentators would work from the safety of a London studio, while Canelo, Mbilli and the undercard fighters would be expected to fly to Riyadh, attend media events and fight. If the risk is enough to keep the broadcast team away, the fighters have every reason to question why they should be there.

The background explains everything. Dan Rafael reported earlier on missile strikes and drone activity aimed at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, even while noting Canelo planned to go ahead anyway. Those strikes turned travel safety and the host city into the dominant story leading up to the bout.

A London crew can watch the live monitors, but calling an event off a monitor is never the same. Commentators lose their direct line of sight between broadcast angles. They miss corner chaos, subtle crowd shifts, and whatever happens outside the camera frame, leaving them watching the exact same feed fans see on their couches.

That is a massive drop in quality for a pay-per-view centered on the sport’s biggest earner. Calling action from ringside lets commentators catch real impacts, subtle cornerman instructions, and shifts in body language that cameras and boom mics miss entirely.

Canelo is penciled in to challenge Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title. The sanctioning body still lists October 31 in Riyadh on DAZN.

The card needs an official word on how the broadcast will work. Rafael’s reporting suggests fight week will look bizarre, even if both guys walk to the ring on schedule.

Ghana News.title: Seven Ghanaian fishermen rescued after drifting into Togo and Benin waters
Ghana News.content:
The seven fishermen who went missing at sea for two weeks have finally returned home after living through a terrifying ordeal.

Their canoe broke down, leaving them completely at the mercy of the ocean currents until a massive international rescue mission brought them back safely to Tema.

The crew, Kwamena Akyem, 40; Kofi Emmanuel, 32; Uncle Amoah, 45; Kwamena Nkum, 29; Kofi Aboagye, 36; Doboa, 35; and Agya Badu, 42, set off from Sekondi toward Axim on October 9 in their canoe, named Second Chance, but their outboard motor stopped working in the middle of the trip.

With no way to steer, winds and strong ocean currents pushed them way off course, drifting them all the way into Togolese and Beninese waters.

Naval Captain Festus Osei-Brobbey, who heads naval training for the Ghana Navy, addressing reporters in during a press briefing in Tema on Thursday, explained that they received a distress alert from the Fisheries Commission on October 20, which kicked off a massive joint search effort.

The Ghana Navy sent out three warships, while the Air Force, Special Boat Squadron, and National Security flew patrols overhead.

It wasn’t just a Ghanaian effort, as Navies from Togo and Benin jumped in to help, alongside regional maritime groups and even the French Embassy, all coordinating under ECOWAS frameworks.

The Beninese Navy finally spotted them with the help of local fishermen later on October 21 and handed them over to a Togolese ship, which then transferred them to the Ghana Navy Ship (GNS) Aflao right at the maritime border early Thursday morning.

Despite everything they went through, all seven were in decent shape. The crew on the Ghanaian vessel gave them food, water, and medical checkups right away.

Two Weeks of Surviving at Sea

Recounting their time lost at sea, crew leader Kwamena Akyem shared that they mostly had to lean on prayer to keep their spirits up. At one point, things got so heavy that they had to throw their entire fish catch back into the ocean just to lighten the canoe so it wouldn’t capsize.

When they finally touched land in Tema, the Ghana Maritime Authority and the ports authority made sure they were taken care of. Each fisherman got a life jacket, fresh water, clothes, and a proper medical check, plus a comfortable place to sleep before making their way back home to Sekondi.

Fixing Gaps for the Future

While everyone was thrilled with the happy ending, Captain Osei-Brobbey admitted the rescue exposed some glaring gaps in maritime safety. He pointed out that communication issues, a lack of night-vision gear, and poor distress signaling made the search harder than it should have been, suggesting that long-endurance drones and faster interceptor boats would go a long way.

On that same note, Professor Benjamin Betey Campion from the Fisheries Commission noted they are currently looking into affordable distress-tracking devices. The idea is to give fishermen a simple way to ping their exact locations to security agencies the second an emergency hits, hopefully preventing situations like this from dragging on for weeks.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS headmaster assault linked to alleged fetus burial, not sexual abuse – Apaak
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak has clarified that an earlier incident involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) concerned allegations of a fetus burial on the school premises, not sexual abuse.

Speaking on JoyNews’ News Night on Thursday, October 22, 2026, Dr Apaak said the incident, which reportedly led to students assaulting the headmaster, was separate from the sexual abuse allegations that have since emerged.

“It is important to indicate that while there is a report about an incident in the same school involving the same headmaster, that report was in relation to allegations of the burial of a fetus, which was said to have generated a reaction from a section of the students, leading to an assault on this very same headmaster,” he said.

“Now, that has nothing to do with any complaint with regards to sexual abuse, as was revealed to us in Manasseh Azure's documentary. It is important to put things in proper perspective,” he added.

According to Dr Apaak, the earlier incident followed allegations that a fetus had been buried on the school premises, prompting a reaction from some students and an assault on the headmaster.

He stressed that the incident should not be conflated with the separate sexual abuse allegations that have since drawn public attention.

The clarification comes amid scrutiny of the handling of allegations against the school's suspended headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai.

An investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni detailed allegations of sexual abuse involving as many as 19 female students.

The Ghana Education Service has suspended the headmaster pending investigations. The police have also forwarded a case docket to the Office of the Attorney-General for study and advice.

The allegations have not been established in court.

The Criminal Investigation Department has been invited to take over the criminal investigation, while the GES continues its administrative inquiry into how the complaints were handled.

The Attorney-General's Office is expected to review the case docket and advise on the next steps.

Ghana News.title: ‘ECOWAS For All’ campaign heads to Makola Market to educate traders on cross-border trade
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will take its “ECOWAS For All” public sensitisation campaign to the Makola Market in Accra on Friday, October 23, to educate traders and other business operators on regional trade and free-movement opportunities.

The engagement will focus on cross-border trade, the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS), customs procedures, immigration requirements, import clearance and business opportunities within the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

The campaign, organised in collaboration with relevant ministries, departments and agencies, was launched on October 2, 2026, under the theme “Bringing ECOWAS Closer to the Citizen: Promoting Awareness, Participation and Opportunities for Regional Integration.”

According to the Ministry, the Makola engagement is intended to improve traders’ practical understanding of ECOWAS trade and free-movement arrangements and how to use the opportunities responsibly.

The exercise will also provide market-specific guidance on border procedures, cargo, health requirements, transport operations and business concerns affecting traders and other market-based operators.

As part of the engagement, participants will have direct access to officials from the Ghana Immigration Service, Customs, Port Health and other relevant institutions through interactive clinics.

The clinics are expected to help address questions on travel requirements, customs documentation and lawful regional trade procedures, while recurring challenges raised by traders and transport operators will be documented for referral to the relevant institutions and follow-up.

The campaign will also highlight entrepreneurship and small-business opportunities within the ECOWAS region, with a focus on market women, women-led trader groups, importers and exporters, cross-border traders, freight and logistics operators, transport unions, artisans and small and medium-sized enterprises.

Young people, apprentices, youth-led businesses, market leaders and representatives of civil society and the media are also expected to participate.

The Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen collaboration between its ECOWAS Office, technical agencies, trader associations, transport unions, market leaders and the media to improve public awareness of regional integration.

The Makola engagement forms part of the broader “ECOWAS For All” campaign aimed at bringing information on regional integration, citizens’ rights and responsibilities, and trade opportunities closer to the public.

Ghana News.title: VRA to defend UG Corporate Tennis Championship Title
Ghana News.content:
The Volta River Authority (VRA) will return to the tennis court on Saturday, October 24, 2026, to defend its title at the University of Ghana Corporate Tennis Championship, with GOIL Ghana, Stanbic Bank Ghana and the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) set to challenge for the trophy.

The championship starts at 8:00 am on the University of Ghana Tennis Court, with the corporate teams competing for supremacy.

VRA heads into the competition as defending Champions of the UG Corporate Tennis Championship after an impressive performance in the inaugural 2025 edition, where the team defeated GOIL in the final to secure the title.

In the final, VRA won both doubles match, taking the first 9 – 4 and the second 9 – 5 to seal the championship without a deciding singles match. The two victories demonstrated VRA's strength in doubles play and secured the team the victory.

The 2026 edition presents another opportunity for participating companies to challenge the reigning champions for the title.

Since the title is on the line, VRA will want to repeat the form and team spirit that secured them the Trophy the previous year. Their opponents, on the other hand, will be determined to break their defence and dethrone the champions.

Beyond the competition, the championship provides a platform for corporate institutions to encourage healthy lifestyles among employees, strengthen professional relationships and build camaraderie through sport.



All eyes will be on the University of Ghana Tennis Court on Saturday 24th October as VRA begins its quest to retain the title against three determined challengers.

The University of Ghana Corporate Tennis Championship is powered by University of Ghana sports & Wellness Directorate and RITE Sports Services.

Ghana News.title: Ministry of Education creates direct reporting channels for sexual abuse complaints after Obuasi SHTS case
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Education is creating direct reporting channels, including a hotline, to allow students, parents, teachers and community members to report sexual abuse in schools without having to go through head teachers or other local authorities who may be implicated.

Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak disclosed this on JoyNews’ News Night on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying the allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) had exposed weaknesses in the existing reporting structure.

“In the wake of this issue, we became aware that there was a challenge within the reporting structure as far as GES is concerned,” he said.

Dr Apaak said the proposed channels would provide an alternative route for complaints to reach the Ministry of Education, enabling authorities to respond to allegations more promptly.

“We believe that if we were to provide a bypass that would allow victims, parents of victims, teaching and non-teaching staff in the schools where some of these despicable occurrences take place, or even community members and leaders, it will make it easier for such complaints to get to the ministry so that we can act tenaciously,” he said.

Dr Apaak stressed that a hotline was one of several reporting options under consideration, acknowledging that students are generally not permitted to carry mobile phones in school.

“The concept of the hotline is one among many other options,” he said.

He cited the Obuasi SHTS case as an example of how complaints could remain unresolved when people who become aware of alleged abuse cannot secure an effective response through existing channels.

“From the documentary, we saw pieces of evidence to suggest that other teachers, a housemistress, and even parents had become aware, and because the structure did not allow them to get the needed response in terms of action, this dragged on,” he said.

The Deputy Minister said the delay may have created opportunities for the alleged abuse to continue and affect other students.

“That may have then given an opportunity to the accused individual to even engage in this conduct and perpetrate this crime against other female students,” he said.

The proposed reporting channels follow allegations of sexual abuse involving the suspended headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, Zakaria Abdulai.

An investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni examined allegations involving multiple students and raised questions about whether concerns brought to the attention of some school authorities and parents received an adequate response.

The case has prompted calls for stronger safeguarding measures and more effective systems for reporting suspected abuse in schools.

The proposed channels are intended to allow complaints to reach education authorities directly, particularly where school-level officials may be implicated or fail to act.

Dr Apaak did not provide a timeline for the introduction of the new reporting options.

Ghana News.title: Police re-arrest 20- year old armed robbery suspect, who later dies after collapsing in custody in Upper East
Ghana News.content:
The Upper East Regional Police Command has re-arrested a 20-year-old suspected armed robber, Muntari Munumi, who later died after reportedly falling unconscious while being escorted by police to assist in the arrest of his alleged accomplices.

In a press release issued on Thursday, October 22, the Command said the suspect was arrested with an M16 assault rifle, three live rounds of ammunition and five expended cartridge shells.

Preliminary investigations indicate that two victims, whose names have been withheld, were attacked at Sapeliga Junction in Kobore while returning home from Bazua after work.

The suspect allegedly robbed them of a Royal motorbike, three mobile phones and GH¢1,820 in cash.

The victims reportedly struggled with the suspect and managed to seize his weapon after he fired several rounds but missed his target. They subsequently contacted the Googo Neighbourhood Watch Committee, whose members mobilised, arrested the suspect and handed him over to the police along with the weapon.

According to the Command, the suspect later disclosed the identities of his alleged accomplices and the source of the weapon. He reportedly agreed to lead police officers to arrest them.

However, while on the way, he complained of dizziness and suddenly fell unconscious. He was rushed to a nearby hospital but was pronounced dead on arrival.

His body has been deposited at the morgue for preservation and autopsy.

The police said efforts were underway to arrest the alleged accomplices and bring them before the law.

The Command commended the victims, the Googo Neighbourhood Watch Committee and the Chief of Sapeliga for their support and cooperation.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Israel frees suspects in two settler attacks as West Bank pogroms intensify
World.content:
Israeli court releases nine settler suspects over West Bank attacks as investigations into recent assaults continue.

Share Israel frees suspects in two settler attacks as West Bank pogroms intensify on social media

Israel has released nine of the 10 Israeli settler suspects arrested over attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, placing them under house arrest.

An Israeli court in Jerusalem ordered the release late on Wednesday, according to Honenu, a law firm that represents Israeli settlers.

Israeli police said one suspect remained in custody and that the investigation into the violent incidents was continuing.

Masked settlers were filmed last week assaulting Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photojournalist covering a Palestinian olive harvest who was taken to hospital and underwent surgery on a finger.

In a separate attack earlier this week, masked settlers assaulted French, Belgian and Polish diplomats and a French mayor in another part of the West Bank.

The suspects had been detained after the United States called for a crackdown on settler violence. France, Belgium and Poland also urged Israel to act.

“In the vast majority of attacks against Palestinians, no arrests are made at all,” said Yonatan Kanonich, head of research at the Israeli rights group Yesh Din. “In cases that receive media coverage … the police arrest several settlers and release most of them shortly afterward.”

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said in a post on X Thursday that the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory was “out of control”, with Palestinians continuing “to suffer daily attacks by Israeli settlers” and journalists and diplomats also being attacked.



Guterres called for “a credible political path towards lasting peace”.

Separately, the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission on Thursday said it documented 17 West Bank pogroms by Israeli forces and settlers against Palestinian farmers and their land during the olive harvest.

The commission recorded 409 attacks in October, 317 of which were by settlers and 92 by Israeli forces.

Nablus recorded the most attacks, 166, followed by Salfit with 91.

The commission said the attacks included assaults on farmers, preventing them from reaching their land, theft of crops and agricultural equipment, damage and burning of olive trees, as well as arrests, threats at gunpoint and live fire.

Ali Hassan Bazzari from Burqa died of wounds from settler gunfire while picking olives on October 7, the commission reported.

On Thursday, settlers set fire to olive trees near Imatin, east of Qalqilya, while Israeli forces forced farmers to leave and detained a farmer and several of his workers, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Near Yabad, west of Jenin, settlers stole 17 bags of harvested olives and equipment, local sources said.

Citing a local Palestinian official, Wafa reported that around Jenin, Israeli forces closed transport roads and most village gates, preventing farmers from reaching land in Barta’a.

World.title: Trump says NBA star LeBron James disrespected US national anthem
World.content:
NBA superstar LeBron James criticised by US President ⁠Donald ⁠Trump for disrespectful behaviour during national anthem.

Share Trump says NBA star LeBron James disrespected US national anthem on social media

US President Donald ⁠Trump criticised ⁠National Basketball Association (NBA) superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behaviour during the singing of the ⁠US national anthem at a recent NBA game.

“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country,” Trump ⁠said in a Truth Social post accompanied by a video showing James moving his body during the anthem.

“LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors ‌and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!”

The clip Trump shared showed James standing in line with the members of the Philadelphia 76ers, swinging his arms in a warm-up-type stretch and performing basketball shooting movements.

A representative for the 76ers ⁠did not immediately respond to a ⁠request from Al Jazeera for comment.

Trump has repeatedly criticised athletes for their behaviour during pre-game renditions of the US national anthem, notably beginning with NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick’s ⁠kneeling protest in support of racial justice.

Trump cancelled the planned White House visit of ⁠the Super Bowl champions Philadelphia Eagles ⁠in 2018 after the team disagreed with his call for players to stand during the anthem.

James became a leading voice in the Black Lives ‌Matter movement in 2020 and has frequently supported progressive issues as he ascended to the top of the NBA’s all-time ‌scoring ‌list.

World.title: Iran says seven ships hit in Hormuz Strait, warns US of wider response
World.content:
The US has pushed back on the IRGC’s claims, dismissing them as an attempt to increase oil prices ahead of US elections.

Share Iran says seven ships hit in Hormuz Strait, warns US of wider response on social media

Iran says that seven oil tankers have been struck and sustained damage in the Strait of Hormuz, the largest single-day toll for the waterway since the United States and Israel started their war against Iran on February 28.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said in a statement on Thursday that four of the vessels were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire overnight. The other three were disabled after striking mines.

The claims could not be independently verified, and the report did not provide details about possible casualties or the tankers’ flags.

The IRGC also warned that it could strike US bases across the Middle East if Washington moves to help tankers transit other parts of the strait.

“The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the IRGC said in a statement on its Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning.”

Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that “Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil prior to the US Midterm Election”.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, he added: “They are making up fake hits, mines, and everything else because more oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the conflict.”



A US Central Command spokesperson, speaking anonymously to Al Jazeera, also called Iran’s mine claims incorrect.

The spokesperson said US forces have cleared the international shipping lanes of mines and that Iran is using missiles and drones.

The strait remains open, the spokesperson said, with 95 percent of vessels getting through.

The attacks, the spokesperson added, show Tehran’s “desperation” under the US blockade, which cuts Iran off from the resources it needs to rebuild the military capabilities the US has said it destroyed.

Americans want ‘relief’ from war costs

“The number of ships and tankers attacked every single day is increasing, and Iran is saying it is continuing to do this because they are not going to allow any change in that situation,” said Al Jazeera’s Mohamed Vall, reporting from Tehran.

“They have full control over the Strait of Hormuz right now, they say.”

Vall said there is also talk in Tehran about an imminent escalation in the war, with the Iranians expecting the US to attack even before US midterm elections in early November.

“The IRGC army chief has boasted that Iran is more ready than anytime before, and has produced enough weapons and equipment to wage a symmetrical war against the United States,” he said.

Reporting from the US White House, Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett said: “Striking Iran does not appear to serve any Republican interests”, adding that pre-election polls tell the same story for Trump’s political party.

“What we’ve seen in surveys in recent months, and as of today, is that most Americans want relief from their tax money going to pay for any potential war with Iran that is ramped up,” Halkett said.

“There is real frustration over the rising cost for everyday Americans, given the rising fuel prices that have occurred as a result of this conflict … As a result, the US president is having to make the case.

“The pressure is on the president, and it’s not just from the opposition party,” she said. “It is also from within the Republican Party as well.”

World.title: ‘Longer we wait, worse it gets’: Struggle of Gaza’s breast cancer patients
World.content:
Breast cancer patients in Gaza face delayed diagnoses, medicine shortages and limited access to scans and treatment, leaving many fearing their condition is worsening.

Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip – Hiba Musbah has already been through seven rounds of chemotherapy for the breast cancer that is plaguing her body. Next week will be the eighth.

But the 36-year-old mother of three, from eastern Deir el-Balah, says her condition has continued to deteriorate as she waits to travel outside Gaza for further treatment.

“I can no longer take care of my children as I used to. My son is the one who helps me,” she told Al Jazeera. Her husband Motaz, who has a heart condition, has had to take on more responsibility as her health has worsened, caring for their three children – Mohammed, 13, Jaber, 10, and Ahmad, eight.

Musbah first noticed lumps around her right breast in January 2024, a few months after the beginning of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. At the time, she initially ignored them because she was displaced and the war was intensifying. Her mother eventually insisted that she seek medical attention.

Doctors confirmed it was cancer, but despite needing urgent surgery, it took two months for Musbah to be operated on, with the delay caused by Israeli military attacks around the Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, where she was being treated.

“The situation was difficult, with the bombardment and the tanks,” she said. “I delayed the operation because of the war. The last time, I nearly died from tank fire, so I postponed the operation.”

Her chemotherapy was initially also delayed for seven months because medicines were unavailable at Nasser Hospital.

Musbah’s experience reflects the reality facing hundreds of women with breast cancer in Gaza, where Israel’s war and blockade have severely weakened the health system’s ability to diagnose and treat the disease.



Shortages of medicines and medical equipment, broken diagnostic machines, the absence of radiotherapy and difficulties leaving the Gaza Strip for specialised care have turned the fight against cancer into another struggle amid Gaza’s deepening health and humanitarian crisis.

Surgery, chemotherapy and the cost of waiting

The lack of access to diagnostic equipment is now another source of anxiety for Musbah. She explains that she needs a new computerised tomography (CT) scan to assess how her condition has progressed, but has been unable to obtain one because the equipment is unavailable at public hospitals.

A private hospital has a scanner, she said, but the examination costs about 150 shekels ($48), which she cannot afford. The waiting time for an appointment can also exceed three months.

“I am now suffering from pain in my back and leg, and I have not had a scan for three months because the equipment is unavailable,” she said. “My doctor told me he was concerned that the disease might have spread through my body, but I still do not know.”

Musbah now struggles to walk and move one of her arms, and experiences pain in her shoulder, legs and eyes, as well as damage to her hair and nails during treatment.

“If I had received treatment early, things would not have reached this point. My condition has become much more difficult because my treatment was delayed,” she said. “Cancer patients also need good food, fruit, meat, fresh produce, but we cannot afford everything we need.”

According to Musbah, she has been waiting for around two years to leave Gaza for treatment after receiving a medical referral. But Israel, which controls all entry and exit from Gaza, has yet to give her security approval to travel.

“I want to travel, receive treatment and get better,” Musbah said. “I want to regain my health and return to the way I was before.”

Growing crisis

According to Gaza’s Ministry of Health, the Gaza Strip recorded about 360 new breast cancer cases annually before the war, compared with 250 in 2024 and around 260 in 2025.

The ministry has warned that these figures may not reflect the true number of cases because screening and early-diagnosis services have largely collapsed, potentially leaving hundreds of patients undiagnosed.



In a statement on October 1, the ministry said repeated breakdowns of mammography machines and shortages of laboratory supplies had severely restricted early detection in Gaza. Chemotherapy, hormonal and targeted therapies were also unavailable or critically scarce, while radiotherapy was completely unavailable.

The ministry said surgery for advanced tumours had also been halted because of a lack of specialised medical capabilities.

The shortage of diagnostic equipment adds another obstacle for women who suspect they may have cancer.

Dr Iman al-Haj Ahmad, an obstetrician and gynaecologist at Hikmat al-Jamei Health Centre in Deir el-Balah, understands these barriers both as a doctor helping women seek diagnosis and as a breast cancer patient herself, having been diagnosed in May 2025.

“I had to search until I found a place where I could get a mammogram,” al-Haj Ahmad said. “I kept thinking about ordinary women who don’t have the medical knowledge or connections that I have. If it was this difficult for me, how much harder must it be for them?”

Before the war, women could seek an initial examination at a primary healthcare centre and be referred to hospitals for mammography, ultrasound scans, and further tests.

Now, al-Haj Ahmad said, imaging services are limited, some cancer specialists have left Gaza, and tests needed to confirm a diagnosis are not always available through public health services. Some patients have to pay privately.

Al-Haj Ahmad waited about a month for surgery, eventually undergoing the operation at Nasser Hospital with a visiting Jordanian medical team while the hospital was operating under dangerous conditions.

Chemotherapy and severe food shortages later took a heavy toll on al-Haj Ahmad’s health. She said she lost about 20kg (44lb), her immune system weakened significantly, and doctors had to pause chemotherapy temporarily.

Al-Haj Ahmad is now receiving hormonal treatment while waiting to travel abroad for radiotherapy. Her referral for treatment abroad had been pending since September 2025.

Despite her own illness, she continues to examine women and refer suspected cases to the surgery department at Al-Aqsa Hospital. She also encourages women with a family history of breast cancer to be especially attentive to changes in their breasts.

“Early detection is especially important in Gaza because treatment options are so limited,” she said.

Pink October

It has been a year since the “ceasefire” began in Gaza, although Israeli attacks continue, bringing the death toll from the war up to more than 74,400 Palestinians.

October is the global Breast Cancer Awareness Month – also known as Pink October. Health workers in Gaza are participating in the international initiative, with staff at Hekr al-Jameh Health Centre in Deir el-Balah trying to reach women through healthcare visits and targeted awareness sessions.



It’s part of a Pink October campaign they’ve called “pink blooms from among the rubble”, which teaches women about breast cancer, demonstrates breast self-examination, and offers psychological support to those affected by the disease.

Sabreen al-Buhaisi, who supervises Hekr al-Jameh’s primary healthcare services, said the centre had screened between 700 and 800 women during the campaign. Seven or eight cases were referred to hospital surgical departments for further assessment.

But identifying women who may have cancer is only the first step. Al-Buhaisi said free mammography was available at a limited number of hospitals, where women face long waits for appointments. Private screening is too expensive for many families.

“The financial cost is very high for women. Our people cannot afford these expenses,” she said.

Still, al-Buhaisi urged women to continue examining their breasts despite the difficult circumstances the vast majority live in.

“Even displacement and living in the camps should not stop you from examining yourself,” she said. “Take five minutes of your time. It can make a big difference in your treatment journey.”

Amid these hardships, Musbah continues her fight against time.

She says she has repeatedly followed up on the travel arrangements, but remains unable to leave, with no clear explanation for the delay.

The evacuation process is coordinated between the World Health Organization and Gaza’s Ministry of Health, but they have to then submit patients’ files to Israel for security screening and approval.

“I have been waiting for two years,” Musbah said. “And I still haven’t travelled.”

World.title: Foreign national beaten to death by a mob in South Africa
World.content:
Share Foreign national beaten to death by a mob in South Africa on social media

A mob has beaten a foreign national to death during a protest in the South African port city of Durban, amid a wave of anti-immigrant tension.

Police said the group approached the man as he stood by the side of a road in Durban’s central business district.

The victim was allegedly assaulted by a group of about 50 people and was declared dead at the scene, a police statement said.

Police did not reveal the nationality of the man or details of the march.

They said the victim was in his 30s or early 40s, and they were still trying to identify suspects in the attack.

Anti-migrant marches

Durban has been at the epicentre of months of protests against foreign nationals, with looting and violence erupting after an anti-migrant march in the city two weeks ago.

Demonstrations calling for government action against African migrants who entered the country illegally began in June, with some escalating into violence.

Nigeria, Mozambique, Malawi and other countries have said some of their citizens have been killed in xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

South African authorities disputed some of those claims, saying that some deaths were linked to criminal activity.

Tens of thousands of migrants have left South Africa in recent months in one of the largest mass exoduses in years to avoid the violence.

The government also said that many were deported for not having the required papers to be in the country.

South Africa is Africa’s largest economy and migrants have moved to the country for opportunities. But communities in South Africa say there are not enough jobs and public services are overburdened.



South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has denounced anti-migrant violence but acknowledged that weak border control systems allowed undocumented migrants to travel to and stay in the country.

Government figures show there are about 2.4 million foreign nationals living among South Africa’s population of 62 million.

World.title: Sri Lanka beat England to overcome Harry Brook hitting fastest 200 in ODIs
World.content:
England captain Brook hits 202 in record ODI time, but Sri Lanka hit a six to win by two wickets with one ball to spare.

Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook’s record-setting knock.

The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.

South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.

Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.

Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.

Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.

Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.

Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka’s blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook’s earlier masterclass.

Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.



He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.

Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.

Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.

Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50, and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.

The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.

Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.

World.title: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
World.content:
"It was very difficult," says their father, Bajash Ali Sagir Hassan, a softly spoken shepherd. "We didn't find cars or transportation. One kind person brought us here [on the fourth day] while others refused."

As the family walked, the twins got weaker, according to their mother Lina. "They were exhaustedâ¦ there was cold and dust. Their vomiting and diarrhoea got worse."

By the time the newly homeless family arrived at al-Sadaqah hospital in Aden, the twins were barely clinging to life. "Just skin and bone," said a doctor, shaking his head, as he looked at their wasted limbs.

Raad was the sicker of the two - his ribs visible and his chest heaving as he took rapid, shallow breaths. He was barely bigger than the hands of the nurse who carried him gently to be weighed and measured.

Bajash looked on, worry etched on his face. He told us the twins were fed twice a day, but sometimes he could only give them water - after the war drove up the price of baby milk.

The diagnosis came quickly - severe acute malnutrition. That can be as deadly as a bullet.

World.title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
World.content:
Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.

Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.

Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.

There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.

Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.

"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.

She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".

The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.

A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".

"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".

"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.

But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.

He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected, external had been received and was being acted on.

World.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
World.content:
A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December.
