Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021.

Charles Tobin, a lawyer representing the BBC, said in court that "we still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff" with two months left in the discovery period, during which both sides are legally required to exchange information with each other on their case.

Trump cancelled a previous deposition on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance" while he was campaigning in Georgia.

In US law, a deposition is an out-of-court statement made under oath in response to questions, which is recorded for use in later proceedings.

The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge EnjoliquÃ© Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

Last week, attorneys asked that Lett compel Trump to face deposition after the last scheduled meeting did not take place.

On that day, Trump attended a midterms campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia and a fundraiser at his property in Mar-a-Lago in Florida.

In a separate filing on Wednesday, Trump's lawyers said that the president could appear for the interview between 11 and 22 January next year, and claimed that the BBC was "wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action."

Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.

The BBC apologised for the error and said that the broadcast gave "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".

The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US.

In July, Trump's lawyers conceded that they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC select or through US broadcasters.

Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, its commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary".

Typically, depositions take place in a lawyer's office - rather than a courtroom - without a judge physically present.

Depositions, however, carry legal weight and take place under oath. They are recorded verbatim by a court reporter, and the transcripts can later be used as evidence during trials.

In defamation cases, lawyers for both sides are normally present for depositions.

World.title: Crowd of 50 beats foreigner to death in South Africa
World.content:
The government has urged the demonstrators to act peacefully, while also accepting the need for immigration reforms. It says tens of thousands of foreign nationals have been deported or repatriated since it launched a crackdown earlier this year.

One of the groups behind the protests, March and March, had initially set a deadline of 30 June for all undocumented migrants to leave South Africa.

Several protests were held ahead of that deadline, with reports of attacks on people from other African countries.

These prompted several countries, including Zimbabwe, Nigeria and Ghana, to take steps to repatriate their citizens amid fears of further violence.

Nigeria accused South African authorities of responsibility for the deaths of two of its citizens that month.

Ghana also confirmed the death of a citizen, Bashiru Isak, a father of three who was fatally shot in Cape Town during demonstrations targeting foreign nationals.

His death led to a diplomatic row with South Africa, which said the scale of the violence had been exaggerated.

One of the leaders of the March and March movement, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, denied that she was xenophobic.

"We can't be living with these people for so many years and now when we say it is too much, it is enough, we are told that we are xenophobic," she told the BBC's Focus on Africa programme.

South Africa has struggled with xenophobic attacks for nearly two decades. In 2008, more than 60 people were killed and tens of thousands displaced during widespread attacks on foreign nationals.

The latest unrest comes against a backdrop of widespread poverty, deep inequality and unemployment affecting roughly a third of the workforce.

Migrants are frequently accused of taking jobs, contributing to crime and placing pressure on public services, although researchers say such sweeping claims are not supported by evidence.

Despite its economic difficulties, South Africa remains one of the continent's main destinations for migrants seeking employment, safety and better opportunities.

Additional reporting by Pumza Fihlani in Johannesburg

World.title: Germany target of 'intensive' espionage, Merz says after suspected Russian spy arrest
World.content:
Germany is the target of "intensive" espionage activity, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said after a Ukrainian national was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia.

Officials said the suspect, named as Vadym Y., had allegedly collected military-related intelligence from Germany.

Merz called the uncovering of the case a "success", but warned "let us not delude ourselves - the activities of Russian intelligence services in Germany remain at a consistently high level".

Several people alleged to be acting on behalf of Russia and other foreign powers have been arrested in Germany this year. Germany has been one of the leading European suppliers of weapons to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

The German Federal Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that Vadym Y., as he was identified under German privacy law, had been in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025.

It also said the Ukrainian man had collected information including "on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives".

He is due to appear before an investigating judge on Friday.

In January, a woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of gathering information for an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy.

Other arrests this year included a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man accused of spying on an individual supplying drones from Germany to Ukraine, according to the prosecutor's office.

World.title: At least four dead after storm brings flooding to southern France
World.content:
At least four people have died in France, and one other has been injured, after flooding caused by Storm Adam.

The storm triggered widespread flooding across southern France on Tuesday, inundating streets and disrupting transport.

The deaths included two women aged 86 and 26 who were found drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-RhÃ´ne region.

Corsica was also hit by severe weather. Local media reported that a 4x4 vehicle was swept away by floodwaters on Tuesday - one of the occupants escaped through a window, but another man was found dead. Authorities have not released further details about the fourth death.

In the towns of MouriÃ¨s and Saint-Martin-de-Crau, between Montpellier and Marseille, dozens of residents were accommodated in emergency shelters after the floods hit. Officials said one person had been injured in that area.

Roads and train lines âin â the area were also disrupted, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot wrote in a post âon X.

"The water has risen to unprecedented levels," Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the Bouches-du-RhÃ´ne department, said in a statement on Wednesday.

Witkowski expressed "a thought for all those who are in distress", adding: "We are mobilised at an exceptional level to resolve several issues."

World.title: Lula says rival should be disqualified over alleged Meta interference ahead of Brazil vote
World.content:
Brazilian President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva's campaign has requested the disqualification of right-wing challenger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro in the lead up to the final round of the presidential election on Sunday over alleged interference by social media company Meta.

In a petition filed to the country's top electoral court on Wednesday, the leftist incumbent president accused Meta, the tech giant behind Whatsapp, Instagram and Facebook, of limiting its content to boost Bolsonaro's campaign.

In response, Bolsonaro filed a petition seeking to disqualify Lula over what he said was the mass dissemination of government posts on WhatsApp.

The company has denied the campaigns have been treated unequally.

It comes after UN experts said on Wednesday that they were concerned about reports of discrepancies in the ability of each campaign to reach voters on Meta's platforms.

A report led by the UN's special rapporteur on freedom of expression said Meta must ensure a level playing field online during the election.

It cited incidents including "temporary interruptions of one candidate's campaign account; differences in audience engagement, user feeds, view counts and reach; restrictions on that campaign's Instagram posts".

"Information, including from Meta employees, suggests that accounts linked to one side of the presidential race were disproportionately curtailed," it read.

Meta has denied taking action to favour one side of the election and has said it would comply with an order from a Brazilian court to treat Bolsonaro and Lula equally.

Lula's campaign had previously filed a complaint alleging that accounts and content related to Bolsonaro were boosted.

Users also reported that Meta's artificial intelligence tools were not generating images related to Lula.

World.title: Paris extends curfew as Marseille and Lyon ban protests after riots
World.content:
Paris is extending a partial curfew restricting movement in parts of the city until Monday, as Marseille and Lyon impose a total ban on protests this weekend.

The Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums in the French capital will also be closed on Saturday as more demonstrations are expected.

France is still reeling from major disorder at the weekend, when large protests against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed.

In other parts of the country where protests have not been banned completely, only authorised union demonstrations will be allowed on Saturday, President Emmanuel Macron said.

Interior Minister Jean-Didier Berger said police deployments would be increased by 20% compared to last weekend, after the government was accused of being blindsided by the scale of the unrest.

France's justice minister said on Thursday that 217 people had been jailed over last weekend's disorder after being convicted in fast-track trials, with that number expected to rise.

GÃ©rald Darmanin said 2,700 people had been arrested across France and more than 1,000 have appeared in court.

Half of those detained had no prior criminal record, he said, according to Le Figaro newspaper.

Police in Paris said its curfew in Place de la RÃ©publique, where protesters gathered last weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area will be extended until Monday.

Movement will be prohibited in both areas from 23:00 local time (21:00 GMT) until 06:00 the following morning, the prefecture for the capital city said, adding that it had been ordered by Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez and Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu.

Public transport Marseille will be suspended on Saturday to try to prevent a repeat of the riots in the city.

The city saw some of the worst violence last weekend and damage to more than 500 businesses.

The prefecture for the RhÃ´ne region - which covers Marseille - said a curfew for minors would be extended to the entire population overnight on Saturday 24 October, from 23:00 until 05:00 (21:00 - 03:00 GMT).

Similar announcements have been made in Nice in the south, Toulon on the south coast, the centre of Rouen in the north-west, and Grenoble in the east.

Macron met intelligence services and ministers on Thursday, to prepare for the next national day of protests on Saturday.

"The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations. Those who want to continue to demonstrate, when they are trade union organisations, will have alternative routes proposed by the prefects," the French president announced.

"When they're not union organisations, wherever possible, they'll be banned."

He attacked what he called "political and even seditious acts organised by far-left groups that aim to bring down the Republic".

Curfews were imposed in several cities in the aftermath of the weekend rioting, and Macron said the government wanted a return to calm.

The gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement was behind many of last weekend's protests and Paris authorities have said several of their proposed marches have been banned.

Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings have been in place this week in cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.

Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu promised a "massive" deployment of police officers this week to deal with any unrest this weekend, but some officers have told French media they are not trained to deal with large crowds.

World.title: 2027: INEC addresses candidates’ list complaints, says preparations on track
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it has completed nine of the 14 activities contained in its timetable for the 2027 general elections, with preparations for the polls intensifying.

The commission disclosed this on Wednesday at a youth engagement programme in Abuja, where its National Commissioner for Information and Voter Education, Mohammed Haruna, represented the INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan.

The event, titled “The Electorate: A Youth Dialogue with INEC,” is in collaboration with Yiaga Africa, Enough is Enough Nigeria and the Nigeria Youth Futures Fund (NYFF) under the theme, “Let’s Talk About the 2027 Elections.”

Mr Haruna said the commission had made substantial progress in implementing its electoral timetable, which includes the conduct of political party primaries, publication of the voters’ register and release of the final list of candidates for the elections.

He described the voters’ register as a key component of the electoral process, noting that it would be used to determine eligible voters for accreditation on election day.

The national commissioner said the publication of candidates nominated by political parties was also among the activities already completed.

He, however, acknowledged that the initial publication generated complaints from some political parties over alleged omissions and discrepancies in the names released by the commission.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, INEC had invited affected parties to submit petitions and was working to resolve the complaints before finalising the candidates’ list.

Mr Haruna said the commission had also increased the frequency of its meetings as the elections drew closer to review its level of preparedness and take decisions required for the smooth conduct of the polls.

How INEC is structured

Mr Haruna also explained the structure of INEC, saying the commission is headed by “a chairman and 12 national commissioners who are responsible for policy decisions.”

He said the commission also has resident electoral commissioners deployed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

He explained that national commissioners are nominated by the president, considered by the Council of State and subsequently confirmed by the Senate.

Young Nigerians and 2027 elections

Speaking at the event, Yiaga Africa’s Programme Manager for Governance, Yetunde Bakari, called for deliberate measures to ensure that young Nigerians can participate safely and meaningfully in the 2027 elections.

Ms Bakari said young people should not be viewed merely as voters, but also as candidates, community mobilisers and participants in shaping Nigeria’s democratic future.

She cited findings from a Yiaga Africa voting intention survey which showed that 84 per cent of respondents were likely or very likely to vote in the 2027 elections.

However, she said 61 per cent of those surveyed feared that electoral violence could prevent them from voting.

She added that only 40 per cent of young respondents said they were very likely to participate in the elections, describing the figure as a concern that should be addressed by electoral stakeholders.

“Encouraging young people to vote will not be enough if we do not create conditions that make their participation safe, accessible and worthwhile,” she said.

Ms Bakari commended INEC for beginning preparations early, citing measures such as online voter registration, printable Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), planned nationwide mock accreditation exercises and efforts to strengthen the governance of electoral technology and artificial intelligence.

She, however, said INEC’s preparedness must be visible to citizens, arguing that public confidence would depend on transparency, effective communication and the credibility of the electoral process.

She urged the commission to communicate promptly with voters whenever technical or operational challenges arise, ensure transparency in the deployment of AI and make adequate arrangements for eligible voters in hard-to-reach communities.

Ms Bakari also urged young Nigerians to rely on credible sources of information, reject electoral violence and misinformation, and continue to hold elected officials accountable after the elections.

World.title: Police arrest four suspects over killing of police inspector, civilian in Rivers
World.content:
The Police Command in Rivers State says it has apprehended four persons over alleged involvement in the killing of a police inspector and a civilian in the state.

The command’s spokesperson, Blessing Agabe, disclosed this in an interview with journalists in Port Harcourt on Wednesday.

Ms Agabe, an assistant superintendent of police, said a police inspector named Womoma was shot dead on 4 August while on duty at a checkpoint along the East-West Road near Elele Alimini Junction in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers.

She also linked the suspects to the killing of Joseph Onyeka, who was shot dead in Rumuji Community on 23 July.

According to her, the suspects were apprehended following credible intelligence received by the police about the gang’s activities.

“Following credible intelligence on 4 October at about 4 p.m., the commander of the Violent Crime Response Unit led a team of police officers to confront the criminal gang.

“Our officers confronted the armed robbery and kidnapping gang, leading to the arrest of four suspects in Rumuekpe Community, Emohua Local Government Area,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Agabe said the police recovered several firearms and ammunition during the intelligence-led operation.

She said preliminary investigations linked the suspects to armed robbery and kidnapping incidents in Choba, Elele Alimini, Emohua and Rumuekpe communities.

“During interrogation, they confessed to the robbery and murder of Onyeka on 23 July at Rumuji Community and shooting of Insp Womoma while on checkpoint duty on 4 August,” she said.

READ ALSO: Akwa Ibom Assembly adopts recommendations to establish state police

Ms Agabe said two AK-47 rifles, two pump-action rifles, an English-made double-barrel rifle, a locally made revolver pistol and 58 rounds of live ammunition were recovered from the suspects.

She said efforts were ongoing to apprehend fleeing members of the gang.

The police spokesperson said the Commissioner of Police in Rivers, Olugbenga Adepoju, had directed personnel to intensify raids and targeted operations against criminals.

She said Mr Adepoju commended the operatives for their courage and professionalism in tackling crime in the state.

“The commissioner of police has assured residents that the command will sustain intelligence-led operations and investigations to dismantle criminal networks,” she said.

She urged residents to report suspicious activities promptly, assuring them that information provided would be treated confidentially.

(NAN)

World.title: Why opposition eyes can’t see the colours of a rainbow, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
With the general elections only three months away, opposition politicians are becoming increasingly good at running in circles. They have fancy names for this waste of time: consultations, tours, deliberations and meetings. As soon as one round ends, another begins – all motion, no movement.

It is quite ironic that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which should be at its wit’s end, is the party rallying a broad-based coalition and co-opting elements from opposition parties into a working alliance to retain power.

The trope in opposition circles is that the next general election is between APC and the Nigerian voters. This is a lazy assumption that not only ignores how ruling parties in Nigeria and elsewhere have been defeated, but one that assumes that voters are obliged, without effort, to inherit the opposition’s enemy.

Tinubu As Scapegoat

On the contrary, it is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s allies who are attempting to turn political differences into electoral cooperation even while at an advantage. In the end, there will be no shortage of claims about how the APC won, without genuine reflection about why the opposition lost.

President Tinubu is the number one scapegoat. Indeed, he has always been – from allegations of orchestrating a one-party system to planting the seeds of discord that unsettle the opposition.

He alone is responsible for the shoddy affairs in all political parties except his own, and he alone should be held to account for the blind ambition that threatens the chances of the opposition.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It is also Tinubu’s fault that the dominant APC is the party seeking to forge a rainbow coalition, rather than the other way around.

Perhaps Tinubu is also responsible for confusing the opposition parties on the petrol subsidy and depriving them of the power to offer coherent alternatives to the current economic travails. And since the announcement this week of the first Ebola case in Nigeria after 12 years, it’s already being suggested that Tinubu has weaponised Ebola to either derail or stall the 2027 elections.

Lessons of History

What they conveniently forget is that, perhaps until now, the history of the Nigerian variant of multiparty democracy has been more or less consistent.

When the Northern Peoples Congress (NPC) and the National Council of Nigerian Citizens (NCNC) formed the Nigerian National Alliance (NNA) in the run-up to independence, it was not because of ideological cohesion. It was a special purpose vehicle with one overriding aim – to capture power.

By 1964, the NCNC, part of the NNA, dissolved into a counter-group, the United Grand Progressive Alliance (UPGA), to challenge the NPC. Former allies turned into battering rams again to contest for power. The undercurrents of what happened then formed the background to Nigeria’s first military incursion into politics.

The civil-democratic cycles that followed in 1979 and 1999 also reveal shallow ideological inclinations and a greater focus on politics, tending towards regional alliances with a mix of ethnic and religious flavours.

Trend Across Africa

Nigeria’s coalition politics is not peculiar; indeed, it is quite a trend across Africa – except that Tinubu’s coalition is unique – initiated by a ruling party co-opting other parties into a power-sharing cooperative.

Kenya’s National Rainbow Coalition, or NARC, brought together opposition forces and defectors from the ruling establishment ahead of the December 2002 election. Its principal components were the National Alliance Party of Kenya grouping and the Liberal Democratic Party/Rainbow Coalition grouping. Under Mwai Kibaki, it defeated the Kenya African National Union (KANU), the party that had governed Kenya since independence in 1963.

The game changer was opposition coordination. In Kenya’s 1992 and 1997 elections, opposition parties collectively received more than 60 per cent of the vote but remained divided. In 2002, the alliance converted previously fragmented support into a winning electoral force.

The wheeling and dealing for the 2027 general elections are therefore not new, except that opposition politicians have, in this instance, opted to be poor students of history. Otherwise, they lack no template from which to borrow, learn, or copy and paste.

Retooling the Template

It’s the same template that the ruling APC reworked in 2013 and, by 2015, was able to successfully dislodge and dislocate the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) ambition to rule Nigeria for 60 years. What is more confounding is that many members of the currently fragmented opposition groups were active in politics or played direct roles that supported the APC’s rise to power.

That both the history and the lessons of the past have become a chemical formula that is difficult for the opposition parties to replicate is not just a problem for the political elite but a serious challenge for citizens yearning for credible options on the ballot.

Divided They Stand

An opposition whose principal flagbearers are overflowing with political enthusiasm but without a serious plan reduces the quest for alternative leadership through the democratic process to a mere academic exercise.

What, for example, was the point of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, taking issue with Diaspora remittances, when his party solicits funds abroad? Or the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, hiring lobbyists in the US at great cost when the party’s local faithful can barely rent a campaign tent?

It is not very difficult to see why the opposition is on their way to yielding the gunpowder and the flame to a ruling party struggling to convince an electorate at the very nadir of social dissatisfaction: they are afraid of the ultimate compromise that could lead to individuals giving up personal ambition for an overriding group interest.

To make any headway in the circumstance, the stumbling block of personal ambition must be removed. Self-seeking and self-interest are the mountains the opposition needs to level before they can think of displacing President Tinubu in next year’s elections.

A divided front will never work. The longer it takes them to forge a common front, the more difficult it becomes to have one. Perhaps, the contingency plan is to go into the elections, find faults with the process, get some alibis, go to court and hope for a judgement in their favour.

Merry-Go-Round

It doesn’t help that the presidential candidates and running mates in the two main opposition parties – NDC and ADC – contradict themselves and have failed to provide clear alternative directions on critical national issues such as security and the petroleum subsidy.

Coalitions mean binding agreements rather than affectionate declarations; pooled resources rather than parallel fundraising campaigns; functioning local coordination rather than competing claims of nationwide popularity; and programmes that explain why and how replacing the government would improve the country.

For now, Nigerians are being treated to a familiar production: the ruling party campaigning for another term while its challengers campaign for the chairmanship of the next coalition meeting.

If this were a book, the perfect title would be 2027: Defeat Made Easy.

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

World.title: EFCC secures order to freeze account over alleged N1.06bn fraud
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has obtained a court order to freeze an account belonging to Yili Fu Liang Trading Co. Ltd over the alleged transfer of N1.065 billion from Renmoney Microfinance Bank through unauthorised electronic transactions.

The judge Yelim Bogoro of the Federal High Court in Lagos granted the order on 16 October following an ex parte application by the commission in suit number FHC/LAG/MISC/1392/2026.

The EFCC also asked the court to place six Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) on a watchlist pending the conclusion of investigations and possible prosecution.

In a statement on Thursday by the EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale, the commission said it began investigating the matter after receiving a petition from Blackwood Law, acting on behalf of Renmoney Microfinance Bank Limited, on 21 September.

The petition concerned alleged unauthorised transfers through the bank’s electronic banking platform on 18 September.

According to an affidavit filed in support of the application, 12 suspicious transactions occurred between 4:52 p.m. and 8 p.m. that day. The bank’s preliminary review put its financial exposure at N1.065 billion.

Gbolahan Dada, an EFCC investigator attached to the Bank Fraud Section, said preliminary findings traced the funds to beneficiary accounts bearing the name Yili Fu Liang Trading Co. Ltd and linked to a collection account operated through Kora Payment Network.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The statement noted that the affidavit revealed that investigators identified nine inflows totalling N1,065,500,000 into the collection account on 18 September.

Mr Dada further alleged that the account holders did not have corresponding funds in their accounts before the transactions occurred. He said the funds needed to be preserved while investigations continued and possible prosecution was considered.

The investigator also stated that checks on the BVN portal and account-opening documents allegedly linked the six BVNs listed in the application to the company.

He alleged that the individuals behind the company were Nigerians operating under the umbrella of a Chinese company and said they needed to be questioned as part of the investigation.

The EFCC told the court that the account freeze and BVN watchlist were necessary to prevent the funds from being dissipated while investigations into alleged stealing and money laundering continued.

The application was brought under Section 44(2)(k) of the Nigerian constitution, sections 26 and 28 of the EFCC Act, and the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

After hearing submissions from the commission’s lawyer, Z.B. Atiku, Justice Bogoro granted the request.

The court adjourned the matter until 19 January 2027 for a report on the investigation.

The allegations have not been established in court.

World.title: SROL champions responsible mining at Nigeria Mining Week 2026
World.content:
Segilola Resources Operating Limited (SROL), a subsidiary of Thor Explorations Ltd and operator of Nigeria’s first commercial gold mine, reaffirmed its commitment to responsible mining at Nigeria Mining Week (NMW) 2026, where it participated as a Diamond Sponsor.

Held from 12th to 14th October at the Abuja Continental Hotel, the 11th edition of NMW brought together government representatives, investors, mining companies and technical experts to fully explore this year’s theme of “unlocking investment and growth through partnerships” and building capacity across the mining value chain. The event was hosted by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and organised by the Miners Association of Nigeria in partnership with PwC Nigeria.

Delivering the keynote address at the main conference, SROL’s Country Manager, Austin Menegbo, noted that the success of the Segilola Gold Mine is operating proof that successful commercial gold mines can be built and operated in Nigeria and also highlighted the importance of patient capital, technical discipline, effective regulation and strong community partnerships in establishing a commercially viable mining industry in Nigeria.

He said: “The opportunity before Nigeria is significant. But potential, by itself, creates no jobs, earns no export revenue, builds no skills and transforms no communities. Potential becomes valuable only when institutions and industry work together to convert it into responsible production. Segilola has shown that this can be done. Our responsibility now is to make the path clearer for the projects that should follow—not bylowering the bar, but by making the rules coherent, the processes credible and the partnerships real. If we do that, Nigeria will not merely have a successful gold mine. It will have a stronger mining industry: one that attracts serious capital, rewards responsible operators, expands Nigerian participation and delivers enduring value to the nation.”

SROL’s senior management and technical team also participated in key panel discussions: Menegbo; Madhurii Sarkar-Amoda, Community Development and Stakeholder Manager; Sikiru Haruna, Mines Manager; and David Mbrekpadiaha, Environment Lead, contributed to discussions ranging from beneficiation and refining, responsible mining and maintaining social license to operate across the mine life cycle.

At its masterclass, “From Compliance to Stewardship – Water Management: The SROL Way”, SROL shared insights into its approach to water management, recycling and conservation. The session highlighted the importance of integrating water stewardship into mining operations and managing water resources responsibly throughout the mining process.

SROL also delivered “Building a Commercial Gold Industry in Nigeria – Lessons from Segilola and the Path to Scale”, sharing lessons from establishing Nigeria’s first large-scale commercial gold mining operation and exploring opportunities for the wider industry. Through its exhibition booth, the company further engaged stakeholders on environmental stewardship, workplace safety and host community development.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria’s mining sector offers significant opportunities for economic diversification, job creation and industrial development. Realising this potential will require investment, effective regulation, local capabilities and responsible environmental management.

SROL’s participation at NMW 2026 reinforces its commitment to sharing operational expertise, advancing responsible mining practices and supporting the development of a competitive mining industry that creates lasting value for Nigeria and its communities.

World.title: Diri calls Duke pretender, alleges presidential ambition is bid for rehabilitation
World.content:
Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has accused former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke of political pretence, alleging that his presidential ambition is a bid to secure political “rehabilitation”.

Mr Diri made the allegation while responding to Mr Duke’s remarks about the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, escalating their disagreement over the feasibility of constructing roads and bridges across Bayelsa’s swampy terrain.

In a video posted Thursday on the Bayelsa Government New Media Facebook page, Mr Diri described Mr Duke as a “jester and a pretender”. He accused him of adopting an insulting posture towards him as a serving governor during an appearance on ARISE News Television.

“There is no councillor from PRP in your own ward, yet you pretend to be a presidential candidate so that at the end of the day, you will be rehabilitated,” Mr Diri said.

Mr Duke is the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.

The governor’s remarks followed Mr Duke’s description of him as a “local champion” during an interview on ARISE News, in which the former governor questioned the feasibility and affordability of the coastal highway.

Mr Duke argued that the proposed highway was impractical because of Bayelsa’s swampy terrain and the financial implications of building hundreds of bridges along the route.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But Mr Diri rejected the criticism, insisting that the state’s experience in constructing roads and bridges across difficult terrain showed that the project was achievable.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Diri cited road projects in Bayelsa to counter Mr Duke’s claim that the highway was unbuildable through the state.

The governor said he was particularly disappointed that a former governor from the Niger Delta would make remarks he considered dismissive of Bayelsa and its people.

“The former governor went to ARISE TV. What I saw there was more of an insult,” Mr Diri said.

He also took exception to Mr Duke’s reported remark that he (Duke) did not know him.

“Donald Duke, hear me well, I am not ‘that fellow’. I am an elected, sitting governor of Bayelsa State,” he said.

“If you claimed you don’t know me, I don’t likewise know you.”

Mr Diri argued that Mr Duke, as a former governor, should respect the office of a governor regardless of their personal relationship.

He also dismissed Mr Duke’s description of him as a local champion, saying his political responsibility was to represent the interests of the people who elected him.

“I am a local champion because that is where I was raised. I was elected to serve the local people. I was elected to champion their cause,” he said.

The governor later questioned Mr Duke’s record on the Bakassi dispute, which led to the transfer of the peninsula to Cameroon following a 2002 International Court of Justice judgement.

“Donald Duke, let me ask you, you were in office when Bakassi was ceded to Cameroon. Because you were not a local champion, you did nothing about it,” Mr Diri said.

He accused the former governor of failing to defend local interests while in office, contrasting that record with his own commitment to defending Bayelsa and its people.

Mr Diri said his response went beyond a personal disagreement; he saw it as an attack on the state and its people.

“I do not take up people. I am not one to insult people. I don’t insult leaders, I don’t insult elders. But what you have done is not just about me. It is about my environment; it is about my people,” he said.

“I will stand tall at all times to defend this environment and defend the people of Bayelsa State.”

Diri misconstrued my statement – Duke

When contacted for his reaction to Mr Diri’s remarks, Mr Duke told PREMIUM TIMES on Thursday that the governor misconstrued his statement.

“I never said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road was not desirable; all I said was that, at this time, it is not financially feasible, and Minister Umahi vindicated me by stating the road is being diverted to join the East -West Highway for the same reasons I stated,” Mr Duke said in a written text to our reporter.

“I can understand him championing the road within his vicinity. That’s perfectly acceptable. If the road were ever built, I’d be one of its greatest beneficiaries as I live both in Lagos and Calabar. I used Bayelsa only as an example of the challenging terrain the road will have to traverse.

“But honestly, I doubted from the outset the road would be built. I said it then, and I say it again: the road, as we know it, will terminate at Epe, and that’s what has happened.

“And how did I disrespect his office? By disagreeing with him?” the former governor said.

Background

The dispute began after Mr Duke questioned the technical and financial feasibility of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, a federal government project planned to traverse nine coastal states.

Mr Duke argued that Bayelsa’s swampy terrain would make construction difficult and expensive, and questioned the project’s priority amid Nigeria’s competing development needs.

Mr Diri, however, said his administration had built roads and bridges in similar conditions, citing projects including the Nembe-Brass Road, the Sagbama-Ekeremor-Agge Road, and the 630-metre bridge across River Nun at Angiama in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

In a subsequent response reported by PREMIUM TIMES, Mr Duke maintained that the existence of roads and bridges in Bayelsa did not settle questions about the coastal highway’s cost, engineering requirements and economic justification.

World.title: FIFA approves Normalisation Committee to run Nigerian football
World.content:
FIFA has approved the appointment of a Normalisation Committee to manage the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) pending fresh elections to its Executive Committee, following months of leadership uncertainty and calls for comprehensive reforms.

The NFF announced the decision in a statement, saying the Bureau of the FIFA Council approved the committee’s appointment on Thursday.

According to a letter signed by FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström and addressed to NFF Acting General Secretary Emmanuel Ikpeme, FIFA and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) will jointly appoint the committee’s members.

“The normalisation committee shall consist of a suitable number of members, who will be appointed jointly by FIFA and CAF as soon as possible,” the letter said.

FIFA also set a deadline for the committee’s tenure, stating that its mandate would end once it had completed its assigned tasks, but no later than 31 May 2027.

“The period during which the normalisation committee shall perform its functions shall expire as soon as it has fulfilled all of its tasks, but by no later than 31 May 2027,” the letter stated.

The NFF said the committee would oversee the federation pending fresh elections into its Executive Committee. Its members will not be allowed to contest any positions in the forthcoming elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances,” the letter stated.

Meanwhile, the NFF Secretariat will continue to handle the federation’s day-to-day administration and run Nigerian football until the committee members are appointed.

Leadership crisis

The decision follows the mass resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Musa Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s Executive Committee on 27 August.

Mr Gusau resigned 34 days before the end of his four-year tenure, which began after he was elected in Benin City on 30 September 2022.

The resignations triggered a leadership transition and disrupted preparations for the NFF elective congress scheduled for 27 September in Lafia, Nasarawa State. The electoral process was suspended as FIFA and CAF consulted on the federation’s future.

Emmanuel Ikpeme, a former NFF Deputy General Secretary, was appointed acting General Secretary to oversee the Secretariat, while Ademola Olajire became acting Deputy General Secretary.

The crisis unfolded against a difficult period for Nigerian football, including the Super Eagles’ failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the Super Falcons’ failure to qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup. The latter ended Nigeria’s record of appearing at every edition of the women’s tournament since its inception in 1991.

Tinubu’s reform directive

On the day the NFF leadership resigned, President Bola Tinubu ordered comprehensive reforms of Nigerian football, calling for changes to governance, administration, stakeholder representation, development pathways, domestic competitions and accountability.

“The reform must respond to a longstanding need to strengthen governance, administration, stakeholder representation, development pathways, domestic competitions and accountability across Nigerian football,” Mr Tinubu said.

He directed National Sports Commission (NSC) Chairman Shehu Dikko to work with the NFF Secretariat and football stakeholders, and to engage appropriately with FIFA and CAF.

Zurich meeting, FIFA-CAF consultations

On 1 September, Mr Dikko led a Nigerian delegation to FIFA headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland, to discuss the crisis and a reform roadmap.

The delegation included NSC Director-General Bukola Olopade, former NFF President Amaju Pinnick, acting NFF General Secretary Emmanuel Ikpeme and the federation’s Director of Legal Services, Okey Obi.

CAF 2nd Vice President Kurt-Okraku and FIFA Director of Member Associations for Africa Gelson Fernandes also attended the meeting.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino later said the discussions covered institutional, governance and developmental issues, including ways to strengthen Nigeria’s football structures and create more opportunities for young players.

In a letter dated 7 September, FIFA and CAF directed the NFF to suspend its electoral process while they assessed the legal, governance, administrative and electoral implications of the leadership crisis. They also announced plans for a joint assessment mission to Abuja to engage relevant stakeholders.

The approval of the Normalisation Committee marks a new phase in the process, with FIFA and CAF now set to appoint the members who will oversee the federation until its assigned tasks are completed and fresh elections are held.

The committee’s composition and full details of its responsibilities have yet to be announced. Its effectiveness will be measured by its ability to stabilise the NFF, address governance concerns and provide a credible path towards elected leadership.

World.title: Foundation seeks effective implementation of VAPP Law in Imo
World.content:
The CLEEN Foundation, a non-governmental organisation, has urged security agencies, justice actors, and community leaders in Imo State to address knowledge gaps hindering the implementation of the Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Law.

The Executive Director of the organisation, Peter Maduoma, made the call in Owerri on Wednesday at the opening of a two-day state-level policy dialogue on bridging VAPP Law implementation gaps.

Mr Maduoma explained that the dialogue aimed to improve institutional capacity and foster accountability among stakeholders for a more coordinated, survivor-centred response system.

He said that despite the established legal frameworks, survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) continued to face barriers in accessing justice, protection, medical care, and psycho-social support.

“Ground-level empirical evidence indicates that the primary driver of this operational failure is a critical knowledge deficit among key sub-national duty-bearers,” he said.

He argued that frontline enforcement officers and civil society groups in many states had never physically seen, read, or received formal guidance on the VAPP legislation.

“The practical effectiveness of these legal provisions depends on the ability of institutions and duty-bearers to understand and perform their respective obligations,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the foundation will distribute copies of the VAPP Law, assess institutional bottlenecks, and support local government actors to establish designated reporting desks.

He said that the intervention, funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs through the Norwegian Embassy, is currently being implemented across 13 focal states.

Mr Maduoma urged participants to draft and sign a state-specific action plan with clear monitoring indicators to ensure effective local-level enforcement across Imo.

Need for sexual assault referral centre in Imo

In his contribution, the traditional ruler of Umuororonjo Autonomous Community, near Owerri, Clinton Uboegbulam, urged the Imo State Government to establish a Sexual Assault Referral Centre.

Mr Uboegbulam said that a dedicated centre would streamline victim data collection and enable institutional stakeholders to manage GBV cases efficiently.

“GBV occurs daily, but our ability to effectively handle these cases depends largely on the facilities and procedures we put in place,” he said.

Also speaking, the Executive Director of Open Arms Initiative, Juliet Okeihi, said the absence of centralised data was hindering full implementation of the law.

Mrs Okeihi lamented that many law enforcement officers, legal practitioners, and community stakeholders still lacked a comprehensive understanding of the legal instrument.

She commended the dialogue for exposing inter-agency operational gaps and the lack of structured coordination among key duty-bearers in the state.

“The law is in place, but how well are we using the instrument of the law to tackle the cases?” she asked.

On her part, the State GBV Coordinator and Social Welfare Officer, Amarachi Ekeocha, emphasised the need for a functional agency to oversee referral pathways.

Mrs Ekeocha expressed concern over prolonged judicial delays, saying that some rape cases lingered for over five years, despite the law stipulating resolution within three months.

She advocated continuous sensitisation across the judiciary, effective utilisation of the sex offenders register, and stronger collaboration among relevant state actors.

Contributing, the state Director of Public Prosecutions, Martins Udoku, said the state Ministry of Justice had commenced uploading rape and violent crime records onto official registers.

The two-day event drew participants from the police, Ministry of Women Affairs, Ministry of Justice, NAPTIP, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, traditional rulers, and civil society groups, among others.

(NAN)

World.title: Stop announcing how much your movie made at the cinema — Filmmaker Biodun Stephen tells colleagues
World.content:
Nollywood filmmaker Biodun Stephen has urged colleagues to stop announcing cinema earnings, warning that the practice puts unnecessary pressure on other filmmakers and creates a narrow definition of success in the industry.

Stephen made the remarks during Paul & Baaj: In Character podcast, where she argued that publicising box office figures could distract filmmakers from focusing on the quality and impact of their work.

“I think that we really should do away with the announcements,” she said.

“I feel like this is a distractions and it puts pressure on those other people who… feel as if that is the determine and that’s how you determine my success,” she added.

The filmmaker explained that frequent announcements of cinema earnings could make others feel unsuccessful if their projects failed to achieve similar figures.

Using a slippers business as an example, Stephen said people often rush to replicate successful ventures without understanding the effort and strategy behind them.

“Somebody starts selling slippers and people are rushing to buy slippers, the next one… is going to sell slippers… because they think that slippers sells, meanwhile they don’t understand what you have put in to ensure the slipper sells.”

Biodun Stephen also questioned the tendency among some filmmakers and actors to pursue international recognition before establishing a strong presence in Nigeria.

“It’s great to hunger for more, but I always say, have you even conquered Nigeria that can you stand and say that if I go to Kano they know me as an actor?”

She further argued that box office earnings alone were insufficient to determine a film’s quality, longevity or potential to reach international audiences.

According to her, a film could generate substantial cinema revenue without necessarily being outstanding, while a well-made production with export potential might earn less and receive little recognition.

“The film go tough but it can be a lot of crap and then the film that is really good that can travel, that has export value can do 40 million… the only yard stick for measuring success is this very shallow number.”

Explaining her approach to filmmaking, Stephen said her motivation was rooted in purpose rather than the pursuit of box office records or audience numbers.

“I’m doing it because I am living a life of purpose, I’m not chasing the numbers, I’m not chasing the audience.”

She added that the emotional impact of her stories and the difference they made in people’s lives were more meaningful to her than industry awards.

“When people call me to pray… and cry and say thank you so much, Jesus, my work is done, no award.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Benue State capital, Makurdi, has been thrown into darkness following the withdrawal of services by members of the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, in the Jos Electricity Distribution Plc, JED, chapter, over an alleged attack on some of its members by suspected armed men.

The union alleged that the attackers invaded the Makurdi District office of JED, seized the Benue State Operating Officer, Mr. Samson Abah, and an unspecified number of other workers before taking them to the River Benue Bridge, where they were reportedly assaulted.

According to the union, the attackers also seized the workers’ mobile phones and other personal belongings, demanded money for their release and allegedly forced them to reconnect electricity supply to the Benue State Government House.

The Acting National Secretary of NUEE, Dominic Igwebike, who disclosed this in a statement, said the incident followed the disconnection of electricity supply to Government House over an alleged discovery of meter bypass by government officials.

The union’s position came amid an escalating disagreement over electricity supply to the state government’s seat of power, with the Benue State Government dismissing the allegations and accusing JED of making unsubstantiated claims against it.

Igwebike said the union could no longer guarantee the safety of its members if they continued to work under the prevailing circumstances, insisting that the withdrawal of services was necessary to protect their lives and property.

He said, “Our members cannot continue to work under their brutalised, intimidation and threats to life until we are assured of the safety of our lives and properties.”

Confirming the shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, a JED staff member, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak on the matter, said the workers withdrew their services following the alleged attack on their colleagues.

“Our office was attacked and our union asked us to withdraw our services, so we have shut down power supply to Makurdi.

We have left the office after shutting down, and Makurdi will not have power supply until the matter is resolved with our union,” the staff member said.

However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image.

In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Chief Solomon Iorpev, the government said it would not accept allegations linking it to violence, abduction or illegal electricity connections without credible evidence.

The statement read, “The Government of Benue State strongly rejects the baseless and defamatory allegations contained in the press statement issued by Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED Plc) on October 22, 2026. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.”

Addressing the allegations surrounding the reported attack on JED workers, the government questioned the evidence linking it to the incident, arguing that the distribution company had not provided verifiable details to substantiate its claims.

According to the statement: “JED Plc’s own use of the word ‘allegedly’ confirms that it has no evidence linking the Government to the incident of October 21, 2026. No names, identities, or credible references were provided. The Government categorically rejects this insinuation.”

On the dispute over electricity supply to Government House, the state government said issues concerning transformer energisation and alleged metering irregularities should be handled through the appropriate regulatory and judicial channels.

It stated, “Issues of transformer energization and metering irregularities are regulatory matters. They must be addressed before the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts, not through inflammatory press releases.

“Assertions of abduction, assault, and injuries remain unsubstantiated. The Government does not condone violence and demands that impartial, evidence-based, and transparent investigations be carried out by security operatives,” the statement added.

Expressing displeasure over JED’s handling of the controversy, the government described the company’s public reaction as premature, arguing that it should have allowed security agencies to establish the facts before making allegations in the media.

“The reckless outburst by the JED without conclusive investigations is suspicious and amounts to sponsorship by enemies of state to tarnish the image of the government,” the statement alleged.

The government also faulted JED’s reference to an earlier incident on September 3, 2026, describing the company’s account as misleading.

It challenged the distribution company to produce documentary evidence of its alleged previous communications with the state government over the dispute.

“The company has failed to produce records of its alleged ‘several communications’ with the Government. The State challenges JED Plc to publish such correspondence if it exists,” the statement said.

Insisting that electricity distribution companies must comply with the same regulatory requirements and safety standards applicable to their customers, the government said JED must also be held accountable for its operations.

The statement added: “JED Plc itself acknowledges that interventions must comply with regulatory requirements and safety standards. The Government insists that this standard binds JED Plc as firmly as it binds any customer, including public institutions.”

The state government further warned JED against what it described as attempts to politicise its operations and damage the integrity of the state.

“The Benue State Government will not tolerate attempts by any business entity to politicize its operations or malign the integrity of the State. JED Plc is hereby strongly warned to desist from making baseless accusations in the media,” it said.

Consequently, the government demanded the immediate withdrawal of what it described as the insinuation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of the allegation that it engaged in meter bypassing or illegal electricity connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State.

It warned that it would consider legal action if JED persisted in disseminating what it described as false information.

“The Government remains committed to the rule of law, the protection of lives and property, and constructive engagement with stakeholders in the electricity sector. However, it will not hesitate to pursue legal remedies should JED Plc persist in disseminating falsehoods,” the statement said.

The government added that the people of Benue State deserved reliable electricity supply, respectful treatment and accountability rather than what it termed reckless allegations.

As of the time of filing this report, the dispute had resulted in a shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, with the workers insisting that they would not resume operations until the matter was resolved with their union.

World.title: S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse
World.content:
By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo

The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police.

While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law.

The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday.

The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly.

Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly.

The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations.

He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training.

Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property.

The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters.

Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people.

According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.”

Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state.

Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities.

He said the establishment of state police would help “curtail incessant violence and herdsmen attacks in different parts of the state.”

However, the member representing Igbo-Eze South Constituency, Hon. Harrison Ogara, cautioned that the proposed state police system could be abused by political officeholders if adequate safeguards were not established.

Ogara expressed concern that state police formations might be used to intimidate political opponents, stressing that effective oversight and accountability mechanisms were necessary to protect the institution from political interference.

He said: “State Police formations could be used to intimidate political opponents if adequate safeguards are not put in place.”

The lawmaker also called for professional standards, transparent accountability structures and sustainable funding arrangements to ensure that state police personnel discharge their duties without undue political influence.

According to him, effective oversight would be essential to ensuring that the proposed security structure serves the public interest rather than the interests of those in power.

The Speaker of the House, Chief Uche Ugwu, said the proposed changes to the naming of Nigeria’s policing institutions could also influence institutional orientation and the attitudes of personnel.

The proposal includes changing the name of the Nigeria Police Force to the Federal Police Service, alongside the establishment of the State Police Service.

Ugwu said the changes could contribute to a shift in institutional orientation and personnel attitudes, potentially improving the delivery of policing services.

The proposed constitutional amendment comes amid growing calls for the decentralisation of Nigeria’s security architecture to enable states to respond more effectively to local security challenges.

Proponents argue that state police would improve intelligence gathering and response times, while critics have raised concerns about possible political abuse, inadequate funding and the need for strong accountability mechanisms.

Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker

The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill.

Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny.

He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large.

The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing.

“We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said.

Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard on Thursday afternoon that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill.

He disclosed that the Bill had already received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it will ultimately be passed into law.

He said that the passage of the Bill into law would help address peculiar security challenges of every state as every state better understands its own terrain more than strangers.

Later in the day, the Abia State House of Assembly voted in favour of the State Police Bill.

The Acting Clerk Abia State House of Assembly, Mr Promise confirmed this in an interview with Vanguard.

Speaking later with Vanguard, Deputy Speaker Nmeregini, said that the State Police Bill was passed by “unanimous vote.”

World.title: Tinubu backs local engineers to unlock gas pipeline capacity
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to unlocking Nigeria’s gas resources to power industries, improve electricity supply, create jobs and boost export earnings, backing indigenous engineering firms to play a greater role in major energy projects.

The President spoke against the backdrop of Lee Engineering Group’s construction of two compressor stations designed to enable the Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System (ELPS) to operate at its full capacity of 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day.

Tinubu made the remarks while receiving the Founder and Chairman of Lee Engineering Group, Chief Dr Leemon Ikpea, at the State House, Abuja.

He reaffirmed his administration’s Nigeria First policy and urged international oil companies operating in the country to provide more opportunities for competent Nigerian engineering and manufacturing firms to participate in major energy projects.

Lee Engineering is handling the engineering, procurement and construction of two midline compressor stations in Edo State.

Although the ELPS II expansion increased the pipeline’s designed capacity from 1.1 billion to 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day, the compressor stations are required to raise operating pressure and enable the system to deliver at its full capacity.

The project is expected to strengthen gas transportation to power plants and industries along the pipeline corridor, support increased supplies to neighbouring West African countries through the West African Gas Pipeline, and create opportunities for additional export earnings.

Tinubu said the Nigeria First policy must translate into more contracts for capable indigenous firms, greater use of locally manufactured equipment and the creation of skilled jobs for Nigerians.

He encouraged international oil companies to build stronger partnerships with Nigerian engineering companies that had demonstrated the capacity to deliver complex projects.

The President also highlighted his administration’s 2024 executive orders and presidential directives on local content compliance, contracting costs and approval timelines, describing them as measures to attract investment, reduce delays and expand opportunities for Nigerian businesses.

Ikpea commended the President’s Nigeria First policy, disclosing that Lee Engineering’s fabrication yard in Warri, Delta State, was manufacturing some components for the compressor stations.

He said the facility housed some of the industry’s most advanced fabrication equipment.

Ikpea added that Nigerian companies had invested significantly in modern equipment, technology and skilled personnel, enabling them to undertake complex engineering, procurement and construction projects previously handled by foreign contractors.

He said greater participation by indigenous firms would help retain more jobs, expertise and economic value within Nigeria.

World.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA
World.content:
— Petrol supply drops 20.6%

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries fell by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August, while petrol supply from domestic refineries also declined amid reduced imports.

The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday showed that average daily petrol receipts dropped by 23.4 per cent to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August.

The report attributed the decline to lower domestic supply and reduced imports following the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes.

Between January and September 2026, Nigerian refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude.

Domestic crude accounted for 80.4 per cent of total refinery intake during the period, while imported crude contributed 19.6 per cent.

The report also showed that Dangote Refinery operated at 105.98 per cent utilisation in September, processing approximately 689,000 barrels of crude oil per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day.

The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from the refinery’s inventory, indicating that it processed more crude than it received during the month.

On petrol supply, the NMDPRA data showed that domestic refineries supplied an average of 28.5 million litres per day in September, down 20.6 per cent from 35.9 million litres in August.

Petrol imports also declined by 30.1 per cent to 10.2 million litres per day from 14.6 million litres.

Despite the decline, domestic refineries remained the largest source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts in September, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports.

The September average of 38.7 million litres per day was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026.

Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres of petrol per day, representing 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent.

The NMDPRA reiterated that September’s decline in petrol receipts reflected a 21 per cent drop in domestic supply from August levels and a 30 per cent reduction in imports amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes.

World.title: Edo govt demolishes building allegedly used for organ harvesting, cultism
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

A house in Uwalor-Oke in Uromi, Esan North East Local Government Area of Edo State has been demolished for allegedly being used for cult activities and organ harvesting.

Besides the demolition, the suspected organ harvester Ebhata Eromosele was also arrested by the Edo State Special Security Squad codenamed Operation Flush out Kidnapping and Cultists, in collaboration with Edo State Security Corps, the Nigerian Police Force and other sister security agencies, supervised by the Principal Security Officer (PSO) to the governor.

The building was said to have been used for ritual activities where Eromosele was alleged to have harvested the organs of three young women, out of which one of the victims, a pregnant woman, died in the process; one who was hospitalised has been discharged while another is receiving treatment in an undisclosed hospital in Esan Central Senatorial District.

Another building located at Idi-Negbon Eguare Ewatto, allegedly used for cult-related activities, was also not spared as it was touched by bulldozers.

In a statement by Governor Monday Okpebholo’s Chief Press Secretary, Dr. Patrick Ebiojele, the coordinator of the Special Security Squad, Amiolemen Idemudia said criminals would be wiped out of Edo State.

He noted that Ebhata Eromosele engaged in ritual activities before nemesis caught up with him and have been arrested and today his building is demolished in Uromi.

He said, “A lifeless body killed and dumped was traced by Edo State Security Corps to this bungalow apartment used by the suspect.

“A search of this residence exposed the suspect as security operative saw bloodstained bedspread and other incriminating evidence indicating that Ebhata is into ritual activities and organ harvesting.”

Idemudia said the governor has warned that his administration will not tolerate crime of this nature and will make the state unsafe for criminal elements.

On the cult issue, Idemudia said there were cult fracas in Ewatto disturbing the peace of the community.

He said that one Bright Ejetuwamen was at the forefront of the fight, using his properties at Ewatto for cult-related activities. He said the property has been demolished.

“Governor Monday Okpebholo will not spare any hideout or properties used to perpetrate crime as it will be demolished. The cultist has been apprehended. All criminals must leave Edo State,” he said.

The Zonal Commander, Edo State Security Corps, SP Johnson Oyameda (rtd), said the success recorded in the arrest of the ritual suspect was as a result of over a month of surveillance.

“The body of a lady mutilated and dumped in a drainage was recovered while still alive. Not up to two weeks another body was recovered again and these incidents led to stepping up surveillance around the area and the surveillance paid off.

“Ebhata Eromosele murdered a lady and dumped the body but my men on surveillance saw him and trailed him to this apartment which has been demolished today,” he said.

Both the suspected ritualists and cultists have been arrested and are in the custody of the Edo State Police Command for further investigation and prosecution.

World.title: Many Northern states pass state police bill into law; others dither
World.content:
police badge

…Benue, Kebbi, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Zamfara, Yobe pass bill into law

…Borno, Katsina, Bauchi, Adamawa, Kano and Jigawa still brainstorming on bill

A crucial legislation which was initiated at the National Assembly to empower states to establish their police forces and use for maintaining security, which was sent to the state Houses of Assembly for adoption into state laws, has been given acceleration by many of the 19 northern states. Our correspondents find out that the bill has already been passed into law in Benue, Kebbi, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Zamfara and Yobe states. However, states such as Borno, Adamawa, Bauchi, Katsina, Kano and Bauchi are still brainstorming on the security legislation.

By Soni Daniel, Editor, Northern Region, Umar Yusuf (Yola), Peter Duru (Makurdi), Ndahi Marama (Maiduguri), Femi Bolaji (Jalingo), Haruna Aliyu (Birnin Kebbi), Golok Nanmwa (Jos),

Hadiza Yusuf (Kano), Edwin Phillips (Lafia), Idris Salisu (Gusau), Fauziyya Lawal (Katsina), Maryam Usman (Damaturu), Christopher Ameh (Bauchi), Muhammad Inuwa (Dutse),

Birnin Kebbi: The bill was received with joy once it got to the floor of the Kebbi State House of Assembly and it was deliberated upon and eventually passed into law that empowers the state to set up its own police.

The Kebbi State House of Assembly aligned with the position of the National Assembly and recommended the alteration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and for related matters.

This followed the presentation of the report of the House Committee on Home Affairs and Internal Security, led by Muhammad Garba Bena, during Wednesday’s plenary session, presided over by the Speaker of the Assembly, Salihu Maikasuwa Dangoje.

After the presentation of the report, the House proceeded to a vote, in which 20 out of the 24 members present at the sitting voted in favour of the establishment of State Police Services, while 4 members were officially absent.

Thereafter, the House, led by the Speaker, adopted the position of the National Assembly and recommended that the Bill for the Establishment of State Police Services (Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 Sixth Alteration Bill, 2026) be passed, having secured the required two-thirds majority from the Kebbi State House of Assembly, as stipulated by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).

The Plateau State House of Assembly has also adopted the position of the NASS and passed the state police bill into law without much delay.

The decision was taken during plenary on Tuesday presided over by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation of the committee’s report by its chairman, Prof. Theodore Bala Maiyaki, who represents Qua’an-Pan South Constituency.

Presenting the report, Maiyaki said, “The proposed constitutional amendment has become necessary in view of the security challenges facing the country, the manpower shortage in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen local policing arrangements.”

Following deliberations, the lawmakers adopted the committee’s recommendations and voted in support of the proposed constitutional amendment.

In Taraba, the state House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police, marking a major legislative step toward decentralizing security and reinforcing crime prevention across the state.

The bill, transmitted from the National Assembly as part of ongoing constitutional review processes, was formally laid before the lawmakers by the Majority Leader, Hon. Jethro Yakubu Zikengyu, and received by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. John Kizito Bonzena.

Following exhaustive deliberations on the floor of the House, members unanimously voted to adopt the legislative measure, signaling strong backing for localized security architectures to tackle emerging criminal challenges.

Speaking after the adoption, Speaker John Kizito Bonzena noted that establishing a state police system will drastically improve response times, foster closer intelligence sharing with federal security agencies, and create meaningful employment opportunities for youths.

Bonzena said: “The proposed state police framework will strengthen our institutional capacity to curb criminal activities, protect rural and urban communities, and guarantee public safety across Taraba State.”

In Zamfara State, the members of the state House of Assembly have passed the resolution supporting constitutional alterations aimed at facilitating the establishment of state police.

The Speaker of the Assembly Hon. Bilyaminu Ismail Moriki, disclosed that the establishment of state police would complement the efforts of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal in addressing insecurity in the state and in across the country.
