Moriko expressed optimism that the Zamfara State Government would provide the necessary framework and support required to ensure the effective operation of state Police if established.

“Our Governor Dauda Lawal Is committed to a peaceful Zamfara. That is why he assured of his total support to see this new development see the light of the day,” Moriki said

Lawmakers in the Nasarawa State House of Assembly have also adopted the position of the NASS and passed the bill as sent to them by the national Assembly to establish state police in the state.

The approval was given on Wednesday during plenary in Lafia, presided over by the Speaker, Dr. Danladi Jatau.

Jatau read the 26 clauses of the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly, before putting each clause to a voice vote.

The state lawmakers unanimously voted in favour of all the clauses, after which the Speaker declared that the bill as passed into law.

In a similar display of support for state police, the Yobe State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment establishing state police in Nigeria.

The Speaker of the Yobe State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Chiroma Buba Mashio confirmed this to Vanguard correspondent on Thursday.

Mashio signed the resolution on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.

Yobe’s approval adds the state to those supporting decentralised policing amid persistent security challenges across the country.

In the same vein, the Benue State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the establishment of state police in Nigeria, adopting a proposed constitutional amendment bill seeking to provide the legal framework for decentralised policing to tackle the country’s growing security challenges.

The decision was taken during plenary presided over by the Speaker, Mr. Alfred Emberga, following deliberations on the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026.

The Executive bill was presented for consideration by the House Majority Leader, Mr. Peter Ipusu, who urged lawmakers to give it accelerated consideration to ensure the legislative process was completed within the stipulated timeframe.

The proposed amendment seeks to establish a constitutional framework for the creation and operation of state police services alongside the Federal Police Service, with provisions addressing their responsibilities, funding and operational guidelines.

The House in a unanimous vote passed the constitutional amendment.

The Speaker in his ruling directed the Clerk to convey the resolution of the House to the National Assembly.

However, the bill is still facing deliberations in the Katsina State House of Assembly, after it took the first legislative step towards considering the proposed State Police Bill, following its receipt and passage through first reading.

The development marks the beginning of the Assembly’s consideration of the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police and decentralise Nigeria’s policing system amid persistent security challenges.

The same situation has played out at the Borno State House of Assembly, which is still deliberating on the state police bill after it received it from the NASS.

The Clerk of the Borno State House of Assembly, Shettima Garba, confirmed that the House leadership is yet to deliberate nor pass the Police Bill into law.

The clerk said however that had met and read out the bill at one of its plenary sessions.

According to him, the bill needs ample time to study its positive or negative impact to the citizenry.

In Jigawa State, the State House of Assembly has raised a committee to critically examine the constitutional amendments bill and make recommendations on how it reflects the interests of the people of Jigawa State.

‎The Speaker of Jigawa State House of Assembly, Haruna Dangyatim, said the Assembly had already received the bill and would work on it within the stipulated timeline.

‎Dangyatim said: “‎We have received the Constitution Amendment Bill from the National Assembly, and I want to assure you that we will do the needful before the deadline given to all state assemblies which is the end of this month.

‎“Within the stipulated timeline contained in the letter of the bill, we are given 30 days to complete the legislative work on the bill from the date we received the letter,” he stated.

‎The Speaker assured that the House would give the bill accelerated attention, saying that they were studying the document thoroughly to ensure that their position aligns with the aspirations of the people.

‎In Kano, the State House of Assembly has conducted the first reading of the proposed State Police Bill and distributed copies of the draft legislation to members for further study.

The Chief Press Secretary and spokesperson of the Assembly, Kamal Sani Shawai, disclosed this to Vanguard on Thursday while explaining the status of the proposed bill.

Shawai said copies of the draft had been given to lawmakers to enable them to study its provisions before the House reconvenes to deliberate on it.

He said the Assembly would take further action on the bill after members had familiarised themselves with its contents.

But in Adamawa, the assemblymen are yet to deliberate and take a position on the state police bill.

The Chairman of the House Committee on Information, Hon Musa Kalam, however said that they members would soon meet to take action on the bill.

A similar situation is playing out at the Bauchi State House of Assembly, which is yet to conclude consideration of the proposed State Police bill, despite the expiration of the two-week deadline given to an ad-hoc committee set up to examine the proposal.

The Speaker of the House, Abubakar Y. Suleiman, had constituted the committee, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Jamilu Ummaru Dahiru, to deliberate on the bill and report back to the whole house.

However, two weeks after the committee was given the deadline to complete its assignment, the House is yet to announce the outcome of its deliberations or the passage of the bill.

The delay leaves the proposed establishment of State Police in Bauchi State pending, amid growing calls for stronger security measures to tackle insecurity across the country.

World.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
World.content:
Javier Tebas

By Adegboyega Adeleye

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation.

According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum.

The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials.

Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister.

Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president.

However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters.

In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum.

Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension.

The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel.

In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity.

“Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility.

He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules.

The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport.

The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced.

World.title: DSS Secures Seventh Death Sentence As Adamawa Court Convicts 3 Persons for Kidnapping Catholic Priests
World.content:
A high Court of Adamawa State, on Thursday, sentenced to death three persons who kidnapped two Catholic priests in February 2025.

Delivering judgement, Justice Christopher Mapeo found the three men guilty of criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harboring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the release of

Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman.

The judge sentenced the three men, Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf, to death for kidnapping, armed robbery and other offences.

Thursday’s death sentence is the seventh secured by the DSS this year. On 20th May, 2026, Ekiti High Court sentenced two men, Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death by hanging for kidnapping.

About two weeks later, on 3rd June, 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced to death by hanging, four men who, in June 2022, massacred scores of worshippers at the St. Francis Catholic church, Owo, Ondo State.

The convicts are Idris Abdulmalik Omeiza, Alqasim Idris, Jamiu Abdulmalik and Abdulkareem Idris.

Less than two weeks later, on 15th June, 2026, a Katsina High Court sentenced a female arms courier, Hauwa’u Mukhtar, to death by hanging.

The following day, on 16th June, 2026, a Kogi High Court sentenced Jibrin Halilu to death by hanging for kidnapping and murdering his neighbour in Obajana, an industrial town in the state.

About a week after the Kogi sentencing, on 22nd June, 2026, a Sokoto High court sentenced three persons Muhammed Yusuf Sallau, Jabbi Ahlaji Yale and Kabiru Muhammed, to death by hanging, for terrorism and for transporting arms.

Less than three months later, on

28th September 2026, a Sokoto High Court sentenced Ibrahim Usman aka Dan Iyali to death by hanging over his involvement in the killing of three kidnapped persons in the state.

World.title: NEC Approves 90-Day Action Plan To Ease Cost of Living For Nigerians
World.content:
* Shettima charges 36 govs to translate reforms into improved living conditions

* Tasks them on jobs, affordable transportation, healthcare, others



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The National Economic Council (NEC) on Thursday rose from its monthly meeting and endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms.

The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.

NEC’s endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, during its 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

This is just as the vice-president said while President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.

The council also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting of how proceeds from fuel subsidy removal are being utilised.

Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about the progress recorded under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery.

He identified the reduction of headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions.

The finance minister’s presentation placed particular emphasis on translating macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment.

Addressing NEC members, Shettima charged state governors and relevant government institutions to ensure that the gains of the administration’s economic reforms translate into affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security for Nigerians.

He said the success of economic policies must ultimately be measured by their impact on citizens’ daily lives, stressing that the responsibility of government extends beyond announcing reforms to building institutions that enable Nigerians to plan their futures with confidence.

“The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said.

According to him, the council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform and livestock development represent critical decisions about the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress.

“Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” Shettima said, emphasising that Nigeria’s federal structure must strengthen cooperation rather than become an obstacle to the delivery of essential services.

On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the vice-president underscored the need for state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would reduce the financial burden on commuters.

He maintained that the success of the programme should be determined by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed.

“The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said.

Shettima maintained that President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, noting that governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions.

“President Bola Tinubu has made economic reform the instrument of a larger national ambition. Our contribution must give that ambition social depth and productive strength.”

He urged governors to bring their understanding of local realities into national policy decisions, insisting that effective implementation requires clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government.

“Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said.

The vice-president challenged members of the council to judge every policy proposal by its capacity to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

“Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” Shettima said.

NEC also received an update on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, who allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring members that Nigeria possesses the institutional capacity to contain the situation.

The minister briefed council on efforts by the ministry, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, to operationalise a robust national response system.

He identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and effective strategic communication as critical components of the response.

Pate acknowledged the efforts of 21 state government that had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms.

Council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by the Governor of Gombe State, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, and resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity.

The council emphasised the need for timely release of counterpart funds, strengthened routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to ensure better coverage in subsequent campaigns.

It further stressed that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to achieving the complete eradication of polio in Nigeria.

On livestock development, NEC received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by the Governor of Kebbi State, Comrade Nasir Idris, and acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country.

Council noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the Federal Government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between the Federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential.

Also, NEC received a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, and resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the Federal and state governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country.

Council specifically directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles.

It further resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings arising from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares.

To give effect to the decision, council agreed to constitute a committee to coordinate the proposed financing arrangement, engage relevant stakeholders and develop practical measures to ensure that the economic benefits of the programme translate into affordable, accessible and sustainable transportation for Nigerians.

World.title: Court Orders Speedy Trial of 3 Suspected Kidnappers of NYSC Members, Suspects to Remain in DSS Custody
World.content:
A high Court of Imo State, on Thursday, ordered the speedy trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day.

The court set aside four days, starting from 27th October, to the 30th of the month for continuation of the trial,

urging prosecution and defence counsel to cooperate with the court to ensure judgment is delivered before January 2027.

Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, made the appeal during proceedings in the cases involving three defendants accused of abducting prospective NYSC members and two others facing charges over a separate kidnapping case.

During the hearing, an officer of the Department of State Services (DSS), Ikem Emmanuel, testified on the investigation that led to the arrest of the three defendants in the NYSC-related case.

He told the court that the investigation involved intelligence gathering, data analysis, record checks, interviews and statements obtained from the defendants, victims and witnesses.

He stated that an identification parade was conducted, during which victims and witnesses identified the defendants as members of the criminal gang that kidnapped them.

The officer further told the court that one of the defendants, Usman Aliyu, admitted in his statement to participating in the operation and allegedly disclosed that 11 persons were involved.

The investigator maintained that the defendants’ statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers.

In a related proceeding involving two other defendants, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their statements were taken in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers.

Following the proceedings, Justice Orafu adjourned the cases to October 27, 28, 29 and 30 for continuation of hearing, and ordered that the five defendants remain in the custody of the DSS.

World.title: Ebola: FG Directs Information Agencies to Intensify Enlightenment
World.content:
The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, has directed agencies under his ministry to intensify public education on Ebola Virus Disease (EVD).

According to a statement issued by the minister’s Media Aide, Rabiu Ibrahim, the agencies include the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN).

Others are the Voice of Nigeria (VON) and the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) had confirmed a case of Ebola involving a woman who recently travelled to Abuja from Uganda.

The woman is in isolation and receiving treatment, while health authorities have identified her contacts and are monitoring them.

The minister said: “The Federal Government is taking every necessary step to contain this case and protect Nigerians. Accurate and timely information is one of our strongest defences.

“Our agencies must reach every community, in every language, with clear facts on how Ebola spreads, how to protect ourselves and where to report suspected cases.”

Idris directed the agencies to collaborate with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to ensure all public information is verified and evidence-based.

He also tasked the NOA with deploying its nationwide offices for grassroots sensitisation, in collaboration with traditional and religious leaders, community groups and the media.

The minister urged Nigerians to remain calm, rely on official information and avoid spreading unverified claims on social media.

He advised members of the public to report suspected cases immediately by calling the NCDC’s toll-free, 24-hour emergency line on 6232. (NAN)

World.title: Federal Agencies CEOs Mobilise 100,000 Supporters For Tinubu’s Campaign Kick-off Saturday
World.content:
* Projects 1.2m jobs from local value-addition policy, defends economic reforms



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Forum of Chief Executive Officers of Federal Government Parastatals (FORCEPA) has hinted that it has mobilised over 100,000 supporters to storm the Kaduna venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign kick-off on Saturday, reaffirming its support for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s in January 2027.

The forum, made up of over 500 chief executives of federal agencies and parastatals, also pledged to mobilise 10 million votes for Tinubu and Shettima, citing the need for policy continuity and consolidation of the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

Speaking at a news conference in Abuja, its chairman, Dr Kazeem Kolawole Raji, who was joined by other officers of the forum, said members had been deployed in Kaduna to coordinate mobilisation and engage stakeholders ahead of the campaign event.

According to him, “We have decided, as a group comprising over 500 CEOs across the country, to lend our support to the re-election of Mr President. In view of this, we have decided to mobilise over 100,000 supporters for the presidential campaign kick-off in Kaduna on Saturday.”

Declaring that the Tinubu administration deserved a second term, he said the forum was established to harness the institutional experience and networks of federal agency chiefs to promote public awareness of government policies and programmes.

FORCEPA particularly defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, including petrol subsidy removal, describing them as difficult but necessary measures to strengthen public finances, attract investment and support long-term growth.

The forum, however, acknowledged the hardship facing households and businesses, saying the success of the reforms would depend on their ability to deliver jobs, higher incomes and improved living standards.

“The next phase of national transformation should consolidate progress, address implementation challenges and translate economic stabilisation into more tangible improvement in the lives of ordinary Nigerians,” Raji said.

The forum also projected that a proposed policy requiring local value addition to raw materials before export could generate at least 1.2 million jobs within one to two years of implementation.

Raji said the policy framework envisaged at least 30 per cent value addition before raw materials could be exported, adding that the proposal had undergone executive and legislative processes, including reviews by the Ministry of Justice and the National Assembly.

He said local processing of commodities such as cocoa would expand manufacturing, reduce reliance on imported finished goods and ease pressure on foreign exchange demand.

The 1.2 million jobs figure, however, is a projection of the policy’s potential impact, not an established outcome.

The agency chiefs also cited entrepreneurship support, student loans and innovation programmes as evidence of efforts to expand economic opportunities.

One official said his agency, which operates in 58 locations nationwide, had supported more than 100,000 entrepreneurs since its establishment in 1993.

He added that nearly 300 young Nigerian innovators had travelled to London to present their ideas to international investors, with the government reportedly covering their travel, accommodation and feeding expenses.

On the rising cost of living and building materials, the officials acknowledged persistent pressures on households but argued that increased domestic production could reduce import dependence and exposure to exchange-rate fluctuations.

They cited cement manufacturing as an example of how local production could strengthen the economy and reduce reliance on imports.

The officials also said savings from petrol subsidy removal had created room for interventions such as student loans and conditional cash transfers, while urging journalists to scrutinise the deployment of the funds and assess the impact of the reforms.

They pointed to improvements in foreign reserves and relative stability in the naira as signs of progress but admitted that the benefits had yet to provide sufficient relief for many Nigerians.

Arguing that structural economic challenges required sustained policy implementation, the officials cited Lagos State’s development experience as an example of the potential benefits of long-term planning and continuity.

FORCEPA said its platform would strengthen coordination among federal agencies, improve public understanding of government programmes and promote accountability.

It added that the ultimate measure of the administration’s policies would be their impact on employment, household incomes, industrial growth and citizens’ welfare.

Raji urged members and supporters to remain united, disciplined and peaceful during the electioneering, describing the planned Kaduna mobilisation as a demonstration of the forum’s support for Tinubu’s second-term bid.

“One good term deserves another. Continuity for consolidation, leadership for transformation, renewal for a greater Nigeria,” the forum added.

World.title: CBN Takes Steps to Strengthen Nigeria-China Financial Corridor
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has convened a high-level business and financial roundtable in China to explore opportunities to deepen Nigeria’s financial markets.

According to a statement from the Corporate Communications Department of the CBN, the meeting held in Beijing on Wednesday, brought together Nigerian and Chinese business leaders.

The statement said that the engagement, with the theme, ‘Strengthening the Nigeria–China Financial Corridor,’ also aimed to identify practical barriers to stronger financial flows between the two economies.

“It provided a platform for businesses operating across both markets to share firsthand experiences and discuss how financial connectivity, banking relationships and investment channels could be strengthened,” it said.

Meanwhile, the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, emphasised the importance of engaging directly with businesses to understand the opportunities and constraints affecting financial activity between Nigeria and China.

Cardoso underscored the importance of translating stakeholder engagement into a clearer understanding of the financial and institutional issues requiring attention.

He said particular attention would be paid to opportunities that could inform efforts to develop deeper, more accessible financial markets.

Deputy Governor for Economic Policy at the CBN, Philip Ikeazor, in his opening remarks, set out the objectives of the engagement.

Ikeazor said that it was important to translate stronger macroeconomic fundamentals into increased investment and more developed financial markets.

The Nigerian Ambassador to the People’s Republic of China, Lt.-Gen. Abdulrahman Dambazau (rtd), also addressed participants.

Other speakers included Chairperson of Blue Diamond Group, Festus Mbisiogu, and Chairperson of CIG Motors, Chief Diana Chen, who brought perspectives from businesses operating across the Nigeria–China corridor.

At the heart of the engagement was an interactive session in which participants discussed opportunities for greater financial activity and the practical challenges encountered in conducting transactions between the two countries.

Issues raised included the need for more efficient cross-border payment arrangements, stronger banking connectivity, and the potential benefits of a larger Nigerian banking presence in China.

These were considered alongside broader opportunities to facilitate financial flows and to improve access to financial services and investment opportunities in Nigeria.

The engagement also featured a presentation on Nigeria’s economic reform progress, improved macroeconomic fundamentals, and emerging investment opportunities in the country’s financial markets.

The insights gathered are expected to inform the CBN’s continued engagement with relevant financial institutions and regulatory counterparts, focusing on practical areas for cooperation within its mandate.

The Beijing roundtable is part of the CBN’s broader strategy to deepen Nigeria’s financial relationships across Asia.

Following engagements in Singapore and at the IMF/World Bank Annual meetings in Bangkok, the apex bank’s China programme includes bilateral discussions with the People’s Bank of China.

It also includes engagement with the leadership of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), and meetings with Nigerian and Chinese businesses.

The programme will also extend to Guangzhou, where the CBN will hold a listening session with the Nigerian business community.

This is to better understand financial challenges and explore opportunities to strengthen remittance channels and facilitate investment in Nigeria. (NAN)

World.title: Senate Probes Varsity Governing Councils, Seeks NUC Reform
World.content:
*Moves to check alleged illegal management structures in public, private institutions

*Backs research fund with 20% of Nigerian Content Fund

*Warns FG over Aiyetoro’s destruction by ocean surges

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Thursday moved to investigate the governing structures of public and private universities across Nigeria over alleged violations of statutory requirements, as it intensified efforts to strengthen regulatory oversight, improve research funding and protect vulnerable coastal communities from environmental devastation.

The upper chamber resolved to constitute an ad hoc committee to investigate Tansian University, Umunya, Anambra State, and other tertiary institutions following allegations that some universities had adopted management structures inconsistent with established governance regulations.

The decision followed a motion by Senator Victor Umeh (Anambra Central), who raised concerns about the alleged operation of corporate-style management structures, including managing directors and executive directors, in some private universities.

The development came during consideration of the National Universities Commission Act, 2026 (SB. 1056), sponsored by Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, which seeks to strengthen the regulatory authority of the National Universities Commission (NUC) over the establishment, administration, monitoring and management of universities and other degree-awarding institutions.

Umeh alleged that Tansian University had failed to comply with existing regulatory provisions despite sanctions imposed by the NUC.

According to him, rather than operate a board of trustees as required, the institution was allegedly headed by an executive director who exercised powers to appoint and dismiss vice-chancellors at will.

He argued that such practices undermined established university governance standards and weakened the commission’s capacity to enforce compliance.

Responding, Senate President Godswill Akpabio called for a comprehensive investigation to establish whether the university and other institutions had violated applicable laws.

“This consideration of the bill does not preclude our committees on Basic and Tertiary Education from bringing to the Senate the university so named for necessary action,” he said.

Akpabio specifically called for an ad hoc committee to “investigate where it got its powers from to have directors”.

He warned against allowing alleged regulatory breaches to persist until the proposed legislation came into force.

“Even before the law takes effect, we must bring erring private and public universities to order so that we don’t end up degrading the standards of education this country,” the Senate President said.

He further warned that weaknesses in university administration could undermine public confidence in Nigerian academic qualifications and the credibility of certificates awarded by the institutions.

The proposed legislation seeks to modernise the legal framework for university regulation, strengthen accreditation and enforcement mechanisms, improve institutional governance and update the composition and functions of the NUC governing board.

Presenting the bill on behalf of Bamidele, Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno said the existing law required an overhaul to reflect the expansion of private universities, technological advancement, globalisation and changing national development priorities.

The bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, which was given four weeks to report back.

In a related development, the Senate passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund, with a proposed annual allocation of 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund.

Sponsored by Bamidele and presented by Monguno, the proposed legislation seeks to bridge funding and coordination gaps in research, support indigenous technology and facilitate the commercialisation of locally developed inventions.

Monguno said Nigeria possessed the universities, polytechnics, research institutes and technology entrepreneurs needed to drive innovation but lacked a sustainable framework to coordinate research activities and translate discoveries into commercially viable products.

“The importance of research and innovation to national development cannot be overemphasised. In a rapidly evolving global economy driven by science, technology, industrial advancement and the application of knowledge, the capacity of a nation to generate ideas, develop indigenous technologies and translate research findings into practical solutions is critical to its economic competitiveness and prosperity,” he said.

He added that the proposed fund would ensure that research extended beyond academic publications and laboratory experiments.

“It recognises that research should not remain confined to academic publications or institutional laboratories, but should be translated, where viable, into goods, services, technologies and practical solutions capable of improving the lives of Nigerians,” Monguno said.

Under the bill, the fund would receive 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund annually, alongside government appropriations, grants, donations, investment income and proceeds from patents and commercialisation.

Its resources would support research grants, infrastructure, product development, indigenous technology, intellectual property protection and technology transfer. Administrative expenditure would be capped at 25 per cent of the annual contribution from the Nigerian Content Development Fund.

Contributing, Senator Samson Ekong lamented the country’s neglect of research and innovation.

“Research and innovation, we would have gone far in this country if we had taken these two aspects of education seriously,” he said.

He asked: “How do we catch up when we ignore research, when we ignore innovation?”

The bill was also referred to the Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund for consideration and a report within four weeks.

Meanwhile, the Senate has urged the Federal Government to urgently intervene to prevent further destruction of Aiyetoro community in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State by Atlantic Ocean surges.

The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Senator Dayo Faduyile, who raised concerns over the destruction of homes, schools, healthcare facilities and other public infrastructure.

Lawmakers noted reports indicating that approximately 80 per cent of buildings in the coastal community had been lost to sea incursion, threatening residents’ livelihoods, cultural heritage and continued habitation.

The Senate called on the Federal Ministry of Environment, the Niger Delta Development Commission, the Ondo State Government and the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission to collaborate on a comprehensive shoreline protection programme.

It also demanded a transparent review of previous and ongoing shoreline protection contracts to establish their funding, implementation status, outstanding obligations and completion timelines.

The chamber further urged the National Emergency Management Agency and relevant state authorities to provide the affected residents with safe water, healthcare assistance and temporary shelter.

Amending the motion’s prayers, Ekong called for the inclusion of affected communities in Akwa Ibom South in the proposed federal intervention.

Supporting the amendment, Akpabio stressed the need for a broader national approach to shoreline protection.

“Some of these things are above the resources of the state, and that is why these issues are being brought here to the Senate,” he said.

The Senate mandated its Committees on Environment, Niger Delta Development Commission and Special Duties to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks.

The Committee on Legislative Compliance was also directed to monitor adherence to the resolutions.

World.title: Atiku Demands Publication of 103m Voters’ Register Ahead of 2027 Election
World.content:
Former Vice President and ADC Presidential Candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has demanded the immediate publication of the preliminary voters’ register by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), questioning the credibility of the electoral body’s preparations for the 2027 general election.

Atiku alleged that the register was unavailable on INEC’s online portal during the announced public scrutiny period of October 9 to 15, despite the commission’s announcement that Nigeria had more than 103 million registered voters.

In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said the failure to make the register accessible raised concerns about transparency and voters’ ability to identify errors.

“INEC has announced more than 103 million registered voters. Nigerians went to its portal to inspect the names and found an empty page. That is an outrage. A figure cannot answer an objection. A press announcement cannot tell a voter whether her name has been omitted. Show Nigerians the register,” he said.

Atiku cited Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act 2026, which he said requires the voters’ register to be displayed at registration areas and online for public scrutiny.

He also questioned what he described as conflicting statements about the display of the register, alleging that INEC’s chairman reportedly said on October 5 that the exercise had already been completed, while the public was subsequently informed that it would take place from October 9 to 15.

“Which statement is true? Where was the register published? For seven full days, or for no days at all? INEC must produce the dates, the links and the records of access,” he said.

The former vice president also raised concerns about Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which he said permits a returning officer to count a ballot paper without INEC’s official mark if satisfied that it came from a book supplied to the polling unit.

He questioned the safeguards for verifying the origin of such ballot papers and preventing electoral fraud.

“Nigerians cannot be denied access to the voters’ register before election day and then be asked to accept unmarked ballot papers after voting. INEC must set out enforceable safeguards against counterfeit ballots, and the National Assembly must close any loophole that leaves the authenticity of a vote to an officer’s unsupported assurance,” Atiku said.

The statement also accused INEC of failing to respond to inquiries about the identities of companies awarded contracts to print sensitive election materials.

Atiku maintained that the ADC and its presidential candidate had the right to demand transparency from the electoral commission over the procedures that would guide the 2027 presidential election.

Addressing President Bola Tinubu directly, the former vice-president linked the controversy to the economic and security challenges facing Nigerians.

“You will not add an unseen voters’ register to their suffering and call it a route to another four years in office,” he said.

Atiku further alleged that INEC’s conduct had created opportunities for manipulation by preventing voters from checking additions, removals and omissions from the register.

He called on the commission to publish the register by local government, area council and ward, explain the conflicting dates and provide voters with the opportunity to challenge false entries and restore omitted names.

“Anything less is an assault on the credibility of the 2027 election,” he said.

The former vice president also urged Nigeria’s international partners, election observers and democratic institutions to pressure INEC to comply with the law before election day.

“I call on Nigeria’s international partners, election observers and democratic institutions to press INEC publicly to comply with the law. Do not wait until election day to ask whether this contest is credible. Demand access to the voters’ register now. Ask how every ballot paper will be authenticated. Transparency before the vote is as essential as scrutiny of the results afterward,” he said.

He said by insisting that access to the voters’ register was fundamental to protecting citizens’ voting rights.

“The right to vote begins with the right to know that your name is on the list. INEC must stop hiding behind a blank screen. Publish the register. Open it to scrutiny. Answer the country,” Atiku said.

World.title: Suliman Carrim hit with fresh charges in vehicle theft case
World.content:
Businessman Suliman Carrim faces fresh criminal charges linked to the alleged attempted theft of two vehicles and the use of fraudulent bank documents. His case returns to court on 30 October 2026. Image: X

North West businessman Suliman Carrim faces fresh criminal charges linked to the alleged attempted theft of two vehicles belonging to Absa.

Carrim appeared in the Musina Magistrate’s Court in Limpopo on Thursday, 22 October, in connection with allegations involving fraudulent bank documents and an attempt to move vehicles across the border.

The case was postponed to 30 October for a bail application.



The latest development adds to Carrim’s legal troubles as he awaits a separate bail ruling over his alleged failure to appear before the Madlanga Commission.

CARRIM LINKED TO ALLEGED VEHICLE THEFT

According to police, the latest charges stem from an incident at the Beitbridge border post on 22 July 2026.

Officers intercepted two vehicles that were allegedly being transported from Mahikeng in the North West to Malawi.



Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said investigators established that arrangements had allegedly been made to obtain bank authorisation documents for the vehicles to leave South Africa.

However, the required authorisation was allegedly not provided.

Investigators believe fraudulent bank documents were subsequently arranged to facilitate the vehicles’ movement across the border.



The vehicles were still under finance and were returned to the bank.

Two suspects were initially arrested in connection with the incident.

The Commission’s Recommendations Task Team added Carrim as an accused in the two cases on Wednesday, 21 October.



The National Prosecuting Authority alleges that Carrim acted with others in an attempt to remove the vehicles from South Africa using fraudulent documentation.

The allegations remain before the courts.

MADLANGA COMMISSION CASE CONTINUES

Carrim’s latest court appearance follows his arrest at OR Tambo International Airport earlier this month.



He was arrested while preparing to travel abroad after allegedly failing to return to the Madlanga Commission despite being directed to appear.

He appeared in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court, where the State opposed his release on bail.

Prosecutors argued that he posed a flight risk.

Carrim’s legal representatives disputed this and maintained that he intended to return to South Africa.



The Pretoria court postponed its bail ruling to 28 October.

Carrim remains in custody and is expected back in the Musina Magistrate’s Court on 30 October in connection with the vehicle case.

World.title: Bank account costs: How South Africa compares with Botswana
World.content:
Bank customers in South Africa and Botswana face different charges for maintaining transactional accounts, with monthly fees and everyday transaction costs varying between banks.

The differences highlight why consumers need to consider more than just the advertised monthly fee when choosing where to bank.

How much do South African Bank customers pay?

According to its official 2026 pricing guide, Capitec charges customers R7.50 per month to maintain its main account. The fees took effect on 1 March 2026.



The bank also charges R2 for payments to other South African banks, R1 for payments to other Capitec customers and R3 for debit orders.

Customers who withdraw cash at another bank’s ATM pay R10 for every R1 000 withdrawn, according to Capitec’s published tariffs.

Meanwhile, First National Bank (FNB) offers an Easy Zero account with no monthly account fee. However, customers may still incur charges when conducting transactions.

FNB publishes separate pricing guides for its various accounts, meaning customers need to check the charges applicable to their chosen product.

What do Botswana bank customers pay?

In Botswana, Botswana Savings Bank (BSB) lists a monthly maintenance fee of P60 for its transactional account.

The account is designed for working people, young customers, pensioners and self-employed individuals. According to the bank’s official website, customers can deposit and withdraw money at BSB branches and ATMs.



Opening the account costs P100, while its listed features include free monthly statements, transaction notifications and transfers between BSB accounts.

BSB also offers an ordinary savings account with a lower monthly maintenance fee of P12. However, this is a different product, with withdrawal conditions that distinguish it from a standard transactional account.

The bank lists a P3.30 fee for withdrawals at its ATMs and charges P25 for subsequent over-the-counter withdrawals after the first free withdrawal.

Why the fees matter

The published tariffs show that banking costs depend on the account customers choose and how frequently they transact.

In South Africa, Capitec’s R7.50 monthly fee provides a clear baseline, while FNB’s Easy Zero account demonstrates that some products have no monthly maintenance charge.

In Botswana, BSB’s P60 transactional account fee is higher than its P12 ordinary savings account fee, but the two products offer different facilities and conditions.

Customers comparing banking costs across the two countries should therefore consider monthly maintenance, ATM withdrawals, electronic payments and other charges together.

The figures are based on the banks’ published tariffs and should be checked against the latest pricing guides before opening an account.

World.title: Mandla Ncikazi finds new home after Orlando Pirates departure
World.content:
Lamontville Golden Arrows have welcomed Mandla Ncikazi back to the club as their new head coach following his departure from Orlando Pirates.

The 57-year-old left the Buccaneers on Thursday, with Arrows announcing his return shortly afterwards. The club described him as a “proud son of the club” with a deep understanding of its traditions.

Ncikazi previously coached Golden Arrows during the 2020/21 season, guiding them to a club-record fourth-place finish in the PSL before joining Orlando Pirates as an assistant coach.



During his five-year spell at Pirates, Ncikazi contributed to the club’s success, helping the Soweto giants win nine trophies.

His return to Arrows follows discussions with the Pirates management on Thursday morning, during which he expressed his desire to pursue an opportunity to lead a team again. The club subsequently gave him its blessing to take up the new challenge.

Ncikazi leaves Pirates for Arrows

“Mandla leaves with our gratitude and our blessing. His contribution to Orlando Pirates has been evident throughout his time with us. We respect his wish to pursue this new opportunity and wish him success as he takes on a new responsibility,” said Pirates chairman Dr Irvin Khoza.



Ncikazi returns to a familiar environment, bringing valuable experience gained during his time at Pirates. His appointment will give Arrows an experienced coach as they look to build on their previous achievements.

Meanwhile, several Orlando Pirates supporters have wished the 57-year-old well following his departure.

Some fans have highlighted his contribution during the early stages of the Buccaneers’ success in the 2020s, acknowledging the role he played during his time at the club.

World.title: Fake kidnapping: R40k ransom plot backfires
World.content:
A woman accused of staging her own kidnapping in a R40 000 ransom plot appeared in the Kwa-Thema Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 22 October 2026. Image: X

A Gauteng woman accused of staging her own kidnapping to demand R40 000 from her family has appeared in court, with prosecutors revealing how the alleged scheme unravelled.

Ntombifuthi Mavis Rumo, 37, appeared in the Kwa-Thema Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, 22 October.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) alleges that Rumo conspired with two other people to fake her abduction after experiencing financial difficulties.



The case has been postponed to 29 October.

GAUTENG WOMAN ACCUSED OF FAKING KIDNAPPING

According to the NPA, Rumo allegedly met Bonginkosi Mndebele, 27, and another person on 7 October to discuss their financial problems.

Prosecutors allege that the three decided to stage her kidnapping and demand money from her family.

Her relatives subsequently received a ransom demand of R40 000.

However, the alleged plan ran into trouble when the family could not afford to pay.

The NPA said Rumo was dropped off along Vlakfontein Road on 12 October, with relatives instructed to collect her.



Police initially investigated the matter as a kidnapping.

However, the investigation later shifted towards an alleged staged abduction.

HUSBAND TAKES WIFE TO POLICE

The court heard that Rumo’s husband brought her to the police on 20 October.

During the investigation, she allegedly identified Mndebele as one of the people involved.

Police subsequently arrested the two suspects.

Rumo and Mndebele face charges of defeating the administration of justice.

A third alleged participant has not been charged.

Mndebele did not appear alongside Rumo on Thursday because he was in hospital.

STATE TO OPPOSE BAIL

The Kwa-Thema Magistrates’ Court postponed the case to 29 October for bail investigations and Mndebele’s appearance.

The State intends to oppose bail for both accused.

The court proceedings mark a major turn in a case that initially sparked concern for Rumo’s safety after her family reported her missing and received a ransom demand.

World.title: You can buy a holiday home in these coastal towns for R4 000 a month
World.content:
Owning a holiday home doesn’t have to be expensive.

South Africa’s vast coastline means there are dozens of opportunities to find or build an affordable holiday home.

5 Coastal towns with R300 000 holiday homes

These are your options for an affordable move-in-ready coastal home. Most are on KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast, where the water’s warm year-round and there’s ample local tourism to keep the property occupied.



Scottburgh

Among the 178 sales this year in Scottburgh, the average sale price is R1.2 million.

But in Scottburgh Central, buyers can acquire a 1-bedroom flat with partial sea views for R300 000.

Without a deposit, the bond should be roughly R3 000 a month on this property. Levies in this block are R995, and rates and taxes start at R400.

Elsewhere in Scottburgh, buyers can purchase a 3-bedroom townhouse for R550 000.

The area periodically lists some very affordable homes.

Port Edward

In Port Edward, buyers can purchase a studio apartment for R400 000 in the Edwardian Hotel.



The apartment sleeps 2 adults and 2 children under 16.

The property includes amenities like a pool and restaurant.

Rates and taxes are R650, and levies are R1 134.

The nightly rate in peak season starts at R960.

Ramsgate

In Ramsgate, buyers can get a generously sized flat 100 metres from the beach.

One listing on Private Property is for a fully furnished 1-bedroom, 78-square-metre flat on Marine Drive within walking distance to Lawrence Rocks.

The bond on the property should be roughly R4 000 a month, while rates and taxes are R600.

Other flats in the building rent for R600 a night.

Bathurst

The only town on this list that’s not on the South Coast, Bathurst is a 20-minute drive to Port Alfred.

The average sale price in Bathurst is R690 000, but for R399 000, a buyer can get a 1-bedroom cottage on a quarter-acre plot. The property allows buyers a place to stay while they build their dream house.

Rates and taxes on the property are R235. In total, a buyer can expect to spend R4 219 on the home.

Margate

In Margate, buyers can get a 24-square-metre studio apartment starting at R335 000.

For this price, buyers can expect to spend R3 400 a month on a bond.

Other listings in Margate include a 2-bedroom flat 300 metres from the beach, which is listed for R450 000. Rates on this seaside flat are R500 and levies are R600.

Questions to ask before buying a holiday home

It can be tempting to buy a home thinking of all the good times you’ll have, or all the money it could make.

But just because a holiday home is cheap doesn’t mean it is affordable.

What’s the maintenance on a property?

The best holiday home costs almost nothing to maintain. Flats and townhouses are the best option. You won’t need to pay to maintain a garden or roof.

These are typically common areas you pay to maintain through your levies.

Is there any interest in the area?

If you decide to sell, there should be enough interest in the area that offloading it is easy. If the town isn’t developed or has less than desirable service delivery, selling the property could become a hassle.

What does it cost to own all-in?

Besides the bond, rates and levies should be your number one concern. Also consider insurance and home maintenance. If you want to rent it to others, consider what it will cost to have someone manage the property.

Will it be a reliable income source?

If you’re thinking of turning the place into a short-term rental, there must be enough demand year-round. If you want to use it as a holiday home for your family, you may miss out on peak season rates.

Then consider whether the body corporate or municipality allows short-term lets.

Can you only afford it if it is generating income?

The best holiday home is one you can afford to own even when it’s not to let. Rental income is never guaranteed.

Before buying, consider how long you could keep paying to maintain the property if it stops generating income.

World.title: DJ Warras murder: ‘Trial delayed long enough,’ says judge
World.content:
The murder case of DJ Warras (left), involving accused Victor Majola (centre) and Hlengiwe Buthelezi (right), has been postponed again following delays over legal representation. Images: X

The murder case of popular radio personality Warrick “DJ Warras” Stock has suffered another setback, with a Johannesburg judge expressing frustration over repeated delays.

Two accused, Victor Mthethwa Majola and his girlfriend Hlengiwe Goodness Buthelezi, appeared in the Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg on Thursday, 22 October.

However, outstanding issues surrounding their legal representation once again prevented pre-trial proceedings from moving forward.



Judge William Karam postponed the matter to 2 November.

DJ WARRAS MURDER CASE HITS ANOTHER DELAY

Both accused approached Legal Aid South Africa after experiencing difficulties securing private legal representation.

The court heard that Legal Aid had received the case docket, including electronic evidence, from their previous attorneys.

However, concerns about a possible conflict of interest between the accused complicated arrangements for their defence.

Legal Aid is now considering appointing private practitioners to represent them.

Karam made it clear that the delays could not continue indefinitely.



“This matter has been delayed long enough, with respect,” the judge said.

The prosecution also raised concerns about the lack of progress.

The State indicated that it was ready to set a trial date but had been unable to make meaningful progress with pre-trial proceedings for several months.

Both accused remain in custody.

WHAT HAPPENED TO DJ WARRAS?

Stock was shot and killed outside Zambesi Flats near the Carlton Centre in Johannesburg on 16 December 2025.

He had reportedly been overseeing security-related work at the building when gunmen approached his vehicle and opened fire.

Majola and Buthelezi face charges of premeditated murder and conspiracy to commit murder.

Meanwhile, Armindo Joaquim Pacula has already been sentenced to 25 years in prison for Stock’s murder after admitting his involvement.

Pacula also received sentences for firearm, ammunition and immigration offences.

The case against Majola and Buthelezi will return to court on Monday, 2 November, when the parties are expected to address outstanding pre-trial arrangements.
