Who runs the McDonald’s inside the YPF station?

Arcos Dorados runs it, as the company that operates McDonald’s restaurants across Latin America. YPF supplies the station and its Full store.

Will more YPF stations get a McDonald’s?

The alliance covers stations across Argentina, but neither company has named the next sites. The first restaurant is the first concrete result of the deal.

Can US investors buy YPF and Arcos Dorados?

Both companies have shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange, so US investors can buy them through a normal brokerage account. This article is not investment advice.

Why does an oil company sell hamburgers?

YPF wants its stations to earn money from more than fuel, so it adds food, coffee and shops. Marín says the burger is an extra service that keeps drivers and families coming back.

COLOMBIA · COMPANY NEWS

Key Facts The country Colombia is a South American country of about 53 million people and a major trading partner of the United States.

The company Banco de Bogotá is a Colombian bank more than 155 years old and a member of the Grupo Aval banking group.

What happened On 21 October 2026 IDB Invest announced up to US$70 million for the bank, with US$50 million committed and US$20 million optional.

The purpose The Banco de Bogotá financing is meant to lend more to micro, small and medium-sized companies, which Colombians call mipymes.

The extras Other investors are expected to add about US$80 million, and IDB Invest will help design an ecosystem credit plan for the Colombian Amazon.

The catch No loan term, interest rate, borrower count or payout date has been published.

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

Banco de Bogotá, one of Colombia’s biggest banks, has secured US$50 million from IDB Invest, the private-sector arm of the Inter-American Development Bank. The Banco de Bogotá financing is meant for small firms and can grow to US$70 million.

For US readers the deal matters because it is dollar funding from a Washington-based lender, aimed at small Colombian firms that trade with American buyers. It also shows international lenders still backing Colombian banks, with about US$80 million more expected from other investors.

What the Banco de Bogotá Financing Covers

Under the Banco de Bogotá financing, IDB Invest will provide up to US$70 million in two slices, called tranches. The first, up to US$50 million, is committed, while the second, up to US$20 million, is optional.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The package mixes IDB Invest’s own money with funds from other investors, who are expected to supply about US$80 million. IDB Invest belongs to the IDB Group and says it manages about US$22 billion in assets for more than 400 clients in 25 countries.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Gets the Money

The funds are meant for micro, small and medium-sized companies that want to grow, modernise operations, raise productivity or start new projects. Colombian banks call these firms mipymes, and they are the backbone of local hiring and trade.

The bank says its small-business loans total about COP 11.8 trillion (about US$3.7 billion at 3,174 pesos per US dollar on 22 October 2026). It reports a presence in 93% of Colombian territory, more than 1,000 municipalities and 4.3 million clients.

An Amazon Credit Plan Comes With It

IDB Invest will also advise the bank on an ecosystem credit programme in the Colombian Amazon. The aim is to find ways to benefit local communities and territories through financial products tied to protecting and conserving ecosystems.

Juan Carlos Echeverry, the bank’s president and a former Colombian finance minister, said the Banco de Bogotá financing will widen access to credit for companies. He said it supports the bank’s sustainable development goals, and the bank puts its sustainable loan portfolio at about COP 25.11 trillion (about US$7.9 billion).

Open Finance and the Bank’s Reach

The bank also reports progress on open finance, a system that lets customers share their banking data with other firms through secure software links. It expects COP 1 trillion (about US$315 million) in new transactions through those links by the end of 2026.

From January to August 2026 it logged COP 604,480 million (about US$190 million), with a record COP 106,960 million (about US$34 million) in August. For March to December 2025 the total was about COP 220,000 million (about US$69 million).

About the Bank and Its Parent

Banco de Bogotá is part of Grupo Aval, one of Colombia’s largest banking groups, and serves more than 69,000 corporate clients. Its Company Intelligence profile gives the background, and the Rio Times report on its new president explains the leadership change.

Trade with the United States is a daily concern for Colombian firms, as the Rio Times report on US exports to Colombia shows. Small suppliers are often the first to feel changes in orders, tariffs and credit.

What It Means for US Readers

US investors and exporters can read the Banco de Bogotá financing as a sign that development lenders still channel dollars into Colombian small business. Small Colombian firms supply goods and services to American buyers, and dollar funding can help them fill orders.

IDB Invest belongs to the Inter-American Development Bank Group, a multilateral lender headquartered in Washington. Nothing in the announcement changes tariffs, trade rules or the outlook for US exports to Colombia.

What Is Not Known

Neither IDB Invest nor the bank has said how long the Banco de Bogotá financing runs or what interest it will carry. The announcement also does not say how many companies will receive credit or when the cash will be paid out.

It is not stated whether the optional US$20 million will be used, or which investors will supply the extra US$80 million. The announcement also gives no budget or timetable for the Amazon programme.

More: Colombia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much money is in the Banco de Bogotá financing?

The package is up to US$70 million, with US$50 million committed and up to US$20 million uncommitted. Other investors are expected to add about US$80 million.

Which companies will benefit?

The Banco de Bogotá financing targets micro, small and medium-sized companies in Colombia, which local banks call mipymes. The announcement names no sectors, borrowers or loan sizes.

What is IDB Invest?

IDB Invest is the private-sector lender of the Inter-American Development Bank Group, which is based in Washington. It says it manages about US$22 billion in assets and works in 25 countries.

What is the Amazon credit programme?

It is technical assistance to help the bank design ecosystem credit, meaning financial products linked to protecting and conserving nature. Its budget, timetable and products have not been published.

When was the deal announced?

IDB Invest published the announcement on Wednesday 21 October 2026, and the Colombian business daily La República reported it on Thursday 22 October. The bank has not said when the money will be disbursed.

CHILE · STATE OIL FIRM

Key Facts The country Chile is a copper-rich South American economy that imports more than 95% of the oil it uses, so world prices reach its pumps fast.

What happened Diesel in Chile rises 91.5 pesos a litre (about US$0.09) from Thursday, 22 October, and petrol rises 41.3 pesos (about US$0.04).

The oil price Brent crude, the global benchmark, traded near US$111.74 a barrel on the morning of 22 October, with a high of US$112.60.

The profit ENAP earned US$579 million in the first half of 2026, up 82% from US$318 million a year earlier.

The state bill Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said on 21 October that the state subsidises diesel by about 200 pesos a litre (about US$0.21).

Spending Quiroz said the government has spent 300 billion pesos (about US$308 million) in three weeks to slow the rises.

Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

Chile’s state oil firm ENAP communicated on 21 October that diesel will rise 91.5 pesos a litre (about US$0.09) on Thursday, 22 October. On that morning Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded near US$111.74 a barrel, according to La Tercera.

Short for Empresa Nacional del Petróleo, ENAP earned US$579 million in the first half of 2026, while the government pays to cushion the pump. For US readers, the story shows how a state-owned refiner and its owner handle an oil shock above US$110.

What ENAP Reported on 21 October

The company communicated its new reference fuel prices on Wednesday, 21 October, lifting diesel by 91.5 pesos a litre (about US$0.09). Petrol rose by an average of 41.3 pesos (about US$0.04), and the new prices apply from Thursday, 22 October.

How the Mepco Price Cushion Works

Mepco is Chile’s fuel price stabilisation mechanism, created by Law 20,765 in July 2014, according to the Finance Ministry. It works through increases and cuts to the specific fuel tax, which softens swings in the pump price.

La Tercera says the Kast government changed Mepco in March for fiscal reasons, passing world oil rises more directly to local prices. Chile’s truckers dropped a strike threat after the latest rise and defended the government’s handling of Mepco.

What the State Is Paying for Diesel

Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said on 21 October that the state subsidises diesel by about 200 pesos a litre (about US$0.21). He added that conservative President José Antonio Kast’s government has spent 300 billion pesos (about US$308 million) in three weeks, according to T13.

Quiroz blamed the war in the Middle East, the war in Russia and the destruction of refineries around the world. The government is doing everything fiscally possible, he said, to keep the increases gradual.

The Profit and Debt Behind ENAP

ENAP earned US$579 million in the first half of 2026, up 82% from US$318 million a year earlier. Its core earnings, known as EBITDA, reached US$974 million, up 43% from US$682 million.

The company credits higher sales of its own production and stronger international refining margins. Its operations in Ecuador, Egypt, logistics, refineries and Magallanes drove the result.

Why the State Wants the Firm’s Cash

The Finance Ministry set a 2026 dividend withdrawal of US$593.5 million, and the firm had paid about US$100 million in taxes by then. At the April shareholders’ meeting Quiroz asked that 70% of the company’s profits go to the state, according to BioBioChile.

In July, Fitch Ratings, a credit rating agency, kept ENAP at A- internationally and AAA locally and raised its stand-alone profile from b to bb-. ENAP also agreed on 19 October to buy Pluspetrol’s Ecuadorian oil business for US$207 million, as we reported.

What It Means for US Readers

Brent, the benchmark behind Chile’s import costs, rose on reports of planned new US strikes on Iran, so US policy feeds into Santiago pump prices. Our report on the 22 October price rise has the full list of fuels.

The state says it is spending about US$308 million in three weeks, which investors in Chilean debt may watch as a fiscal factor. Fitch’s A- rating dates from July, before the latest oil jump.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how long the government can keep paying for the diesel cushion, or whether it will change Mepco again. It is also unclear how the high oil price will change the company’s results in the second half of the year.

Actual prices at each station may differ from the Metropolitan Region averages. Economist Juan Ortiz of the OCEC-UDP research centre expects another rise around mid-November, according to La Tercera.

More: Chile news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is ENAP?

It is Empresa Nacional del Petróleo, Chile’s state-owned oil company, which refines crude and also produces oil abroad. Its operations in Ecuador, Egypt, logistics, refineries and Magallanes drove the first-half result.

Who sets fuel prices in Chile?

ENAP communicates weekly reference prices for fuels, and the new ones apply from Thursday, 22 October. Mepco, run by the Finance Ministry, adjusts the specific fuel tax to soften the swings.

What is Mepco?

Mepco is the state mechanism that stabilises fuel prices through increases and cuts to the specific fuel tax. Quiroz says the government now subsidises diesel by about 200 pesos a litre (about US$0.21).

How much did ENAP earn in 2026?

The company earned US$579 million in the first half of 2026, up 82% from US$318 million. Its EBITDA was US$974 million.

How high is Brent crude?

Brent traded near US$111.74 a barrel on the morning of 22 October, with an intraday high of US$112.60. La Tercera links the rise to fears of new strikes on Iran.

World.content:

ARGENTINA · ENERGY

Key Facts The country Argentina is South America’s second-largest economy, run by President Javier Milei, who is selling state assets and extending private licences in energy and water.

The company Edenor is an Argentine power distributor serving about 3.39 million customers, with shares listed in New York.

What happened Edenor registered a wholly owned holding company, Edenor Inversiones, in the official gazette on 19 October 2026.

The money It starts with 30 million pesos (about US$19,700) of capital, all paid in by Edenor, and may buy stakes abroad.

The context Edenor agreed on 10 August to buy 70% of gas distributor Metrogas from YPF for US$780 million.

The catch The registration does not place Metrogas or the fuel stake inside the new company, and the gas deal still needs regulatory and government approvals.

Power Index Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 61.2 points (October 2026 edition).

Edenor, the Buenos Aires electricity distributor whose shares trade in New York, has registered a new Edenor holding company called Edenor Inversiones. Argentina’s official gazette published the registration on Monday 19 October 2026, iProfesional reported.

For US investors the filing shows how the company may structure its fast expansion beyond power lines into gas and fuels. It follows a US$780 million agreement to buy Metrogas, the capital’s biggest gas distributor, from the state-controlled oil group YPF.

What the Edenor Holding Company Is

Edenor Inversiones S.A.U. is a wholly owned subsidiary, which means Edenor holds every share. Public deed number 763 of 7 October 2026 created it, with its office at Edenor’s headquarters on Avenida del Libertador in Buenos Aires.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The Edenor holding company starts with 30 million pesos (about US$19,700 at 1,526.67 pesos per US dollar on 22 October) in capital. It is split into 30 million shares of one peso each, and Edenor paid for all of them, iProfesional reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Argentina Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Wide Mandate for New Deals

The Edenor holding company may buy, hold, manage and finance stakes in other firms, in Argentina or abroad. Its purpose is not limited to energy, and it may lend money or give guarantees to firms it invests in.

It may not carry out activities covered by Argentina’s financial-entities law, and it may not raise money from the public without authorisation. Edenor already created a similar vehicle, Edenor Tech, in July 2024, which was meant to cover energy, fuels, critical minerals and technology.

Who Runs It

Daniel Marx chairs the board of the new company, with Edgardo Alberto Volosin and Eduardo Marcelo Vila as directors. Carlos Esteban Cvitanich chairs the supervisory committee, which watches over the accounts.

Edenor’s controlling group includes businessmen Daniel Vila, José Luis Manzano and Mauricio Filiberti, who bought control from Pampa Energía in 2020. Filiberti, nicknamed the chlorine king, built his fortune in chemicals.

The US$780 Million Metrogas Deal

In a 10 August 2026 filing, Edenor said YPF accepted its offer for 70% of Metrogas and 5% of MetroENERGÍA, a related energy firm. The total price is US$780 million, and YPF would sell all its shares in both.

Closing depends on conditions that include approval from ENRGE, the national gas and electricity regulator. The filing gave no closing date, though iProfesional reported on 30 September that sources expect closing before the end of 2026.

Approvals Still Ahead

Metrogas has signed an agreement with the national government to extend its distribution licence by 20 years, from December 2027 to the end of 2047. The agreement still needs national government approval, and Metrogas shareholders meet on Thursday 29 October to vote on it, Perfil reported.

Under the agreement Metrogas must invest US$186.8 million over ten years and drop its claims against the state, Perfil reported. A presidential decree is still needed, and the news site iProfesional says it is expected in the coming months.

Edenor Also Backs a Shell Fuel Business

Edenor holds a fifth of the Argentine fuel business that trader Mercuria took over from Raízen. Manzano also owns a fifth and Mercuria owns the other three-fifths, iProfesional reported.

The deal closed on 1 September and covers the Dock Sud refinery and 894 Shell-branded stations, at a total value of US$1.42 billion. Forming the Edenor holding company does not automatically move the Metrogas or Shell stakes into it.

What It Means for US Readers

Holders of Edenor’s New York-listed shares and its dollar bonds are watching how the group pays for its expansion. Edenor’s board wants shareholders to lift its bond programme from US$1.7 billion to US$2.4 billion at a meeting on 12 November, iProfesional reported.

An Edenor holding company could keep new businesses apart from the regulated power distributor, which has a licence to protect. The registration does not say how the Metrogas purchase will be financed, so the effect on Edenor’s debt is open.

What Is Not Known

Edenor has not said which assets will move into the Edenor holding company or when. The gazette notice does not link it to Metrogas, and the vehicle for the gas purchase has not been announced.

The final price may also depend on closing adjustments, and the filing gives no payment schedule for the US$780 million. It is also unclear whether the government will approve the licence extension on the terms signed.

More: Argentina news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Edenor?

Edenor is a large Argentine electricity distributor, serving about 3.39 million customers in northern Buenos Aires and its suburbs. Its shares trade in Buenos Aires and in New York.

What is Edenor Inversiones?

The Edenor holding company, Edenor Inversiones, is owned completely by Edenor and was created by a deed of 7 October 2026. It can buy and manage stakes in other companies in Argentina or abroad.

How much capital does the Edenor holding company have?

It starts with 30 million pesos (about US$19,700) of capital, all paid by Edenor. The amount is small compared with the US$780 million Metrogas deal.

Will the new company buy Metrogas?

The gazette notice does not say so, and Edenor has not announced which vehicle will carry the purchase. Edenor itself accepted the YPF terms in its 10 August filing.

What happens next with Metrogas?

Metrogas shareholders meet on 29 October to vote on the 20-year licence extension. The national government and the energy regulator ENRGE must also approve before the sale can close.

Sources: iProfesional, 19 October 2026; iProfesional, 30 September 2026; iProfesional, 15 October 2026; iProfesional, 11 October 2026; Perfil, 30 September 2026; Edenor filing (Form 6-K), 10 August 2026.

World.title: Dunamis Ministries in San Ignacio issues statement following allegations against Pastor
World.content:
Dunamis Ministries in San Ignacio issues statement following allegations against Pastor

By Zoila Palma: Today, Dunamis Ministries in San Ignacio, Cayo issued a statement following allegations against a well-known Pastor.

“The leadership of Dunamis Ministries is aware of the criminal proceedings involving the founder of our Church and acknowledges the concerns expressed by members and the public.

We wish to make it clear that the Church does not intend to prejudge the matter or express any opinion concerning the guilt or innocence of the individual charged. These are questions to be determined exclusively by the Court upon consideration of the evidence presented,” the church said.

In addition, the church said that it recognizes the seriousness of the allegations and remains committed to the principles of accountability, fairness, integrity, and respect for the rule of law.

The church says that it plans to take appropriate administrative measures as may be necessary to ensure the uninterrupted operation of its services, the spiritual welfare of its congregation, and the protection of all persons within its ministry.

“We assure our members that the Church’s mission and responsibilities extend beyond any single individual and that its leadership remains committed to providing stability, guidance, and responsible stewardship during this period.

We respectfully request that the privacy and dignity of all persons concerned be respected while the legal process takes its course,” the church added.

World.title: Belize becomes 1st country to sign new United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework
World.content:
Belize becomes 1st country to sign new United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework

By Zoila Palma: Today, Belize became the first country to sign the new United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework.

This morning, Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca joined Raúl Salazar, United Nations Resident Representative to Belize, for the launch of the Framework for the English- and Dutch-speaking Caribbean.

The Framework, signed by both parties, will guide and strengthen cooperation between the Government of Belize and the United Nations over the next five years.

In his remarks, Minister Fonseca highlighted the tangible results of Belize’s partnership with the United Nations, particularly in education, social development and climate change.

Fonseca highlighted the importance of continued collaboration and called on partners to build on existing progress to advance sustainable development priorities for Belize and the wider Caribbean.

World.title: International News: Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
International News: Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz

By Zoila Palma: Seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by Iran or hitting naval mines, according to Iranian state television on Thursday.

The reported incidents come amid growing fears of renewed full-scale conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel, raising concerns about global oil supplies and maritime security.

The claims have not been independently confirmed, AP reports.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps navy renewed its threat to attack U.S. military bases in the region if Washington continues assisting commercial vessels travelling through the strategic waterway.

Despite the reported attacks, some tankers continue transporting oil under U.S. military protection, with operators reportedly travelling at night and disabling location-tracking systems to reduce the risk of being targeted. Shipping analysts say the increased risks have driven up tanker charter costs and complicated oil deliveries.

The United Nations has urged Washington and Tehran to return to diplomacy and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global energy shipments.

World.title: Southern trailblazer Tony Zabaneh passes away
World.content:
Southern trailblazer Tony Zabaneh passes away

By Zoila Palma: Belize has lost a respected figure with the passing of Antonio “Tony” Zabaneh, the beloved patriarch of the Zabaneh family, who passed away on October 21, 2026.

In 2025, Zabaneh was honored with The Order of Distinction award for contributions to Business & Community Service.

His family has announced his transition into eternal life and is inviting relatives, friends and well-wishers to join them in celebrating his life and legacy.

A Mass of Celebration of his Life will be held on Tuesday, October 27, at 2:00 p.m. at the Holy Redeemer Cathedral in Belize City.

A Mass of Thanksgiving for his Life is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, at 2:00 p.m. at St. Pius X Church in Independence Village, followed by interment in the village.

The Zabaneh family is asking for the presence and prayers of all those whose lives were touched by Tony Zabaneh. His passing marks the loss of a family patriarch whose life and legacy will be remembered by those who knew and loved him.

World.title: Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow found safe after nearly six weeks
World.content:
Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow found safe after nearly six weeks

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have confirmed that missing Police Constable Kenyon Barrow, who disappeared in September, has been found safe after approximately 40 days.

The confirmation came on Thursday morning, October 22, through an official update shared by police with members of the media. Authorities confirmed that Barrow, who is from Orange Walk Town, had been located and was safe.

Barrow was reported missing on September 17 after relatives lost contact with him. He was last seen around September 11 or 12, prompting concerns about his whereabouts.

His disappearance triggered an extensive search involving the Belize Police Department, Belize Defence Force personnel and community volunteers. Search teams reportedly used drones to examine heavily vegetated areas around Orange Walk, while officers conducted house-to-house inquiries in an effort to locate him.

Barrow, who was attached to the Orange Walk Police Formation, had reportedly stopped reporting for duty on July 30, several weeks before he was reported missing.

The news that he has been found safe brings a positive end to weeks of uncertainty surrounding his disappearance.

Police have not yet disclosed where Barrow was found, what circumstances led to his disappearance or whether he will be returning to active duty.

World.title: Belize participates in Routes World 2026 in Germany
World.content:
Belize participates in Routes World 2026 in Germany

By Zoila Palma: Belize is participating in Routes World 2026, taking place October 21–23 in Frankfurt, Germany.

The annual forum brings together airlines, airports, and aviation stakeholders worldwide to strengthen air connectivity and support global economic growth.

Belize’s delegation is led by Director of Tourism Evan Tillett and includes Anthony Hunt and Nicolás Gurwicz of the Aviation Development Committee.

The Belize Tourism Board says that for the next 3 days, the delegation is meeting with senior airline network planners from key markets to advance discussions on future route development and explore opportunities to expand air access to Belize.

World.title: BDF and University of Belize sign scholarship agreement for service members
World.content:
BDF and University of Belize sign scholarship agreement for service members

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Defence Force (BDF) and the University of Belize (UB) have signed a scholarship agreement aimed at expanding educational opportunities for BDF service members. The agreement reinforces both institutions’ commitment to academic development, professional growth and capacity building within Belize’s security sector.

This builds on a Memorandum of Understanding signed on July 15, 2025, which established a strategic partnership between the two institutions. Under the existing partnership, two BDF service members are currently pursuing tertiary-level studies at the University of Belize.

The agreement was signed by representatives of both institutions, including Michel Chebat and UB President Dr. Vincent Palacio, who reaffirmed their commitment to creating greater educational opportunities for the men and women serving in Belize’s security apparatus.

The partnership is expected to support the development of leadership, innovation and professional skills within the BDF while strengthening collaboration between the military and the country’s national university.

World.title: International News: United Nations warn El Niño could become strongest on record, urges Governments to prepare
World.content:
International News: United Nations warn El Niño could become strongest on record, urges Governments to prepare

By Zoila Palma: United Nations officials are warning that the current El Niño climate event could reach unprecedented strength, potentially triggering extreme heat, droughts and flooding across the world.

World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Secretary-General Celeste Saulo issued the warning on Wednesday, urging governments to take early action to reduce the potential damage.

The WMO’s latest global seasonal climate updates show sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific could rise as much as 3.8 degrees Celsius above average between November and January.

Saulo said the event is expected to peak toward the end of 2026, but its effects could continue long after, adding to rising global temperatures driven by human-caused climate change.

UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher warned that the phenomenon could have severe humanitarian and economic consequences, including food insecurity, displacement, migration and increased conflict.

He stressed that governments, development banks and international financial institutions must provide funding before disasters occur, rather than waiting until communities are already affected.

World.title: Water pressure
World.content:
Addressing a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Water Minister Matthew Samuda (left) acknowledges the public’s concerns about higher water bills, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.Naphtali Junior

WATER Minister Matthew Samuda and National Water Commission (NWC) officials are defending the utility’s proposed 51 per cent tariff increase, arguing that rising operating costs, ageing infrastructure, and repeated droughts have made higher revenue necessary to maintain and improve water supply.

Speaking at a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Samuda acknowledged the public’s concerns about higher bills, but argued that the country can no longer postpone major repairs to its water system, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.

“If we could have asked for one per cent and been okay we would have asked for one per cent. No politician on the planet Earth is interested in increasing the cost of living. This is a necessary step to resolve long-standing issues in our water sector,” Samuda said.

He said Jamaica is “in a race against time” to replace ageing infrastructure and improve the reliability of water supplies, warning that the country’s long history of inadequate investment has left the utility facing mounting challenges.

In the meantime, Shaw noted that the NWC needs to be able to meet the public’s expectations while maintaining its daily operations.

“We need to continue the operations from one day to the next. Our citizenry is expecting that when they go home and turn on that tap, there’s water in it. There can’t be any worse feeling. So if you were to measure when you go home and you turn on [the switch] and there’s no light versus turn on and there’s no water, I think it’s a no-brainer, and as such, this tariff is going to right-size our position to ensure that we continue to deliver, as is our commitment to the citizens of Jamaica,” he said.

Samuda said the proposed increase must be viewed against the economic and environmental challenges Jamaica has faced since the last interim tariff adjustment granted in 2019.

He said the COVID-19 pandemic caused significant revenue losses when hotels and other commercial customers shut down, while disruptions to supply chains and rising prices subsequently increased the cost of operating the utility.

He added that droughts in 2022, 2023 and 2025; along with Hurricane Beryl and Tropical Storm Rafael in 2024; alongside Hurricane Melissa last year, further affected the NWC’s operations and revenue.

The minister argued that the utility continued to incur expenses even when drought reduced the amount of water available to sell.

He also pointed to rising energy costs and changes to staff salaries, saying the NWC’s energy costs were now close to 50 per cent higher than in 2019, while salaries had doubled over the same period.

“Nobody plans for three out of your five worst droughts ever during this period. Nobody plans for the worst El Nino in 200 years, which is what this is becoming, and… when we talk about these things people say, ‘El Nino? Whatever.’ But the last time we had an El Nino like this it triggered global famine. This is not a normal weather phenomenon that we are going through,” he added.

Samuda argued that these pressures had been absorbed while the NWC’s tariffs remained unchanged, but said the utility could no longer defer essential repairs to its ageing infrastructure.

He noted that the NWC had never replaced even one per cent of its asset base in a single year during Jamaica’s independent history — a shortfall he said had contributed to the deterioration of pipes and other infrastructure.

He pointed to repeated breaks in a major pipeline at Coral Gardens in Montego Bay, which he said had broken six times in one month and required a $170-million intervention to safeguard the main supply line serving the city.

“The reality is the capital replacement ratio of a utility is not intended to fall below one per cent of total capital replacement being done on an annual basis. In our independent life that has never happened…we’ve never replaced one per cent of the asset base of the water commission in a single year. We’ve never gotten close, and that is the utility standard globally. So what you have happening in the middle of that seven-year period is also the collapse of ageing infrastructure. I should be changing the third generation of those lines now, not the first generation in that way,” he said.

Samuda said the combination of ageing infrastructure, climate-related pressures, and decades of inadequate investment have left Jamaica with urgent work to do.

“Ultimately, it is our responsibility to do now what should have been done a long time ago. We will do it. And we can have confidence that at the back end of our work and our investment in these varying programmes, they will have the confidence; and I assure them in the coming years we’ll have other things to complain about other than potable water in the pipes,” he said.

The proposed 51 per cent increase has not been approved by the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR), which is to review the NWC’s application.

Furthermore, Acting NWC President Kevin Kerr separately told the Jamaica Observer that the application includes a significantly lower proposed increase for the utility’s lowest consumers, but said the details could not yet be released because the OUR had not reviewed the application.

World.title: Gully bank relocation
World.content:
From left: K2 developer Richard Lake; Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness; developer Michael Lake; and Phillip Paulwell, Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal, cut the ribbon to the development. At back is Delano Seiveright, state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce.(Photo: Andrew Holness on X)

AN initiative by the Government to relocate people whose houses are situated on gully banks, and who are often affected by adverse weather events, is to be piloted in four communities across the Corporate Area.

The disclosure was made by Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Wednesday, during his address at the official opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony of the K2 housing development in downtown Kingston.

Although the timeline of the pilot’s execution was not disclosed, Holness said the project will facilitate the construction of new abodes for people who will be relocated, or the provision of grants for them to source other spaces to call home.

One of the communities of concern mentioned by Holness was the flood-prone Burger Gully, situated in the Kingston Eastern constituency.

“We will be selecting maybe four communities across the Corporate Area to start the pilot project to have persons who are living on the gully banks, particularly those that are at risk of an epiphenomenal weather event, to help them to move from the gully banks. We cannot continue this unsafe practice… that must come to an end,” Holness said.

Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal Phillip Paulwell, who was also at the function, had disclosed in August that close to 150 residents of Burger Gully had signalled their willingness to relocate.

The flooding of the gully, an informal settlement also called 17 1/2 Mountain View Avenue, has been an ongoing problem, but worsened last year as sections of the gully which runs through the community were damaged by flood waters.

At that time, Paulwell said lands were identified in the communities of Mountain View and Rockfort to facilitate the relocation exercise, but a response was being awaited from minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan.

Holness maintained Wednesday that the issue of communities which are currently irregularly settled “must come to an end”, but underscored that “the success of any government policy is dependent upon the government’s ability… to do what it says it’s going to do”.

“In my own constituency I have demonstrated to the people there how the Government can effectively do a relocation. In the best circumstances, relocation is always disruptive. In the best circumstances, persons are going to feel traumatised by relocation. No one wants to have their house uprooted, their furniture taken and destroyed. Nobody wants to have to move from where they have made their life,” said Holness, who is Member of Parliament for St Andrew West Central.

According to Holness, the National Works Agency will also test a programme that will reclaim the reservations [of buildings] 20 feet away from the gullies in Kingston.

“Whenever I speak like this, immediately everybody starts to get worried [that,] ‘Boy, the Government going to come throw me off [my land].’ That’s not what the Government wants to do. The Government has a right in law to, for the public good, have persons relocate. But the relocation must be done in such a way that the people who are relocated are made no worse off,” Holness said.

The K2 development, located in Bournemouth Gardens, Kingston 2, is a 10-storey residence featuring 119 units. It was developed by Sherbourne Limited, led by Michael and Richard Lake.

World.title: Mental Chung sees The Psychic Realm
World.content:
Mental Chung .

An animator/graphic designer by profession, Mental Chung wanted to express that creativity when he launched his music career eight years ago.

He called his sound Reggae Barque, which can be heard on The Psychic Realm, the St Ann artiste’s first album.

Released on October 10, it contains six songs which Mental Chung produced for his Art Creed Records.

“The songs come from new age spiritual concepts surrounding the hidden forces and ones guiding us in life,” he reasoned. “I went for a more mainstream, youthful sound that has elements of reggae, soul and dancehall.”

Quinting Pink Pinch is the only song from the project released to date. The Psychic Realm’s songs are driven by ethereal beats conjured by Stephen Dajure and Aye Psycho.

Their rhythms complement what Mental Chung describes as “playful, militant and thought-provoking” music.

Born Reinardo Chung, he got his creative start as an animator almost 20 years ago with Bad Influence, an eight-minute, dancehall-inspired film released in 2010. It won an award at the Reggae Film Festival which was held in May 2011 in Kingston.

Mental Chung’s stocks rose even more with the Dutty Bwoy series, which was driven by his love for dancehall culture. It has animated cameos by stars like Bounty Killer, Beenie Man, and Usain Bolt.

Lead, Blaze It, and Talk Back are some of the songs that announced Mental Chung’s music career.

— Howard Campbell

World.title: FID wins big
World.content:
.

THE Financial Investigations Division (FID), in its capacity as Jamaica’s assets recovery agency under the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA), has secured a Pecuniary Penalty Order of $62 million against businessman Ou Yongjia, following his convictions for unauthorised use of a trademark and misleading and deceptive conduct.

The order was made by consent in the Home Circuit Court of the Supreme Court on October 2, 2026, pursuant to Section 5(3)(b) of POCA.

As the initial sum payable under the order, Yongjia agreed to forfeit $20 million held in bank accounts that were restrained by the Supreme Court on March 18, 2025. He will pay the balance of $42 million to the FID in monthly instalments commencing February 2, 2027.

The matter began on February 11, 2021, when police executed a special warrant at a business premises owned and operated by Yongjia.

Officers seized 2,840 pairs of counterfeit slippers bearing the trademark designs of three popular brands, two invoice books, and $829,000 in cash. Based on the selling prices recorded in the seized invoice books, the FID estimated the value of the counterfeit slippers at $1.3 million.

Yongjia was charged on March 4, 2021. On December 7, 2022 he pleaded guilty in the Corporate Area Parish Court (Criminal Division) to one count of misleading and deceptive conduct, contrary to Section 28(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, and three counts of unauthorised use of a trademark, contrary to Section 69(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act.

He was fined $375,000 on each count, or nine months’ imprisonment in default, a total of $1.5 million, which was paid on the same day. A separate charge of possession of criminal property was withdrawn by the prosecution.

Following the convictions the matter was committed to the Home Circuit Court so the FID could pursue a Pecuniary Penalty Order or Forfeiture Order under Section 5 of POCA. The FID subsequently filed its application in 2023. By virtue of his convictions Yongjia was deemed, under Section 6(1)(a) of POCA, to have a criminal lifestyle, from which he obtained a benefit.

The FID’s financial investigators examined records relating to four bank accounts held by Yongjia and his business between 2019 and 2024, including records obtained under a Production and Inspection Order. This was followed by a sworn statement of information filed with the court on March 11, 2025. The $62-million sum was agreed between the parties, and Yongjia consented to the order being made without a benefit hearing, and waived his right to challenge or appeal the FID’s application.

Under the consent agreement, interest will accrue at five per cent per annum on any instalment not paid by its due date, and the bailiff of the Supreme Court is authorised to seize and sell chattels owned by Yongjia, without further order of the court, to satisfy any sums left unpaid.

The agreement also provides that failure to comply with the payment schedule is an offence, punishable on conviction before a parish court judge by imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, and that any reversion to or future participation in criminal conduct would permit the FID to pursue the full amount of the assessed benefit.

The court’s order carries a penal notice and gives the FID liberty to apply to enforce its terms.

FID’s Principal Director of Financial Crimes Investigations Keith Darien said the outcome reflects the careful work of its investigators who followed the financial trail connected to the case and presented a clear, evidence-based picture to the court.

“It also reflects the importance of our collaboration with law enforcement partners. The FID remains committed to ensuring that those who profit from unlawful conduct do not keep the benefit,” he said.

Added FID Senior Director of Legal Services Courtney Smith: “Jamaica’s asset recovery framework continues to mature through the restraint, seizure and confiscation of criminal property, advancing the broader objectives of punishment, deterrence and rehabilitation. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to depriving offenders of criminal benefits, encouraging lawful conduct, and ensuring that crime does not pay.”

A Pecuniary Penalty Order requires a person to pay a sum of money in respect of benefits obtained from criminal conduct. Asset recovery under POCA is a lawful, court-supervised process, and the FID said it will continue to take lawful steps, where the evidence supports it, to remove the benefit from crime and protect Jamaica’s financial system from criminal abuse.

World.title: HANDLE WITH CARE
World.content:
Vitel Lawes of West Indies bowls during the ICC Under-19 Men’s Cricket World Cup Super Six match against Ireland at HP Oval in Windhoek, Namibia, on January 25, 2026. (Photo: ICC/Getty Images)

FORMER West Indies all-rounder Carlos Brathwaite believes the coaching staff must ensure Jamaican teenager Vitel Lawes continues to develop, after his recent struggles against India.

Lawes recently returned from the Windies’ white-ball tour of India where he played in the three-match One-Day International (ODI) series.

The 19-year-old came to prominence during the Under-19 World Cup earlier this year and made his senior international debut against New Zealand in July. He took eight wickets in the five-match series, which the Windies lost 3-2, including best figures of 3-39 in the third ODI.

However, Lawes went wicketless in the second and third ODIs against India, conceding 127 runs across the two matches as the Windies lost the series 2-1.

Several Caribbean fans criticised his performances and questioned whether he was ready for international cricket.

Former West Indies fast bowler and cricket commentator Ian Bishop, who covered the series, defended the young Jamaican.

“I’ll say it again: We have to be patient with Vitel Lawes and manage the youth better,” he said on X. “We keep rushing the kid into scenarios he isn’t ready for. Please give him time to grow and get his reps in. He is 19 years old, not 29 years old.”

Brathwaite, who helped the West Indies win the T20 World Cup in 2016, is concerned about the support Lawes will receive as he gains experience at the international level.

“A part of me is happy he’s getting the opportunities and that we’re backing a young player, but for me now the follow-up is how do we support that young player,” he said on The Super Over podcast.

“The challenge I found that West Indies cricket has had is not necessarily finding talent — [because] finding talent has always been quite easy for us — I think the difficulty for West Indies is honing that talent.” Brathwaite believes Head Coach Daren Sammy and his staff must find ways to help Lawes improve, especially with fewer opportunities for young players to gain experience in first class cricket because of Cricket West Indies’ (CWI) financial difficulties.

“You look to three first class games this season and no Super 50, [so] where does a Vitel Lawes now go at a level below international cricket and learn his game? He would have had lots of things that he would have done well and be happy with, and there’ll be a lot more things that he probably was unhappy with coming out of India, things he can work on, but where does he work on those things?” Brathwaite asked.

“Does he work on those things in a random pitch somewhere in Jamaica where the pressure is off and the spotlights are off as well? Or do we throw him in at first class level, 50-over level, T20 level? What is the level between CPL and international cricket? So, my challenge to the powers that be in West Indies cricket is to see what Vital Lawes has done well, see the challenges he’s had, and now give him an opportunity to be able to learn at the level below so he can have a quicker bounce back and not be like a Jewel Andrew a couple years later, flirting between the doldrums and — I don’t want to say failure — but not hitting the heights that we expected of him two years ago.”

Sammy said in September that the team would remain patient with Lawes because of his ability as a wrist spinner.

“Vitel, to me, is a find for us. What we saw in him that caused him to debut against New Zealand was all part of the planning and the processes we put in place. You’ve heard me for years talking about a wrist spinner in the West Indies team, and Vitel came in and immediately had an impact on the bowling unit for us,” he said.

“He’s still got a long way to go but we will continue with his development through either playing games or the specific work we’ve put in place for him. He’s worked really well with Nikita Miller and Ravi Rampaul. We’ll continue creating those opportunities for him and, hopefully, he can continue to grow. A little bit fast-tracked, but we’re pleased with what he’s done so far.”
