World.title: Held Together with Wire: Inside Romania’s Neglected Arms Industry
World.content:
Jobs for the boys

At Uzina Mecanica Bucuresti, Romania’s only tank manufacturer, the general manager Mihai Rafiu was detained over the summer by anti-corruption prosecutors. He is accused of taking bribes from a contractor in exchange for approving procurement deals. The case is still open.

UM Bucuresti declined to comment on the ongoing investigation itself. But the company confirmed to BIRN that its board has temporarily reassigned Rafiu’s duties to the company’s economic director. Rafiu did not respond to questions sent through the company.

At Carfil, one of Romania’s main ammunition makers, a similar story played out a decade earlier, although what followed was rather unusual. In 2015, Carfil’s general manager, Aurel Veltan, was arrested and later convicted of abuse of office for steering company contracts to a firm without following proper procurement rules. A court sentenced him to a suspended prison sentence and banned him from holding leadership roles at state-owned companies for five years. However, Veltan apparently never left Carfil. According to his resume, he stayed on as head of the marketing and sales unit, and in October 2024 he was promoted to commercial director.

Veltan told BIRN that Carfil restructured in 2024 and brought in experienced people for leadership roles, including himself. He pointed to his three decades working in the company’s commercial department. He declined to comment on the criminal case or the sentence he served.

Some of the men running these plants have both a political resume as well as a police file. Ioan Narcis Chisalita, interim director of Arsenal Resita, an artillery factory, spent years as a senator and worked as an adviser to former prime minister Viktor Ponta, who was forced out of office in 2015 after a nightclub fire that killed 65 people.

In 2019, prosecutors named Chisalita as a suspect in a wider corruption case involving a regional road authority, accusing him of using his position in a political party to help push through illegal job appointments. One part of that case against him was closed last year – not because he was cleared, but because the statute of limitations had expired. A separate related case is still active in court, but Chisalita told BIRN he is not a party to the proceedings.

He added that he was appointed interim director of Arsenal Resita because of his “personal experience in corporate governance and in running private companies as an administrator”.

Other figures raise political rather than legal questions. Razvan Marian Pircalabescu spent many years advising ministers before serving as an advisor in the prime minister’s office in late 2024 and 2025 – a period that spanned governments from both of Romania’s main parties, the Social Democratic Party (PSD) and the National Liberal Party (PNL). In August 2025, he was named general manager of Romarm. His own resume shows he simultaneously serves as board president of Carfil, one of the 15 companies Romarm oversees, meaning he effectively answers to himself.

Carfil told BIRN that Pircalabescu’s dual role is “outside the company’s scope of authority” and declined to comment further. Pircalabescu did not respond to enquiries.

At the Sadu munitions plant in the southwestern part of Romania, Viorel Salvador Caragea was, until recently, a special administrator, an Economy Ministry-appointed overseer of the company’s finances.

Caragea spent nearly three decades in the police force, rising to become the top police official in Gorj county before retiring. He was appointed to the job at Sadu with the backing of the Save Romania Union (USR) party. Since then, the national press have reported a string of legal disputes: courts have twice ordered him to pay damages over comments he made online about a prosecutor and a mayor.

Sadu confirmed that Caragea had received BIRN’s questions. The company later informed BIRN that on September 17, after the questions had been sent, he was dismissed as its special administrator. The company gave no further explanation.

These five are by no means anomalies. Several other Romarm subsidiaries have board members or directors with similar political backing, appointed under different governments and different parties.

But the problems extend well beyond those running the companies. Inside the factories themselves, the picture is even more troubling.

World.title: Acquittal Fuels Doubts over Transfer of Bosnian War Crimes Cases to Serbia
World.content:
Novakovic was acquitted in May this year but Karlica’s case was returned for a retrial on certain charges; in August, the Belgrade Court of Appeal upheld Novakovic’s acquittal, and this month, the Humanitarian Law Centre said Karlica was also found not guilty.

Alic said he was “disappointed” with the court proceedings in Belgrade, in which he said he testified.

“I wouldn’t say you get used to it, but as time passes and you follow these proceedings, you come to see that certain people are simply going through the motions,” he said.

Murat Tahirovic, president of the Association of Victims and Witnesses of Genocide in Bosnia, said the verdict fitted a pattern evident in Serbia. He cited the case of eight Bosnian Serb former police officers charged over the execution of more than 1,300 Bosniak civilians at a warehouse in the village of Kravica near Srebrenica in July 1995.

“There is a trial that is still ongoing, which has not been completed, and which started in 2015, involving eight police officers from Kravica,” said Tahirovic.

“That case has been dragging on for 11 years. There is always some reason to postpone it. However, the question is what to do, how to make it serious, so to speak.”

“Any case transferred there will not get its necessary epilogue. If there is a conviction, the sentences will be minimal or there will be acquittals.”

According to Cestic Jelovac, the indictment brought against Novakovic and Karlica by war crimes prosecutors in Serbia did not cover the same factual and legal framework as the indictment transferred from Bosnia, given that the prosecution in Serbia refuses to bring charges of crimes against humanity.

Cestic Jelovac said the prosecution failed to submit new evidence. The judge’s verdict was also “problematic”, she said, “as the court did not assess the presented evidence in an appropriate manner”.

“In the explanation, the judge states that women and children were transported by tractor to the settlement of Urije in order to be sheltered and protected, which is unacceptable because the court did not look at the broader context of the attack on Alici and Ekici and the forced relocation of the Bosniak population.”

“Even with the qualification of a war crime against the civilian population, nothing prevents the court from looking at the role of the accused through the broader context of the event, the way civilians were treated before the event covered by the indictment, and the connection of individual actions. Exactly what the High Court in Belgrade failed to do in the proceedings against Milenko Karlica.”

Calls for closer cooperation

World.title: Multiple Arrests Across Serbia Ahead of Crucial Elections
World.content:
At least seven individuals were arrested or detained on Wednesday by Serbian police on suspicion that they were planning violent actions for election day this Sunday. Five of the individuals were arrested in the northern city of Novi Sad.

The Higher Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade said that the arrests were done in coordination with the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Novi Sad and members of the Security Intelligence Agency (BIA).

The five individuals in Novi Sad, all aged either 27 or 28, were arrested “due to reasonable suspicion that on the day of the parliamentary elections, Sunday, October 25, 2026, with the intent of undermining the constitutional order and security of Serbia, they planned to commit acts of violence, riots, as well as attacks on political opponents and police officers.”

They are suspected of recruiting people for “physical clashes” on Sunday. As the prosecution added, the plan was to come to Belgrade “for the violent alteration of the constitutional order and the overthrow of the highest state bodies.”

The press release stated that “This plan would be executed by using mobile teams operating outside the legal framework to attack political opponents and police officers using tools and weapons”, and that “the means for committing the criminal offences – balaclavas, wooden poles, flares, knives, and weapons” were to be provided by a member of the group.

The suspects have been detained for up to 48 hours.

Lawyer Rastko Naumov told BIRN that his client Srdjan Ilic, an opposition activist from Belgrade, was detained on Wednesday morning because of alleged planned actions during election day.

“They came this morning with an order from the Higher Court in Belgrade to search the house due to the criminal offence of ‘preparing an act against the constitutional order and security of Serbia’,” Naumov said.

He added that all electronic devices were temporarily seized from Ilic, including computers, phones, hard drives and similar items.

After the house search, he was handed a summons to give a statement to the police, where he went voluntarily, after which he was detained for up to 48 hours.

The informal organisation “Belgrade Stays” (Beograd ostaje), of which Ilic was a member, said on the social media platform X that “police appeared at the addresses of several of their activists”, but gave no other details.

In the town of Vrnjacka Banja in central Serbia one more activist was arrested on Wednesday, according to claims from Katarina Obradovic, the municipal coordinator of the opposition Student List.

Obradovic told N1 television that police officers raided the home of a member of the citizens’ assembly of Vrnjacka Banja around half past five this morning, conducted a search and detained him.

“They searched everything from the attic to the basement for no particular reason, and nothing suspicious was found. They asked the lawyer if there were any weapons. In the house, they only found promotional material for the Student List meant for information booths, and nothing else,” she said. His electronic devices were also taken.

Serbia has been facing mass anti-government student protests for nearly two years. The student movement nominated their Student List consisting of professors and experts they chose for snap elections that will be held on Sunday. The Student List is currently the strongest opponent to former President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, which has been in power since 2012.

Ahead of some of the larger protests during this period, Serbian authorities repeatedly arrested some of the most prominent activists.

World.title: Croatian Government Gives 15,000 Unlicensed Apartments 4 More Years
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The Croatian Government has given in on certain aspects of the Hospitality Activity Act, providing 15,000 unlicensed apartments 4 more years to operate.

The Croatian Government has now accepted the final proposal of the Hospitality Activity Act, which extends the validity of temporary decisions for around 15,000 landlords by an additional four years, the Ministry of Tourism and Sport announced. Index reports that these temporary decisions – on the basis of which apartments and rooms operate in buildings that do not have all the necessary papers, an occupancy permit, or are still waiting for the completion of the legalisation process – were due to expire at the end of this year. If the law had remained unchanged, thousands of landlords would have had to lock up, but with the new legislative proposal the Government has moved the deadline all the way to the 31st of December 2030.

protecting the livelihoods of family landlords

Tourism and Sport Minister Tonči Glavina said that this protects the livelihood of family landlords and ensures the continuity of their business so that they have enough time to legalise their properties and obtain permanent permits. “This is an important measure, especially when we take into account that at the end of 2024 around 15,000 landlords were operating on the basis of temporary decisions,” Glavina stated.

unique registration numbers as of 2027

In addition to extending the permits for legalisation, the law also brings novelties aimed at combating unregistered rentals. A unique registration number is being introduced for accommodation units advertised via online platforms such as Booking and Airbnb, but this provision will not enter into force immediately – only from the 1st of May 2027 so that the market has time to adapt. The state plans to establish direct data exchange with the platforms, which means that properties without a valid registration number would no longer be allowed to be advertised online. At the same time, county bodies are obliged to submit accurate data on the number of resolved cases and temporary decisions to the Ministry once a year, by the 30th of June.

higher penalties and closer inspections

The new legal framework also provides for higher misdemeanour fines for violations of the regulations, expanded powers for tourism and tax inspectors, and the digitisation of administrative procedures through the eTurizam system. Another novelty is that the rental of rooms and apartments in family houses will in future also be able to be registered through a craft or a limited liability company (d.o.o.), and not only in the status of a private landlord as has been the case until now. The bill has been sent to the parliamentary procedure for a second reading.

World.title: €3,000 Parking Fine Arrives a Year After Dubrovnik Trip – Poles Outraged
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – A €3,000 parking fine arrived at the addresses of tourists following their Dubrovnik trip an entire year later, and it’s safe to say they’re not happy…

Fines that some former visitors to Dubrovnik “earned” by parking their cars around the historic city centre are arriving months after they return from their holidays, and the case has attracted plenty of attention in the Polish media. Morski reports that one of the fined tourists contacted Croatia’s well known media outlet Index, claiming that because of two entries into the restricted zone he received two fines of €1,500 each, meaning the total sum amounted to €3,000.

“I’m writing to you on my own behalf and on behalf of many Polish tourists who, instead of returning with nice memories from a holiday in Croatia, specifically Dubrovnik, came back deeply disappointed by the greed and inhumane rules that apply in that city,” he wrote.

The Polish tourist claims that the fines reached him more than one year after his trip to Croatia. “Personally I received two separate fines of €1,500 each. In addition, the law firms hired by the city authorities don’t even reply to e-mails and it’s extremely difficult to communicate with them,” he stated. According to him, the problem has caused a lot of dissatisfaction among Polish tourists, and television stations and internet portals are reporting on it.

In addition, this particular Polish tourist complained that traffic signs warning about the entry restriction are in place, but he considers that it is nowhere near clear enough to tourists what they must do in order to be allowed to enter the zone by car, and that the fines are disproportionate to the offence. On the 2nd of June 2025, the City of Dubrovnik introduced a special traffic regime zone around the historic centre in order to reduce traffic congestion and protect the area that has been exposed to a large number of vehicles for years.

The City of Dubrovnik otherwise prescribed fines of €260 for natural persons, €660 for craftspersons and persons performing independent activities, and a significantly higher €1,320 for legal entities. The responsible person in a legal entity can be fined an additional €260.

World.title: Montenegro EU Accession: “Without Croatian Consent There is No Progress”
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The issues surrounding Montenegro and its EU accession closely involve Croatia, with EU Commissioner Marta Kos saying that without Croatian consent there can be no progress.

Complicated, war-mired bilateral issues between Montenegro and Croatia are not part of the negotiating process with the European Union, but they must be resolved, said EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos. She explained that Montenegro’s further progress depends on the consent of all 27 member states. Anadolu/Index reports that Commissioner Kos emphasised that Croatia has its own interests, but that she is encouraged by the steps Montenegro has taken towards resolving these open issues. She considers the signing of the accession treaty by the summer of 2027 to be a realistic goal and that Brussels supports the plan for Montenegro to become the 28th EU member in 2028.

the differences between politics and eu accession negotiations

She also commented on the possibility that Croatian demands could become official Brussels conditions and explained that a distinction should be made between the technical part of the negotiations and the political support of the member states. “Here, I’d like to separate the technical process from the support that every candidate country must receive from all 27 European Union members. What you in Montenegro have achieved in the last three years truly happens once in a lifetime. You have made enormous progress and I’m genuinely proud of you. I hope you in Montenegro are also proud of yourselves,” Kos said.

She stressed that the consent of all member states is necessary for the continuation of the European path. “At that level you have done almost everything; we are just a little short. But if we want to go further in this process in Brussels, we need the consent of all 27 members. Croatia has its interests and speaks openly about them,” she stated. “I’m glad that Montenegro has taken certain steps in recent days and that dialogue between Croatia and Montenegro exists. I think you are on the right path to resolve these bilateral issues as well. They are not part of the negotiating process, but because of everything I have explained they must be resolved,” she added.

one step closer to formal eu membership

Kos also referred to the decision of the Montenegrin Parliament to accept constitutional changes relating to the integrity check of candidates for government members. “The Montenegrin Parliament has brought your country one step closer to the goal, which is full membership of the European Union. This is an excellent result that shows that your MPs also understand why it is now important that, in sporting terms, you are in the final of one of the most important matches in Montenegro’s history,” Kos said. She emphasised that the adoption of the constitutional changes brings Montenegro closer to closing Chapter 23 and then to the completion of the accession negotiations themselves.

the painful issue of war crimes committed against croatia

Kos also answered a question about Parliament Speaker Andrija Mandić. His removal did not succeed in parliament, and the opposition criticised him for expressing condolences to the family of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić. Kos stated that only the Parliament decides on its leadership. “Only the Parliament can decide on its leadership, no one else. In the EU, there is truly no place for glorifying war criminals. It’s important, as President Ursula von der Leyen and I personally have stressed, that reconciliation and respect for the victims are values that mean a great deal to us in Europe,” Kos said.

“The painful history of the former Yugoslavia is full of open wounds. I think it is good to talk about this, but not by looking backwards, but forwards. It is important to say if something is not right or if someone has not acted well. These are our values, and these European Union values are one of the reasons why Montenegro wants to join the EU.”

Ahead of the upcoming Berlin Process summit in Budva, Kos assessed that Montenegro is in the focus of European leaders and that its results are increasingly of interest to the member states. She believes that the summit in Budva, after the one in Tivat, will further strengthen Montenegro’s international visibility and its European perspective. “European leaders see how much Montenegro has achieved and it is clear to Europe who will be our next member. In June at the summit in Tivat the French President Emmanuel Macron was present for the first time, and today the German Chancellor is coming. I believe each of them is delighted when they come here,” Kos said.

She added that, along with regional cooperation, one of the primary topics will be the way in which the EU can help Montenegro complete the negotiations and become a full member.

World.title: Croatia Wants to Host the 2030 UEFA Futsal Championship
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – Croatia has officially put its bid in to host the 2030 UEFA Futsal Championship, with Split and Zagreb as the proposed host cities.

The Croatian Football Federation has formally applied to host the 2030 European Futsal Championship, it was announced on the federation’s official website. As Slobodna Dalmacija reports, the European football federation UEFA has received seven candidacies, including Croatia’s as well as those of Finland, France, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Poland and Spain. As host cities, the Croatian Football Federation has registered Zagreb (Arena Zagreb) and Split (Spaladium Arena).

Interested federations must submit the final bid documentation by the 8th of June 2027, and the UEFA Executive Committee will decide on the host in September 2027. The bidding process was launched on the 29th of June this year, and national federations were invited to submit expressions of interest by the 13th of October 2026. The European Championship will be held during the months of January and February 2030.

As a quick reminder, Croatia was a successful organiser of the 2012 European Futsal Championship, when the host cities were also Zagreb and Split, and it still holds the record for attendance at a single match at the European tournament. At the semi-final match between Croatia and Russia in Arena Zagreb, 14,300 spectators were present.

In addition to Croatia, candidacies to host the 2030 UEFA Futsal EURO have also been submitted by Finland, France, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Poland and Spain.

World.title: Croatia is the Leading Camping Destination by Quality in Europe for 2027
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – Croatia is the leading camping destination in terms of quality in Europe for 2027, following very significant improvement and offer diversity.

Croatian camping has significantly improved the quality and diversity of its accommodation offer, facilities and services over the past two decades, further strengthening its position on the European tourism market. Continued investment in quality, adaptation to market changes and responding to increasingly demanding guest expectations are key to the further development of the sector. Glas Istre/The Voice of Istria reports that these are the main topics of the jubilee 20th Croatian Camping Congress, organised by the Croatian Camping Association (KUH), taking place from the 19th to the 21st of October at the Well Hotel in Terme Tuhelj.

“This is a fantastic day for Croatian camping and the realisation of the dreams of all tourism workers who have worked for years to make Croatian camping the best in Europe in terms of quality. Recent research by PiNCAMP, the camping platform within ADAC, confirms that Croatia has become the leading camping destination by quality, which we can all be very proud of. This is an additional incentive for the further development of Croatian camping, and at the same time confirmation that investments, especially over the last ten years or so, pay off and that guests recognise them. Further development will also depend on the legal framework regulating camping activities in the areas of spatial planning, maritime domain and the sea, and tourism. We expect that conditions and frameworks will be defined in all three areas that will enable further investments. Without new investments there is no raising of quality, and I believe that in the coming years we will see an additional flourishing of Croatian camping and a new rise, especially thanks to the positioning of Croatia as the highest-quality camping destination in Europe,” emphasised Veljko Ostojić, President of the KUH Executive Board and Director of the Croatian Tourism Association.

croatia leads the european ranking

According to the announcement by PiNCAMP, the camping portal of ADAC (the largest German and European and the second-largest automobile club in the world), Croatia will for the first time lead the European ranking of campsite quality in 2027, while the number of Croatian campsites with the ADAC Superplatz label is rising to 29. ADAC PiNCAMP expects continued strong demand from the German and Dutch markets for the next season. How to maintain competitiveness on the European market and create conditions for sustainable growth of the sector is one of the key questions of this year’s Croatian Camping Congress.

“The next step in the development of Croatian camping is not only accommodation, but the complete quality of the stay – from the pitch, sanitary facilities and shade to service and facilities that give the guest a reason to come even outside the summer season. It is important to preserve the diversity of the offer, from places for tents and campers to mobile homes, as well as small family campsites and large resorts. Research should help us direct investments towards specific groups of guests, and technology should facilitate reservations and leave employees more time for the guest. For such development, professional people and clear, predictable business conditions are equally important,” said Adriano Palman, Director of the Croatian Camping Association.

These changes are particularly visible in the development of accommodation quality. According to data from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, in 2007 Croatia had 13 four-star campsites, while there were no five-star campsites. By 2025 the number of four-star campsites had risen to 82, and nine had entered the five-star category. Thus, as many as 58% of the capacity of Croatian campsites falls into the 4- and 5-star category. This development reflects continuous investments in infrastructure, improvement of the existing offer and development of facilities, with which Croatian camping responds to the increasingly demanding expectations of guests.

a huge transformation over the last two decades

“The camping industry has transformed significantly over the last 20 years. Today, 50 percent of Croatian campsites have four or five stars, and they account for 20 percent of all overnight stays in Croatia. The level of their quality is also confirmed by guest loyalty, as shown by the latest research. As many as 50 percent of guests have returned to Croatian campsites seven or more times, which speaks of the competitiveness of this tourism segment,” emphasised Monika Udovičić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport.

From 1 January to 11 October 2026, Croatian campsites recorded almost 3.4 million arrivals and 21.4 million overnight stays, maintaining results at the level of the same period last year, which was a record year in the history of Croatian camping. Germany, Slovenia and Austria remain the leading markets, with more than 60 percent of total overnight stays in campsites, while domestic guests recorded 9.7 percent more overnight stays than in the comparable period last year. The importance of camping for Croatian tourism is confirmed by its 23 percent share of overnight stays in commercial accommodation, with an average stay of 6.2 days – the longest among all types of accommodation.

The continuation of the programme also includes European examples of campsite adaptation to climate change, from the arrangement of green areas and creation of shade to infrastructure adaptation. Business topics cover the development and retention of employees, energy efficiency, and a review of ten years of online reservations in Croatian campsites.

continued investment in the camping sector

A special part of the programme also opens the question of how Croatian campsites present themselves to guests through artificial intelligence. The research covered four leading AI assistants that were asked 100 questions about Croatian campsites on five source markets, with almost 2,000 answers analysed and the accuracy of the claims made and sources used verified. The results provide insight into the reliability of the information that potential guests receive and the opportunities for campsites to improve their visibility and the availability of accurate data in the digital environment.

The professional programme is accompanied by an exhibition of mobile homes, glamping tents, equipment and digital solutions for campsites. The Congress thus connects research and exchange of experience with a concrete offer for investment and business improvement. From the first edition in 2007 to last year’s Congress, around 5,200 participants from Croatia and abroad have taken part in these gatherings. As the central meeting place for representatives of campsites, the tourism sector, institutions and related industries, the Congress encourages the exchange of experience, presentation of innovations and discussion of trends and challenges that shape the future of camping.

The jubilee Congress ends tomorrow with the presentation of the Croatia’s Best Campsites and OK Mini Camps awards, as well as the Naj Kamp Adria 2026 award, which recognise the quality and development of the camping offer.

World.title: SafeJournalists Demands Official Croatian Reaction After Threats to Media
World.content:
October the 21s5, 2026 – The organisation SafeJournalists is currently demanding an official Croatian reaction after imagery of hanged journalists and other threats to the media have come to light.

Extreme condemnation of morbid threats made against journalists in Croatia have come from the international SafeJournalists network following their reporting on Nazi and antisemitic outbursts by Torcida members in Split, Morski reports. Specifically, the organisation has warned about the publication of journalists’ photographs, calls for their liquidation, and banners depicting hanged journalists from Croatian media.

They demand urgent protection of the threatened journalists from the Croatian authorities and prosecution of those responsible. SafeJournalists warns that a campaign of intimidation against journalists has since begun, with them being accused of creating hysteria and conducting a campaign against Torcida. Today, Interior Minister Davor Božinović himself spoke out, saying that the police have launched an investigation into messages aimed at intimidating journalists while they perform their work.

“I have some information about this, the police has launched a criminal investigation precisely because of inscriptions intended to intimidate journalists,” Minister Božinović said before the HDZ Presidency session. “No one has any authority to frighten or intimidate anyone in this country, especially not those who are merely doing their job,” the minister and Deputy Prime Minister stated.

On the 18th of October, the Facebook page Narodni reporteri published photographs of 11 Croatian journalists and one political analyst under the title “12 horsemen of the Croatian apocalypse.” According to SafeJournalists, some commenters called for the journalists to be expelled from Croatia and banned from working, while others suggested finding their home addresses, expressed a desire for their death, or mentioned compiling a liquidation list. The next day, the 19th of October, photos of new threatening messages appeared in the Facebook group Torcida Split 1950.

On one wall in Dalmatia, the following message was written: “Torcida remembers and does not forgive! Journalists are worms.” Particularly disturbing was a banner on which journalists were called “the greatest evil of Croatian society.” The banner showed a tree with hanged journalists from Slobodna Dalmacija, Index, Jutarnji list, Večernji list and 24sata.

The SafeJournalists network expressed particular concern about the political messages accompanying the incidents. They singled out a press conference that Domovinski pokret president Ivan Penava held today in Split. Penava condemned Nazi and fascist chants, but at the same time accused the police and the media of conducting a campaign against Torcida. He also questioned the publication of photographs of suspects sought by the police and criticised the Croatian Journalists’ Association for its warnings about threats against journalists.

SafeJournalists considers that such political rhetoric further worsens the atmosphere in which journalists are exposed to intimidation.

World.title: Vrsar Attracts Visitors from Around the World
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – Vrsar has done exceptionally well in attracting visitors from around the world this year. Tourists from 74 countries descended on the Istrian settlement in 2026.

From distant countries like Japan and Australia to Brazil, New Zealand and South Africa, this year, Vrsar attracted guests from as many as 74 countries around the world. As Istra Terra Magica writes, although at first glance it is a small Istrian destination, the tourist figures reveal its significant international reach: The growth in tourist traffic, especially during the months of May and September, follows the development of Vrsar’s multi-layered tourist offer, which is based on the natural and cultural heritage, tradition and local particularities of the destination.

vrsar’s investment in what it offers the world pays off in 2026

Over the first nine months of this year, Vrsar was visited by guests from 74 countries of the world, including those from Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Brazil and South Africa. At the same time almost 260 thousand arrivals and 1.84 million overnight stays were recorded, i.e. 4 percent more arrivals and 5 percent more overnight stays than in the same period last year. Behind these figures stands a destination that has for years been developing its tourist offer on the foundations of what makes Vrsar special, from the sea and the coast, through sculptural creativity, to the Kontija forest, the Lim Bay and local food and wine scene.

The multi-layered nature of the offer is precisely one of Vrsar’s special strengths. Guests who come for the sea and a holiday here have the opportunity to see, hear, learn and experience much more. What today constitutes Vrsar’s tourist offer stems from what the destination is and what it has been throughout its history. Its natural and cultural particularities, local stories and tradition have over the years received new content and become part of the tourist experience. Such an offer did not arise by chance, but is developing through long-term work, investment and the linking of the destination’s values with experiences that enrich the stay of guests.

The results achieved outside the peak of the summer season are particularly encouraging. In May 20 percent more arrivals and 32 percent more overnight stays were recorded, while September brought growth of 8 percent in both indicators. These results are important in the context of the development of content that gives guests additional reasons to come and stay in Vrsar outside the main summer months as well.

great traffic outside of the summer season

“We’re particularly pleased that we are recording good results outside the main summer months as well. We are developing content because of which guests can discover Vrsar in different parts of the year, and at the same time it is important to us what value tourism creates for the destination. That is why we look at the results through the total number of arrivals and overnight stays, their distribution throughout the year, the length of stay and the motives for which guests choose Vrsar,” emphasises Dr. Sc. Klara Trošt Lesić, director of the Tourist Board of the Municipality of Vrsar.

Germany, Slovenia, Austria and Italy remain the most important source markets for Vrsar, with almost 71 percent of all arrivals. At the same time, the fact that the destination was visited by guests from a total of 74 countries speaks of its international reach, which extends far beyond the traditional European markets, even though arrivals from more distant markets are of considerably smaller volume.

Germany remains the most important individual market with almost 740 thousand overnight stays, or about 40 percent of total overnight stays, with growth of 7.5 percent compared to last year. Among the four leading markets, Italy records the largest growth, with about ten percent more arrivals and overnight stays.

One of the most important foundations of Vrsar’s tourist offer remains camping. In the wider Vrsar area’s campsites, more than 1.34 million overnight stays were recorded by the end of September, or almost three quarters of all tourist overnight stays in the destination. The developed camping offer and Vrsar’s location provide guests with the opportunity to explore the wider region, while the multi-layered nature of local content further enriches their stay.

World.title: Velebit Positioned as a Sustainable Tourist Destination
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – A project involving cross-border cooperation has seen Velebit positioned as a sustainable tourist destination.

For the Croatian people, the mighty Velebit has always been much more than a rocky mountain rich in flora and fauna and hidden endemics. Marin Smolcic reports for Novi list that this mountain range’s imposing slopes are packed with speleological formations, many of which will never be accessible to human eyes. Apart from hiking enthusiasts, only a few have the privilege of being part of this mythical mountain.

The Public Institution Nature Park Velebit, within the framework of the REVERS project, held a two-day event on the 30th of September and the 1st of October entitled “From Protected Nature to a Sustainable Tourist Experience”. The programme included an international round table at the Cerovačke Caves Centre of Excellence in Gračac and a field tour of the Majstorska cesta (Master’s Road), Tulove grede and the area of the Zrmanja River.

The project was also presented at the “Autumn in Lika” fair in Gospić. This time the event brought together representatives of the public, private and civil sectors from across Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro who work in the fields of nature protection, management of protected areas, tourism, local and regional development and science.

During both days, 30 participants took part each day, which opened space for the exchange of experiences and joint reflection on solutions for the sustainable management of protected areas. There is still a lot of work ahead for the organisers of this project because proud Velebit does not reveal its secrets all at once. This is best known by hikers who, during frequent ascents to the same peak, each time discover a new path, spring or viewpoint of a mountain that is too rich and diverse for us to “consume” it visually at first sight.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar remains stable in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and declined in the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate remained stable in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,695 Iraqi dinars throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,700 Iraqi dinars and 1,690 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate slightly declined, fluctuating between 1,694 and 1,693 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following a cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Gulf Keystone says Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has 7 billion barrels of oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – CEO of Gulf Keystone Petroleum Jon Harris said on Wednesday that the firm believes that Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has seven billion barrels of oil, of which 0.5 billion to one billion barrels are recoverable.

Harris told Reuters that the oilfield currently produces 20,000 barrels per day, and by the end of 2028, output is expected to reach 60,000 barrels per day.

This week, Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

The agreement integrates operations in the four Iraqi fields of Hamrin, Sarsang, Atrush, and Shaikan.

If drilling begins next year, the Shaikan oilfield in Iraqi Kurdistan is likely to increase its gross output from around 45,000 bpd to over 90,000 bpd by 2030, according to Harris.

Harris anticipates that the corporation will take advantage of other possibilities in Iraq, such as stake sales on US assets in the country.

World.title: Iraq, UAE discuss options to de-escalate regional tensions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and UAE’s Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed on Wednesday options to de-escalate tensions in the region.

During a phone conversation, the two sides discussed bilateral relations between the two countries, reaffirming the depth of the bonds that bind them together as well as a shared commitment to strengthening and expanding these ties, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The discussion addressed the outcomes of the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers, which took place in Baghdad on October 17–18. Both parties emphasized the importance of leveraging these achievements to enhance communication, foster unity, and encourage collaborative Islamic initiatives.

Along with regional developments, the discussion included approaches to foster a peaceful understanding that helps reduce tensions and improve security and stability in the region.

Hussein said on Sunday that Baghdad is attempting to arrange a meeting between Iran and the Gulf States as part of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and advance regional stability.

There are ongoing discussions between Iraq, the Gulf countries, and Iran aimed at bringing their viewpoints closer together, according to Hussein.

“We are trying to organize a meeting in Baghdad between Iran and the Gulf States,” Hussein said, without specifying a date or the degree of representation expected.

The proposal comes amid regional tensions that severely impacted maritime shipping and security in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq’s Fly Erbil gets Air Operator Certificate
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq-based airline Fly Erbil announced on Thursday that it had obtained an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA)—a milestone the company says paves the way for a new phase of development and the expansion of its flight network.

The airline said in a statement that obtaining the license is a result of years of diligent work by its management and employees in different divisions.

Fly Erbil reaffirmed its commitment to safety and security requirements, as well as the regulations of the aviation sector.

The company mentioned that the step supports the development of air transport in both Iraqi Kurdistan and throughout Iraq.

The airline plans to broaden its flight network by adding more Iraqi cities and introducing new destinations both regionally and globally. Additionally, it aims to enhance its services to comply with international standards and meet travelers’ expectations.

The Iraqi Kurdish airline based at Erbil International Airport emphasized that obtaining this certification marks the beginning of a new phase in its journey.

World.title: Iraq signs seawater deal with ExxonMobil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Wednesday that the state-run Basra Oil Company (BOC) and US-based ExxonMobil signed a memorandum of understanding for the second phase of an Iraq seawater supply project.

On the sidelines of a ceremony held to sign the agreement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that the second phase of the seawater project is designed to support oil fields and maintain reservoir pressure.

With a capacity of up to 2.5 million barrels per day, this initiative complements a separate project currently being carried out by France-based TotalEnergies, which has a capacity of five million barrels per day.

The project is part of the Iraqi government’s approach to attract foreign firms to develop the country’s oil industry, ensure the sustainability of operations, and increase production rates, according to Khudair.

The development highlights Iraq’s appealing investment climate for implementing promising projects.

Khudair confirmed on Saturday that US firms are showing increasing interest in entering the Iraqi market and developing the country’s oil resources and petroleum industry.

The oil minister clarified that the Iraqi government supports US corporations’ involvement in the Iraqi market, citing their significant expertise in the oil sector, as well as their ability to transfer knowledge to Iraqi staff.

Several American companies are operating in Iraq, including oil services and consulting firms such as Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and KBR, according to Khudair. He indicated that the ministry reached agreements with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips.

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase 10 large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is moving toward the acquisition of supertankers to bolster its capacity for transporting and marketing crude oil globally—a strategic step intended to reduce transportation costs and enhance financial returns from crude exports.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is considering the purchase of 10 oil tankers as part of its efforts to develop its export infrastructure and expand options for delivering shipments to global markets.

The step is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the role of the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC) and leverage the ownership of maritime transport assets, which would provide greater flexibility in marketing crude oil and managing shipments.

The plan is considered crucial given Iraq’s desire to improve the terms of its oil sales and reduce the discounts associated with certain existing marketing and transportation arrangements.

In a televised statement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair revealed that the ministry is considering the purchase of 10 supertankers, with an estimated total cost of $2 billion, according to Attaqa News.

According to Khudair, the projected fleet will have a total capacity of 10 million barrels since each tanker has a capacity of around one million barrels.

Owning these tankers would increase export earnings; estimates indicate that Iraq might save between 30 percent and 40 percent on the losses it presently suffers from price reductions.

The Ministry of Oil has more alternatives than only direct procurement; it is also considering proposals from specialist companies to establish joint ventures for the supply of oil tankers.

According to Khudair, one of the suggestions is specialized businesses funding the acquisition of tankers in exchange for a portion of the revenues made from the vessels’ operations, with the price paid over a period of three or four years.

Direct procurement is still a possibility, and the Iraqi government has said that it supports this approach.

World.title: Iraq’s Diwaniyah refinery undergoes major $800 million expansion project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An oil refinery expansion project in Iraq is making tangible progress, as part of the country’s efforts to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and increase the value of its crude oil.

The Al-Barham Group (ABG) is carrying out an $800 million expansion project at the Diwaniyah refinery in Iraq.

This project is one of several refinery expansion initiatives that Iraq is pursuing, including those in al-Amarah, Muthanna, Kirkuk, and Qayyarah.

The refinery manager projected in September 2025 that monthly revenues would reach approximately $35 million once the expansion is complete.

The Diwaniyah refinery expansion is progressing steadily toward the operational phase. An atmospheric distillation unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day will bring the refinery’s total production capacity to 90,000 barrels per day—more than four times its current capacity—according to the British magazine Middle East Economic Digest (MEED).

The Iraqi government signed the expansion deal in February 2025. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) declared that the contractor will start moving equipment on-site within days after securing the required finance.

In July 2025, work officially commenced at the site, with the Ministry of Oil establishing a five-year timeline for the project’s completion.

In addition to the main distillation unit, the project includes a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) processing unit with a capacity of 180 tons per day, a naphtha hydro-treating unit with a capacity of 18,000 barrels per day, a gasoline upgrading unit with a capacity of 10,000 barrels per day, a naphtha isomerization unit with a capacity of 8,000 barrels per day, and a loading terminal with a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day.

The project also includes a power generation plant, a nitrogen plant, a water pumping and purification station, an industrial wastewater treatment plant, and 24 storage tanks for crude oil and petroleum products.

Beside high-quality gasoline, the refinery will produce naphtha, kerosene, red diesel, fuel oil, and LPG, supporting Iraq’s objective of achieving self-sufficiency in petroleum products.

World.title: Iraq’s customs revenues hit record high in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority of Customs has announced a revenue increase of over $72 million in September 2026 compared to the same month in 2025.

The authority said in a statement that total customs revenues rose from $222.8 million in September 2025 to $294.8 million in September 2026—a growth rate of approximately 32.34 percent.

The rise reflects the importance of developing the customs operational system and enhancing the efficiency of revenue collection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The authority indicated that it is implementing a plan to enhance institutional performance, improve customs operational procedures, and increase the efficiency of revenue collection.

The measures are designed to protect public funds, strengthen the state’s financial resources, support financial reform, and promote the growth of non-oil revenues.

In January, head of the authority’s valuation department, Ahmed al-Akeedi, said that the deployment of the ASYCUDA system and the new customs tariff will improve earnings.

Al-Akeedi said that Iraqi customs revenues reached $1.9 billion in 2025, an unprecedented milestone in Iraqi customs history and an exceptional achievement.

Revenues are predicted to grow by at least four to six times with the application of the ASYCUDA system and complete compliance with customs rates, perhaps exceeding $7.63 billion by the end of 2026, according to al-Akeedi.

World.title: 21 years on, double life term for Jammu terror attack that killed baby, 2 others
World.content:
JAMMU: A Jammu court has imposed two life sentences and fines of Rs 2 lakh on Mohammed Sharief, a terrorist who gunned down three members of a family, including a six-month-old infant, in Ramban districtâs Gool area over 21 years ago.

In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation.

Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences. âAll sentences shall run concurrently, while the period already spent in custody shall be set off in accordance with law,â the judge said.

The court ordered that the fines be paid to those injured in the July 2005 terror attack and directed J&K State Legal Services Authority to provide compensation to heirs of the deceased and the survivors.

Judge Gupta rejected defence arguments about the testimony of two injured eyewitnesses, saying they were reliable and corroborated by medical and other evidence. Defective investigations or delay in recording statements could not automatically result in acquittal when credible evidence otherwise established the accusedâs guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the judge said.

World.title: New norms to limit fuel leaks, protect EV batteries in rear-end crashes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt has tightened norms for protection of fuel systems and electric power drive systems, with all new vehicles manufactured from April 2029 onwards required to comply with the new standards, a move that will prevent fire in rear-end collisions.

In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory for Event Data Recorder (EDR) from Oct 2029 if it is installed in any car. The EDR feature is not mandatory for all cars, and it remains an optional feature. EDR records crash details, which help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. It is similar in purpose to an aircraftâs flight-data recorder or black box.

In the case of standards for fire safety, the revised automotive industry standards (AIS)-101 specify that after a rear-impact crash test, liquid-fuel systems must not develop more than slight leakage and continuous leakage must not exceed 30 grams per minute. The key safety requirements include the fuel system not allowing a fire to be sustained following the impact. In the case of electric vehicles, the battery and its securing mechanism must remain in position during and after the impact test.

This standard lays down requirements for protecting occupants from electrical hazards, including the high-voltage circuit being automatically disconnected after a collision.

The ministry has notified revised vehicle safety standards, including updated frontal and side-impact crash protection requirements, with implementation for new models scheduled from Oct 2027 and for all models from Oct 2028.

It has also revised requirements for protecting pedestrians and other vulnerable road users. The updated standard will apply to new models from Oct 2028.

World.title: PM Modi calls for stronger global institutions; takes ‘failed product’ jab at Congress
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and effective international cooperation during crises, while accusing the Congress leadership of repeatedly failing to launch its leader politically.

Addressing the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi, PM Modi said institutions such as the United Nations were struggling to keep pace with the changing world order and emerging challenges, according to news agency ANI.

PM Modi warned that trade, technology and sea routes were increasingly being âweaponisedâ, stressing the need for a global system that prevents the strong from exploiting the vulnerable. Citing ancient Indian statesman Chanakya, he referred to the Sanskrit aphorism âapranitah tu matsyanyayam udbhavayatiâ, which he explained as a situation where the absence of law and order allows the strong to prey on the weak.

âThe world does not need such a situation. It needs a system that stops this 'matsya nyaya' from happening,â PM Modi said.

Highlighting India's role in global cooperation, Modi cited the country's humanitarian assistance during the Covid-19 pandemic. âDuring the Covid-19 pandemic, the world experienced India taking on such a role. India sent vaccines to every country in need; sent medicines to over 100 countries,â he said.





âThe changing world order calls for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South, and international cooperation that stands firm in times of crisis,â he added.

PM Modi said India's vision of becoming a developed nation, or Viksit Bharat, by 2047 went beyond domestic ambitions. âIt is also a guarantee for a better world,â he said, adding that international cooperation must remain effective during crises and not just in favourable circumstances.

âIndia is strengthening its own capabilities to help strengthen the world,â he said.

PM Modi targets Congress over repeated attempts to launch its leader

At the same summit, PM Modi took a swipe at the Congress, accusing the party's leadership of becoming a burden on the organisation and repeatedly attempting to launch its leader politically.

Drawing a comparison with India's space programme, he said, âWe don't have as many launches from Sriharikota in one year as the Congress makes failed attempts to launch its leader in one year.â

Taking another dig at the opposition party, PM Modi questioned how long the country would remain at stake over these attempts. âWho knows how long Congress will keep the country at stake while trying to launch its âfailed productâ,â he said.

PM Modi also accused some people of damaging India's global reputation and seeking foreign intervention in the country's affairs.

âSome hell-bent on dragging India's reputation through mud; they go abroad, defame India, petition foreigners for intervention,â he said.

World.title: Natco’s generic SMA drug approved; ‘clinical trial’ labels trigger Kerala row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Days after a controversy erupted in Kerala over Natco Pharmaâs generic drug for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), regulatory clarifications suggest the row stemmed from labels on bottles supplied free of cost.

The words âPhysician Sample/Clinical Trialâ raised fears among parents that their children were being given medicines meant for clinical trials rather than an authorised drug for routine treatment.

In response to queries from TOI, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) officials said Natcoâs risdiplam powder for oral solution (0.75 mg/ml) had been approved by the Telangana State Food and Drug Administration under the applicable regulations.

The bulk drug had received CDSCO approval on April 7, 2025.

The officials said bioequivalence studies were not required for the oral solution under the regulatorâs draft guidance and that additional clinical trials were not necessary before patients could be switched to the generic formulation.

Natco said it emerged as the lowest bidder in Keralaâs tender and supplies one free bottle for every three purchased under its Patient Assistance Programme, bringing the effective cost to around â¹8,500 per bottle against â¹1.5 lakh earlier for Rocheâs drug.





The company acknowledged that the free bottles carry the label âPhysician Sample/Clinical trials onlyâ, but said they were supplied as samples under the rate contract and not for clinical trials.

It said its generic risdiplam, priced at an MRP of â¹15,900 against â¹6 lakh for Rocheâs product, had met regulatory requirements.

The issue became a political controversy after Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said parents of children with SMA had flagged the labels on medicines distributed through SAT Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram.

He alleged violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and procurement norms and demanded an inquiry.

SAT Hospital authorities have maintained that the medicine distributed was the approved generic formulation, not an experimental drug.

Risdiplam is used to treat SMA, a rare genetic disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness. Kerala had been supplying Rocheâs branded medicine free to eligible children at a negotiated price.

The shift to Natcoâs generic version could substantially reduce treatment costs and potentially allow the state to extend support to more patients.

The controversy comes amid opposition from parents and the Cure SMA Foundation of India to Keralaâs decision to replace Rocheâs medicine with Natcoâs generic version. Parents have sought assurances about the safety and efficacy of switching children who have improved on the existing treatment.

While the regulatory clarification addresses the generic drugâs approval status, the episode raises a separate question: whether labelling that combines âPhysician Sampleâ and âClinical Trialâ can cause confusion when medicines are supplied for patient use.

World.title: Indian diaspora could pay price for West’s immigration backlash, warns Sushant Sareen
World.content:
Sushant Sareen sees the immigration debate as part of a wider crisis facing Western societies.

Why Indians could pay the price

Is the West paying for its own mistakes?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Faultline

US President Donald Trump has blamed immigration for the recent unrest in France and urged President Emmanuel Macron to close the countryâs borders, reigniting a wider debate over migration, integration and the future of Western societies.But the backlash could also hurt Indians who have built successful lives abroad through legal migration, strategic affairs expert Sushant Sareen has warned.âThe law breakers don't care anyways but it's the guys who follow the law who will also get crushed,â Sareen said in an interview on Faultline, hosted by Ananya Dasgupta.Trump has described Franceâs unrest as a consequence of immigration and warned that Europe risks decline unless it tightens its borders. Macron, however, has rejected attempts by foreign leaders to blame migrants for the violence, pointing to the exploitation of Franceâs domestic tensions for political gain.Sareen said the Indian diaspora had established a reputation for success in countries such as the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.âThe Indian diaspora wherever it went it made a success of itself,â he said.However, he argued that this reputation could come under pressure as anti-immigration sentiment grows.Referring to Canada, Sareen alleged that criminal activity involving some members of the Indian community, including people he linked to Khalistani networks, had damaged the image of the wider diaspora.His concern is that Indians unconnected with such activities could also face the consequences of a broader backlash against migrants.Sareen sees the immigration debate as part of a wider crisis facing Western societies. He argued that governments had failed to manage integration and address tensions around migration, leaving established political and social models under strain.âMulticulturalism has collapsed,â he said, describing what he sees as the failure of the Western approach to managing cultural diversity.Yet Western economies continue to need migrant workers, particularly as populations age and employers face labour shortages. Sareen said governments must rethink their immigration systems, including how long migrants can stay and what rights they should have.For Indians hoping to study, work or settle abroad, tougher visa rules could complicate future plans. Those already settled overseas could also face uncertainty if immigration becomes a proxy for wider anxieties about jobs, identity and cultural change.The contradiction is that Western countries need foreign talent even as political pressure to restrict immigration grows.For India, the stakes extend beyond visa policies. If the West responds to its immigration crisis by treating migrant communities as a single group, law-abiding Indians who have contributed to their host countries could find themselves paying the price.Watchwith Ananya Dasgupta and Sushant Sareen as they discuss the France crisis, the Westâs immigration trap, the growing backlash and why Indians could pay the price.

World.title: No consistent improvement in Delhi’s winter air quality over four years: CREA
World.content:
There has been no consistent improvement in Delhi’s winter air quality over the past four years, despite the imposition of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), according to an analysis of government data by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation.

“Delhi’s winter AQI (Air Quality Index) has fluctuated over the past four years, with no consistent improvement. The mean AQI rose from 280 in winter 2022–23 to 304 in 2023–24, fell to 285 in 2024–25 and increased again to 295 in 2025–26. The median AQI followed a similar pattern, rising from 294 to 324, falling to 289 and then increasing to 305,” CREA said in a statement.

A higher AQI indicates poorer air quality.

Delhi’s winter air quality has not followed a consistent downward trend since the 2022 revision of GRAP, and the mean and median AQI for the latest winter were both higher than in 2022–23, said Manoj Kumar, an analyst at CREA.

The mean and median of the AQI are statistical measures used to summarize air quality data over a specific period. Because AQI levels can fluctuate wildly due to weather changes or pollution spikes, these two metrics tell different stories about the air you breathe.

GRAP comprises short-term emergency measures to reduce air pollution and is divided into four stages, depending on the level of pollution recorded or forecast for the near future. The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) announces the different stages based on air quality forecasts.

Every winter, air pollution levels rise in Delhi-NCR and several parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP), mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and falling temperatures. Stubble burning during October and November, along with firecracker emissions, further worsens pollution.

Meanwhile, Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category for the second consecutive day on Thursday.

The 24-hour average AQI stood at 223 (poor) at 4 p.m. on Thursday, down from 245 (poor) a day earlier, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) daily bulletin, which provides the official AQI for the day.

CAQM reviews stubble

The CAQM held separate review meetings with the governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh on Thursday to assess measures to prevent and control paddy stubble burning and reduce other major sources of air pollution. It directed the States to take prompt action on the ground.

The Commission emphasised the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure the effective utilisation of available machinery during the peak harvesting period. The meetings also covered field verification of burnt-area assessments based on satellite fire alerts, along with the district-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors to monitor stubble-burning incidents.

“Paddy stubble management should be pursued not merely as a measure to prevent burning, but as an opportunity to improve the well-being of citizens while fostering a robust industrial ecosystem of a circular economy, with greater utilization of paddy straw as a resource,” an official statement said.

The Commission also called for prompt action on the ground and cautioned district administrations that any laxity leading to an increase in stubble-burning incidents would be “viewed seriously”.

World.title: Delhi SIR: revised data show sharp increase in Form 6 disposal rate
World.content:
A total of 1.07 lakh Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in Delhi’s electoral roll have been disposed of, according to an updated weekly disposal report uploaded on the website of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Thursday. The latest data replaced the weekly disposal report on the website that was there till Wednesday, with officials saying the data being uploaded earlier was wrong and not reflecting the disposals recorded since August 31, when the claims and objections phase began.

The CEO’s office releases a constituency-wise report every week, recording how many applications under each form - Form 6 for inclusion of new voters, Form 7 for deletions, Form 6A for overseas electors and Form 8 for corrections or address changes - have been disposed of since the claims and objections phase under the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls began.

This comes after The Hindu reported that only 0.27%, or 1,238 of the over 4.5 lakh Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in Delhi’s electoral roll had been disposed of between August 31 and October 11.

The revised figures cover each of the seven weeks between August 31 and October 18. Officials said the data displayed publicly earlier was wrong. According to the updated report, 1,07,451 of the 4,59,796 Form 6 applications and 47,105 of the 67,709 Form 7 applications have been disposed of.

“The weekly data being uploaded till now was wrong and it was not reflecting the disposals that happened since August 31, we noticed after the newspaper report,” an official told The Hindu. For instance, the earlier report showed 241 Form 6 applications were disposed of across Delhi’s 70 Assembly constituencies from August 31 to September 6, the first week of the claims and objections period. The updated report now shows 511 for the same week. The second week’s figure has been revised from 34 to 4,543. The sharpest revision is for the week of September 28 to October 4 – from zero to 14,643 disposals.

The updated report also adds the latest week, October 12 to 18, which alone accounts for 43,736 Form 6 disposals - the highest for any week and over 40% of all such disposals so far. According to the updated data, disposals have risen every week, from 511 in the first week to 43,736 in the seventh.

Fifteen constituencies that showed zero Form 6 disposals in all six weeks as per the earlier report, including Burari, Shakur Basti and Kalkaji, now show cases being disposed of.

Tri Nagar is still the only constituency in Delhi with no Form 6 disposals recorded in any of the seven weeks.

Form 7 figures too have been revised sharply upward: from 5,845 to 40,796 for the same six weeks. The first week now shows 10,474 Form 7 disposals against 64 earlier, and the second 17,143 against 274. Over the seven weeks, 47,105 Form 7 applications have been disposed of, along with 1,70,333 Form 8 applications for corrections and address changes.

According to the CEO’s daily bulletin on Thursday, about 4.6 lakh Form 6 applications have been received so far - 2.12 lakh before the draft roll was published on August 31 and 2.47 lakh after. Around 67,709 Form 7 applications have been received, including 16,238 since August 31.

This means about 23% of all Form 6 applications received have been disposed of, compared with about 70% of Form 7 applications. The disposals include applications received before the draft roll was published.

Over 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications are yet to be disposed of. The last date for filing claims and objections is October 30, all applications received are to be disposed of by November 30, and the final electoral roll is to be published on December 4.

World.title: Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation lauded for securing another Guinness record for drone formation
World.content:
Energy Minister K.J. George has lauded the Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC) for securing a Guinness World Record with its 3,473-drone peacock formation during Mysuru Dasara 2026. He also commended the spectacular electrical illuminations that added to the grandeur of the 11-day festivities, which concluded on Wednesday (October 21).

Witnessing the Jamboo Savari procession and the drone show (during torchlight parade) on Wednesday, Mr. George, who also holds the Tourism portfolio, said the initiatives had enhanced Dasara’s global visibility and strengthened Mysuru’s position as a major tourism destination.

The drone show, held over four days at the Torchlight Parade Grounds in Bannimantap, featured 12 visual formations in different colours and designs. The peacock formation, created using 3,473 drones, was the highlight, earning CESC another Guinness World Record following its tiger formation record last year.

The Minister also praised the special Dasara illuminations, which covered 146 km of roads, 123 circles and prominent locations in the city, besides featuring 80 artistic installations. The colourful displays added to the city’s festive appeal and enhanced its visual splendour.

He said the effective management of the city’s electrical illumination during Dasara was a major responsibility. “Given the scale of the festival, which attracts lakhs of tourists, priority was accorded to the reliable management of the power infrastructure, technical preparedness and coordination at various levels. The initiatives undertaken by CESC under the Energy Department have played a significant role in enhancing the grandeur of the Dasara festivities,” the Minister said.

Alongside its responsibility of ensuring an uninterrupted power supply, CESC has also demonstrated its capabilities in executing an impressive Dasara illumination and organising an innovative and technology-driven spectacle. “This achievement has been made possible by the coordinated efforts, technical expertise and sustained hard work of its officers and staff. After creating a tiger formation using drones and setting a record last year, CESC has continued its remarkable journey by creating a peacock formation this year and setting a new record. The electrical illumination and drone show have made a significant contribution towards positioning Dasara as a major global tourism attraction,” the Minister added.

Mr. George credited the Energy Department and CESC officers, technical personnel and staff for their sustained efforts in delivering the illuminations and drone spectacle. He congratulated MLA and CESC chairman Ramesh Bandisiddegowda, Energy Department Additional Chief Secretary Gaurav Gupta, CESC officials, linemen and other staff members.

CESC managing director M.S. Archana said the illuminations and drone show had received widespread public appreciation. The illuminations will remain in place until October 31, allowing tourists and residents to continue enjoying the city’s festive displays.

World.title: Delhi High Court quashes FIR against SSC aspirant over protest
World.content:
The Delhi High Court has quashed an FIR against a Staff Selection Commission (SSC) aspirant booked in connection with a protest at Ramlila Maidan, observing that mere participation in a demonstration does not establish a common intention to disobey police orders or obstruct police personnel.

Justice Sanjeev Narula held that the petitioner could not be prosecuted without material showing that he knowingly participated in the alleged disobedience or shared a common intention to commit the offence.

The case arose from a protest held at Ramlila Maidan in August 2025 by SSC aspirants over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the commission’s examination.

According to the prosecution, some organisers refused to call off the demonstration after the permitted time had expired and instigated protesters to remain at the venue until their demands were met.

The Delhi police subsequently registered an FIR alleging that some protesters had violated prohibitory orders issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita by continuing to occupy the ground. The police also alleged that some protesters pushed and scuffled with police personnel.

The court, however, noted that neither the FIR nor the subsequent status report attributed any specific criminal act to the petitioner. His presence among the protesters, without material indicating a common intention to commit an offence, was insufficient to make out a case under Section 223(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant.

“The petitioner cannot be subjected to criminal proceedings merely on account of his presence amongst the protesters, in the absence of material indicating his knowing participation in the alleged disobedience or any common intention to commit the offence. The continuation of the proceedings against him, in these circumstances, would serve no worthwhile purpose,” the court said in its October 13 order.

“Mere participation in the same demonstration does not, by itself, establish a common intention to disobey lawful directions or obstruct police personnel. The material on record does not disclose any basis for attributing such common intention to the petitioner,” it held.

World.title: Dismissed police official arrested in fraud case
World.content:
A dismissed police official was arrested for failing to appear in the court with regard to a fraud case filed against him by a woman on Wednesday.

A senior official of the city police said Raju was a Sub-Inspector. In 2022, the Mylapore police arrested him for cheating a woman of ₹15 lakh after befriending her.

Raju was subsequently dismissed for misconduct and also arrested. After his release from prison, he failed to appear in the court as required for the ongoing legal proceedings.

When he arrived at the Saidapet Magistrate Court on Wednesday, the magistrate ordered that he be remanded in judicial custody. However, Raju experienced some health issue and was subsequently admitted to the Government Royapettah Hospital.

World.title: Amit Shah vows to clean Yamuna by May 2029, unveils water and sewerage projects worth ₹8,941 crore
World.content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 43 water and sewerage projects worth ₹8,941.22 crore, aimed at cleaning the Yamuna and improving drinking water supply in Delhi.
